typedef struct _xmlURI xmlURI;
typedef xmlURI *xmlURIPtr;
/**
 * A parsed URI reference.
 *
 * This is a struct containing the various fields
 * as described in RFC 2396 but separated for further processing.
 *
 * Note: query is a deprecated field which is incorrectly unescaped.
 * query_raw takes precedence over query if the former is set.
 * See: http://mail.gnome.org/archives/xml/2007-April/thread.html\#00127
 */
struct _xmlURI {
    char *scheme;	/* the URI scheme */
    char *opaque;	/* opaque part */
    char *authority;	/* the authority part */
    char *server;	/* the server part */
    char *user;		/* the user part */
    int port;		/* the port number */
    char *path;		/* the path string */
    char *query;	/* the query string (deprecated - use with caution) */
    char *fragment;	/* the fragment identifier */
    int  cleanup;	/* parsing potentially unclean URI */
    char *query_raw;	/* the query string (as it appears in the URI) */
};
objects.description: Parsed URI structure implementing RFC 2396 fields. Holds components such as scheme, authority/server/user/port, path, query (deprecated), query_raw (preferred), fragment, and implementation flags (cleanup). Used throughout libxml2 URI routines. Ownership: dynamically allocated; must be freed with xmlFreeURI. query is deprecated; prefer query_raw when present.

typedef enum {
    /** Success */
    XML_ERR_NONE = 0,
    /**
     * A warning
     *
     * When parsing XML, warnings are only reported to error
     * handlers.
     */
    XML_ERR_WARNING = 1,
    /**
     * An error
     *
     * When parsing XML, this is used for recoverable errors like
     *
     * - namespace errors
     * - validity errors when validating
     * - certain undeclared entities
     * - ID uniqueness and xml:id errors
     *
     * Note that some recoverable errors in the sense of the XML
     * spec are reported as warnings.
     *
     * In other contexts, this may be used for unrecoverable
     * errors.
     */
    XML_ERR_ERROR = 2,
    /**
     * A fatal error
     *
     * When parsing XML, a "fatal error" according to the XML spec.
     * This typically means that the document isn't well-formed.
     *
     * This also includes OOM and I/O errors, resource limit
     * exhaustion, unexpected errors from other libraries and
     * invalid argument errors.
     */
    XML_ERR_FATAL = 3
} xmlErrorLevel;

functions.name: xmlC14NDocSaveTo
functions.signature: int xmlC14NDocSaveTo(xmlDoc *doc, xmlNodeSet *nodes, int mode, xmlChar **inclusive_ns_prefixes, int with_comments, xmlOutputBuffer *buf);
functions.description: Canonicalizes an XML document (or a provided node subset) and writes the canonical form to the given libxml2 output buffer. Supports Canonical XML 1.0, Exclusive C14N 1.0, and C14N 1.1 modes, with optional inclusion of comments. Use when you want the canonicalized bytes streamed to an existing xmlOutputBuffer (e.g., memory, file descriptor).
requirements: Library must be built with C14N support enabled (LIBXML_C14N_ENABLED).
doc must be a valid, initialized libxml2 xmlDoc*; for canonical form correctness, the document should have been parsed with XML_PARSE_DTDATTR | XML_PARSE_NOENT.
nodes, if not NULL, must be a valid xmlNodeSet* associated with the same document as doc; if NULL, the whole document is canonicalized (inferred; exact behavior not explicitly stated).
mode must be one of: XML_C14N_1_0, XML_C14N_EXCLUSIVE_1_0, or XML_C14N_1_1 (values of xmlC14NMode).

inclusive_ns_prefixes should specify prefixes to be treated as inclusive namespaces for Exclusive C14N; may be NULL if not used (array layout/termination is not specified here; typical pattern in libxml2 is a NULL-terminated list of xmlChar*).
with_comments is treated as a boolean flag; use 0 to exclude comments and non-zero to include comments.
buf must be a valid, open xmlOutputBuffer* ready for writing and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the return value; exact semantics are not documented here, but libxml2 commonly returns >= 0 on success and a negative value on error (inferred).

functions.name: xmlC14NDocDumpMemory
functions.signature: int xmlC14NDocDumpMemory(xmlDoc *doc, xmlNodeSet *nodes, int mode, xmlChar **inclusive_ns_prefixes, int with_comments, xmlChar **doc_txt_ptr);
functions.description: Canonicalizes an XML document (or a provided node subset) and returns the canonical bytes in memory via an output buffer pointer. Supports Canonical XML 1.0, Exclusive C14N 1.0, and C14N 1.1, with optional inclusion of comments. Use when you want the canonicalized form as an in-memory buffer.
requirements: Library must be built with C14N support enabled (LIBXML_C14N_ENABLED).
doc must be a valid, initialized libxml2 xmlDoc*; for canonical form correctness, the document should have been parsed with XML_PARSE_DTDATTR | XML_PARSE_NOENT.
nodes, if not NULL, must be a valid xmlNodeSet* associated with the same document as doc; if NULL, the whole document is canonicalized (inferred; exact behavior not explicitly stated).
mode must be one of: XML_C14N_1_0, XML_C14N_EXCLUSIVE_1_0, or XML_C14N_1_1 (values of xmlC14NMode).

inclusive_ns_prefixes should specify prefixes to be treated as inclusive namespaces for Exclusive C14N; may be NULL if not used (array layout/termination is not specified here; typical pattern in libxml2 is a NULL-terminated list of xmlChar*).
with_comments is treated as a boolean flag; use 0 to exclude comments and non-zero to include comments.
doc_txt_ptr must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the address of the allocated canonicalized buffer on success.

name must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes when len >= 0.
When len < 0, name must be a valid NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to handle allocation failures.
The returned pointer is owned by the dictionary and must not be freed by the caller; it remains valid as long as the dictionary remains alive.

functions.name: xmlDictExists
functions.signature: const xmlChar *xmlDictExists(xmlDict *dict, const xmlChar *name, int len);
functions.description: Checks whether a string is already present (interned) in the dictionary without adding it. Returns the interned pointer if found, otherwise NULL.
requirements: dict must be a valid pointer to a dictionary.
name must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes when len >= 0.
When len < 0, name must be a valid NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
Caller must handle a NULL return to mean the string is not present.

functions.name: xmlDictQLookup
functions.signature: const xmlChar *xmlDictQLookup(xmlDict *dict, const xmlChar *prefix, const xmlChar *name);
functions.description: Looks up or interns a qualified name (e.g., a combination of prefix and local name) in the dictionary and returns the interned const xmlChar* if successful. Useful for namespace-qualified names.
requirements: dict must be a valid pointer to a dictionary.
prefix must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated xmlChar string (whether NULL is allowed is not specified here; unknown).
name must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to handle allocation failures.

functions.name: xmlDictOwns
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the given string pointer belongs to (is owned by) this dictionary (i.e., was interned by it or one of its related dictionaries), zero otherwise. Useful to verify pointer provenance.
requirements: dict must be a valid pointer to a dictionary.
str must be a non-NULL pointer; behavior for NULL is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: xmlDictSize
functions.description: Returns the number of entries (interned strings) in the dictionary as an int. Use to inspect dictionary content size.
requirements: dict must be a valid pointer to a dictionary.

functions.name: xmlDictCleanup
functions.description: Deprecated cleanup function for the global dictionary subsystem. Historically released global resources; modern libxml2 should not require explicit cleanup in typical use.
requirements: Do not use in new code; function is marked deprecated.
If used, ensure no threads are concurrently using the global dictionary (thread-safety is not documented here; unknown).

functions.name: xmlInitCharEncodingHandlers
functions.description: Initialize the global registry of character encoding handlers. Deprecated: kept for backward compatibility; newer creation/lookup APIs are preferred.
requirements: None explicitly stated in this header.
Deprecated API: prefer newer handler creation/lookup functions.

functions.name: xmlCleanupCharEncodingHandlers
functions.description: Cleanup and free resources associated with the global registry of character encoding handlers. Deprecated.
requirements: None explicitly stated in this header.
Deprecated API: prefer newer handler lifecycle.

functions.name: xmlRegisterCharEncodingHandler
functions.description: Register a custom character encoding handler in the (deprecated) global registry. Deprecated.
requirements: handler should be a valid, initialized xmlCharEncodingHandler pointer (inferred from name/signature).
Deprecated API: behavior and lifecycle are legacy; prefer xmlCreateCharEncodingHandler or xmlCharEncNewCustomHandler.

functions.name: xmlLookupCharEncodingHandler
functions.description: Lookup a character encoding handler by predefined encoding enum and return it through out.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the handler.
enc should be a valid xmlCharEncoding value.
Caller must check the returned xmlParserErrors and proceed only if it indicates success (e.g., XML_ERR_OK).

functions.name: xmlOpenCharEncodingHandler
functions.signature: xmlParserErrors xmlOpenCharEncodingHandler(const char *name, int output, xmlCharEncodingHandler **out);
functions.description: Open/obtain a character encoding handler by name and direction (input/output).
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated encoding name.
out must be non-NULL to receive the handler.
Caller must check the returned xmlParserErrors for success before using the handler.
The output parameter indicates direction (inferred: nonzero for output conversion, zero for input).

functions.name: xmlCreateCharEncodingHandler
functions.signature: xmlParserErrors xmlCreateCharEncodingHandler(const char *name, xmlCharEncFlags flags, xmlCharEncConvImpl impl, void *implCtxt, xmlCharEncodingHandler **out);
functions.description: Create a character encoding handler by name using a provided converter implementation (impl) and flags, and return it via out.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
out must be non-NULL to receive the handler.
flags is a bit mask of xmlCharEncFlags (XML_ENC_INPUT, XML_ENC_OUTPUT, XML_ENC_HTML).
impl must adhere to xmlCharEncConvImpl contract: if it returns XML_ERR_OK, it must fill the out pointer with an encoding handler; the handler can be obtained from xmlCharEncNewCustomHandler.
Caller must check the returned xmlParserErrors for success before using the handler.
implCtxt is user data passed to impl (usage semantics not specified here).

functions.name: xmlGetCharEncodingHandler
functions.description: Get a character encoding handler for a predefined encoding enum value, or NULL if not available.
requirements: enc should be a valid xmlCharEncoding value.
Caller must handle a NULL return (handler not found).

functions.name: xmlFindCharEncodingHandler
functions.description: Find and return a character encoding handler by name, or NULL if not available.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated encoding name.
Caller must handle a NULL return (handler not found).

functions.name: xmlNewCharEncodingHandler
functions.signature: xmlCharEncodingHandler * xmlNewCharEncodingHandler(const char *name, xmlCharEncodingInputFunc input, xmlCharEncodingOutputFunc output);
functions.description: Create a (legacy) encoding handler from legacy function pointers converting to/from UTF-8. Deprecated in favor of custom converter API.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
input and/or output should be valid function pointers matching the typedefs (converting to UTF-8 for input, from UTF-8 for output).
Caller must handle a NULL return on failure.
Deprecated API: prefer xmlCharEncNewCustomHandler.

functions.name: xmlCharEncNewCustomHandler
functions.signature: xmlParserErrors xmlCharEncNewCustomHandler(const char *name, xmlCharEncConvFunc input, xmlCharEncConvFunc output, xmlCharEncConvCtxtDtor ctxtDtor, void *inputCtxt, void *outputCtxt, xmlCharEncodingHandler **out);
functions.description: Create a custom encoding handler using stateful converter callbacks for input (to UTF-8) and/or output (from UTF-8). On success, returns XML_ERR_OK and stores the created handler in out.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
out must be non-NULL to receive the handler.
input and/or output should be valid xmlCharEncConvFunc callbacks (can be NULL if not needed; not explicitly stated here).
If the converter(s) can consume partial multi-byte sequences, callers should pass flush=1 on the final call to detect truncated sequences (from xmlCharEncConvFunc doc).
ctxtDtor, if provided, will be used to free conversion contexts; inputCtxt and outputCtxt are user-provided contexts passed to the respective callbacks.
Caller must check the returned xmlParserErrors and only use the handler on success.

functions.name: xmlAddEncodingAlias
functions.description: Add an alias mapping from alias to canonical encoding name in the (deprecated) alias table.
requirements: name must be non-NULL canonical name.
alias must be non-NULL.
Deprecated API: alias management is legacy.

functions.name: xmlDelEncodingAlias
functions.description: Delete an alias mapping for alias from the (deprecated) alias table.
requirements: alias must be non-NULL.
Deprecated API: alias management is legacy.

functions.name: xmlGetEncodingAlias
functions.description: Get the canonical encoding name corresponding to alias from the (deprecated) alias table, or NULL if not found.
requirements: alias must be non-NULL.
Caller must handle a NULL return if alias is unknown.
Deprecated API: alias management is legacy.

functions.name: xmlCleanupEncodingAliases
functions.description: Cleanup and free resources associated with the (deprecated) encoding alias table.
requirements: None explicitly stated in this header.
Deprecated API.

functions.name: xmlParseCharEncoding
functions.description: Parse an encoding name string and return the corresponding xmlCharEncoding enum, or XML_CHAR_ENCODING_ERROR/none if unknown.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Caller must handle return values indicating unknown or unsupported encodings.

functions.name: xmlGetCharEncodingName
functions.description: Return the canonical name string for a given xmlCharEncoding enum.
requirements: enc should be a valid xmlCharEncoding value.
Caller must handle potential NULL return if no name is available (not explicitly stated).

functions.name: xmlDetectCharEncoding
functions.signature: xmlCharEncoding xmlDetectCharEncoding(const unsigned char *in, int len);
functions.description: Detect the character encoding from the first bytes of a byte sequence (e.g., BOM or recognizable patterns) and return the xmlCharEncoding enum.
requirements: in must point to a valid buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be >= 0.
Caller must handle cases where detection fails or returns XML_CHAR_ENCODING_NONE/ERROR (inferred).

functions.name: xmlCharEncOutFunc
functions.description: Convert characters from UTF-8 using the given handler, writing to out from in. Used by parsers for output conversion.
requirements: handler must be a valid, initialized xmlCharEncodingHandler pointer appropriate for output conversion (inferred from name/signature).
out must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
in must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure semantics (not specified here).

functions.name: xmlCharEncInFunc
functions.description: Convert characters to UTF-8 using the given handler, writing to out from in. Used by parsers for input conversion.
requirements: handler must be a valid, initialized xmlCharEncodingHandler pointer appropriate for input conversion (inferred).
out must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
in must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure semantics (not specified here).

functions.name: xmlCharEncFirstLine
functions.description: Convert only the first line (or an initial portion) of input using the given handler. Deprecated.
requirements: handler must be a valid, initialized xmlCharEncodingHandler pointer.
out must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
in must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer.
Deprecated API: exact semantics of "first line" are legacy and not specified here.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure semantics (not specified).

functions.name: xmlCharEncCloseFunc
functions.description: Close and free resources associated with a character encoding handler.
requirements: handler must be a valid handler previously obtained/created by the corresponding APIs (inferred).
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure semantics (not specified).
Do not use handler after successful close (inferred).

functions.name: xmlUTF8ToIsolat1
functions.signature: int xmlUTF8ToIsolat1(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen);
functions.description: Convert characters from UTF-8 to ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1). On success, updates *inlen to the number of bytes consumed and *outlen to the number of bytes produced; returns the number of bytes written or an xmlCharEncError code.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least *outlen bytes available on entry.
outlen must be non-NULL and initialized to the size of out in bytes; on return, set to bytes produced.
in must point to the input UTF-8 bytes.
inlen must be non-NULL and initialized to the size of in in bytes; on return, set to bytes consumed.
Caller must handle negative return values per xmlCharEncError (e.g., XML_ENC_ERR_INPUT, XML_ENC_ERR_SPACE, etc.).

functions.name: xmlIsolat1ToUTF8
functions.signature: int xmlIsolat1ToUTF8(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen);
functions.description: Convert characters from ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) to UTF-8. On success, updates *inlen to the number of bytes consumed and *outlen to the number of bytes produced; returns the number of bytes written or an xmlCharEncError code.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least *outlen bytes available on entry.
outlen must be non-NULL and initialized to the size of out in bytes; on return, set to bytes produced.
in must point to the input ISO-8859-1 bytes.
inlen must be non-NULL and initialized to the size of in in bytes; on return, set to bytes consumed.
Caller must handle negative return values per xmlCharEncError (e.g., XML_ENC_ERR_INPUT, XML_ENC_ERR_SPACE, etc.).

functions.name: UTF8Toisolat1
functions.signature: int UTF8Toisolat1(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen);
functions.description: Backward-compatibility macro alias of xmlUTF8ToIsolat1. Converts from UTF-8 to ISO-8859-1. Same semantics as xmlUTF8ToIsolat1. Deprecated alias.
requirements: Same requirements as xmlUTF8ToIsolat1.
This is a macro alias; link-time symbol is xmlUTF8ToIsolat1.

functions.name: isolat1ToUTF8
functions.signature: int isolat1ToUTF8(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen);
functions.description: Backward-compatibility macro alias of xmlIsolat1ToUTF8. Converts from ISO-8859-1 to UTF-8. Same semantics as xmlIsolat1ToUTF8. Deprecated alias.
requirements: Same requirements as xmlIsolat1ToUTF8.
This is a macro alias; link-time symbol is xmlIsolat1ToUTF8.

functions.name: xmlNewEntity
functions.signature: xmlEntity *xmlNewEntity(xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *name, int type, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Create a new entity declaration object attached to the given XML document. Typically used to construct internal or external entities (general or parameter) based on the specified type and identifiers. Returns a pointer to a newly created xmlEntity on success or NULL on failure (typical libxml2 pattern).
requirements: doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* originating from libxml2.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string naming the entity.
type should be one of the xmlEntityType values (e.g., XML_INTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITY, XML_EXTERNAL_GENERAL_PARSED_ENTITY, etc.).
publicId may be NULL or a NUL-terminated xmlChar PUBLIC identifier, depending on entity type (details not specified).
systemId may be NULL or a NUL-terminated xmlChar SYSTEM identifier, depending on entity type (details not specified).

content may be NULL; for internal entities it represents the replacement text; for unparsed entities it may represent notation/ndata (per struct comment), but exact creation requirements are not specified.
On success, the returned xmlEntity* is owned by the document; freeing is managed via libxml2 APIs (do not free with free()).
If allocation fails or parameters are invalid, the function may return NULL (inferred from libxml2 patterns).

functions.name: xmlFreeEntity
functions.description: Free an xmlEntity object and any resources it owns. Intended for entities created independently (not necessarily those managed by a document’s internal tables). Use with care; many entities are owned by a document/DTD and freed with the document.
requirements: entity may be NULL (no effect) or a valid xmlEntity*.
Only call this for entities that are not managed by an xmlDoc or DTD tables; freeing entities owned by a document may cause use-after-free (ownership details not fully specified here).
Do not use standard free(); always use this API to release an xmlEntity allocated by libxml2 when applicable.

functions.name: xmlAddEntity
functions.signature: int xmlAddEntity(xmlDoc *doc, int extSubset, const xmlChar *name, int type, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, const xmlChar *content, xmlEntity **out);
functions.description: Add (declare) an entity to a document’s entity tables. Can target either the internal or external subset (controlled by extSubset). Optionally returns the created/found entity via out. Return value indicates success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc*.
extSubset selects which subset to modify; valid values and semantics are not documented here (likely 0/1 for internal/external, but exact values unknown).
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string and a valid entity name.
type should be a value from xmlEntityType.
publicId may be NULL or a PUBLIC id depending on type (not fully specified).
systemId may be NULL or a SYSTEM id depending on type (not fully specified).
content may be NULL; for internal entities it is the replacement text; for unparsed entities it may be notation/ndata (not fully specified).
out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to storage for an xmlEntity* and will receive the created or existing entity pointer.
Do not free the returned entity directly; it is owned by the document and will be released with the document.

functions.name: xmlAddDocEntity
functions.signature: xmlEntity *xmlAddDocEntity(xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *name, int type, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Declare and add an entity to the document’s internal subset. Returns a pointer to the created (or existing) entity, or NULL on failure.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*.
name must be non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar.
type should be one of xmlEntityType.
publicId and systemId may be NULL depending on entity type (not specified).
content may be NULL; its meaning depends on entity type (replacement text vs. notation/ndata).
Returned entity is owned by the document; do not free it manually.

functions.name: xmlAddDtdEntity
functions.signature: xmlEntity *xmlAddDtdEntity(xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *name, int type, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Declare and add an entity to the document’s external subset (DTD). Returns the entity pointer or NULL on failure.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*.
name must be non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar.
type should be one of xmlEntityType.
publicId and systemId may be NULL depending on entity type (not specified).
content may be NULL; semantics depend on entity type.
The returned entity is owned by the document/DTD; do not free it manually.

functions.name: xmlGetPredefinedEntity
functions.description: Lookup one of the predefined XML entities by name (e.g., amp, lt, gt, apos, quot). Returns the predefined entity or NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar name of a predefined entity.
Returned pointer refers to a predefined, static entity; it must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: xmlGetDocEntity
functions.description: Lookup a general entity by name in the given document’s entity tables. Returns the entity if found or NULL otherwise.
requirements: doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* and must outlive the returned entity pointer.
name must be non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar.
The returned pointer is owned by the document; do not free it.

functions.name: xmlGetDtdEntity
functions.description: Lookup an entity declaration by name in the document’s DTD (typically the external subset). Returns the entity or NULL if not found.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*.
name must be non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar.
Returned entity is owned by the document/DTD and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: xmlGetParameterEntity
functions.description: Lookup a parameter entity by name within the document’s DTD context. Returns the entity or NULL if not found.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*.
name must be non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar.
Returned entity is owned by the document/DTD; do not free it.

functions.name: xmlEncodeEntitiesReentrant
functions.description: Escape XML special characters and entity references in the input string according to the document’s settings. Produces a newly allocated xmlChar string with entity-encoded content. Reentrant and safe to use without shared global state.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc* (used for entity/encoding context).
input must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
The returned xmlChar* points to newly allocated memory; the caller must free it using xmlFree() (libxml2 convention).
Returns NULL on allocation failure or invalid input (inferred from libxml2 patterns).

functions.name: xmlEncodeSpecialChars
functions.description: Escape only the special XML characters in input (such as '&', '<', '>', '"', and possibly apostrophe), producing a newly allocated, encoded string. Uses the document context for encoding rules.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc* (const).
input must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
The returned xmlChar* is newly allocated and must be freed with xmlFree().
Returns NULL on allocation failure or invalid input (inferred).

functions.name: xmlCreateEntitiesTable
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Create a new, standalone entities hash table. Modern code should manipulate entities via document/DTD APIs instead of standalone tables.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned table (if non-NULL) is heap-allocated and must be freed with xmlFreeEntitiesTable().
API is marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlCopyEntitiesTable
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Create a deep copy of an existing entities table.
requirements: table must be a valid xmlEntitiesTable* created by libxml2 (e.g., via xmlCreateEntitiesTable or from an existing document).
Returns a newly allocated copy which must be freed with xmlFreeEntitiesTable().
May return NULL on failure (inferred).
API is marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlFreeEntitiesTable
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Free an entities table created or copied by the standalone table APIs.
requirements: table may be NULL (no effect) or a valid xmlEntitiesTable* previously obtained from libxml2.
Do not use after freeing. This should not be used on tables owned by an xmlDoc/DTD unless explicitly created standalone.

functions.name: xmlDumpEntitiesTable
functions.description: DEPRECATED, output-only: Serialize (dump) an entities table into the provided xmlBuffer. Available only when LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED is defined at build time.
requirements: This function is available only if the library was built with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
buf must be a valid, writable xmlBuffer*.
table must be a valid xmlEntitiesTable* or NULL (behavior for NULL not specified).
Does not transfer ownership of buf or table; caller retains ownership.
Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlDumpEntityDecl
functions.description: DEPRECATED, output-only: Serialize (dump) a single entity declaration into the provided xmlBuffer. Available only when LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED is defined at build time.
requirements: This function is available only if the library was built with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
buf must be a valid, writable xmlBuffer*.
ent must be a valid xmlEntity* (not NULL).
Does not transfer ownership of buf or ent; caller retains ownership.
Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlHashCreate
functions.description: Constructs a new hash table of (string -> void*) entries. Typical usage: call to obtain a table handle before adding entries. Details of bucket sizing and return-on-error values are not documented here.
requirements: size is expected to be a positive integer specifying initial table size (exact bounds/rounding behavior unknown)
Returns a non-NULL xmlHashTable* on success or NULL on failure (inferred)
The returned table must later be released with xmlHashFree

functions.name: xmlHashCreateDict
functions.description: Constructs a new hash table using an optional xmlDict for string storage/interning. Use when you want the table to cooperate with a pre-existing dictionary. Behavior on NULL dict is not specified here.
requirements: size is expected to be a positive integer specifying initial table size (exact bounds/rounding behavior unknown)
dict, if non-NULL, must be a valid xmlDict* (lifetime/ownership semantics not specified in this header)
Returns a non-NULL xmlHashTable* on success or NULL on failure (inferred)
The returned table must later be released with xmlHashFree

functions.name: xmlHashFree
functions.description: Destroys a hash table and releases all resources. If dealloc is provided, it is called for each entry’s payload before the table is freed.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable* previously created by xmlHashCreate or xmlHashCreateDict
dealloc, if non-NULL, must be a function capable of freeing each stored payload; it will be invoked with (payload, name) for each entry
After this call, hash must not be used again

functions.name: xmlHashDefaultDeallocator
functions.description: Default deallocator callback suitable for use with xmlHashFree or remove/update operations. Frees an entry’s payload using libxml2’s default convention. The exact freeing behavior depends on how payloads were allocated; details are not described here.
requirements: entry is the payload previously stored in the table; it must be compatible with the default freeing strategy (unknown specifics)
name is the key name associated with the payload (read-only, not modified)

functions.name: xmlHashAdd
functions.description: Inserts a new entry under the string key name with payload userdata. Fails if the key already exists (based on naming).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name must be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string identifying the key
userdata is an opaque pointer stored as-is; caller owns its allocation strategy
Return code semantics (success/failure values) are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashAddEntry
functions.description: Adds a new (name -> userdata) entry. Alias of xmlHashAdd with identical semantics.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name must be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string
userdata is stored verbatim; caller manages its lifetime
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashUpdateEntry
functions.signature: int xmlHashUpdateEntry(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, void *userdata, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Inserts or updates an entry under name. If an entry already exists, it is replaced and dealloc is called on the previous payload before overwriting.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name must be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string
dealloc must be able to free any existing payload associated with name; it is called as dealloc(oldPayload, name) when replacing
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashAdd2
functions.signature: int xmlHashAdd2(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, void *userdata);
functions.description: Inserts a new entry keyed by the pair (name, name2) with payload userdata. Intended for composite keys of two strings; typically fails if the key already exists.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
userdata is stored verbatim; caller manages its lifetime
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashAddEntry2
functions.signature: int xmlHashAddEntry2(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a new entry with a two-part string key (name, name2). Alias of xmlHashAdd2 by naming convention.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
userdata is stored verbatim; caller manages its lifetime
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashUpdateEntry2
functions.signature: int xmlHashUpdateEntry2(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, void *userdata, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Inserts or updates an entry keyed by (name, name2). If an entry exists, it is replaced and dealloc is called on the previous payload.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
dealloc must be able to free any existing payload for the composite key; it is called as dealloc(oldPayload, name) (exact name passed for second part unknown)
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashAdd3
functions.signature: int xmlHashAdd3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, void *userdata);
functions.description: Inserts a new entry keyed by the triple (name, name2, name3) with payload userdata. Typically fails if the key already exists.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
userdata is stored verbatim; caller manages its lifetime
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashAddEntry3
functions.signature: int xmlHashAddEntry3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, void *userdata);
functions.description: Adds a new entry with a three-part string key (name, name2, name3). Alias of xmlHashAdd3 by naming convention.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
userdata is stored verbatim; caller manages its lifetime
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashUpdateEntry3
functions.signature: int xmlHashUpdateEntry3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, void *userdata, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Inserts or updates an entry keyed by (name, name2, name3). If an entry exists, it is replaced and dealloc is called on the previous payload.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
dealloc must be able to free any existing payload for the composite key; it is called with the old payload (exact name parameters passed are not specified)
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashRemoveEntry
functions.signature: int xmlHashRemoveEntry(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Removes the entry under key name. If dealloc is provided, it is called on the removed payload before unlinking.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name must be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string
dealloc, if non-NULL, must be able to free the payload associated with name; it is called as dealloc(payload, name)
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashRemoveEntry2
functions.signature: int xmlHashRemoveEntry2(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Removes the entry under the two-part key (name, name2). If dealloc is provided, it is called on the removed payload.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
dealloc, if non-NULL, must be able to free the payload associated with the composite key
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashRemoveEntry3
functions.signature: int xmlHashRemoveEntry3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, xmlHashDeallocator dealloc);
functions.description: Removes the entry under the three-part key (name, name2, name3). If dealloc is provided, it is called on the removed payload.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings
dealloc, if non-NULL, must be able to free the payload associated with the composite key
Return code semantics are not documented here

functions.name: xmlHashLookup
functions.description: Looks up the payload stored under key name and returns it. Returns NULL if no such entry exists (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name must be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string
Returned pointer is the stored payload; lifetime/ownership is managed by the table’s client code

functions.name: xmlHashLookup2
functions.description: Looks up the payload stored under the two-part key (name, name2). Returns NULL if not found (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings

functions.name: xmlHashLookup3
functions.signature: void *xmlHashLookup3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3);
functions.description: Looks up the payload stored under the three-part key (name, name2, name3). Returns NULL if not found (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings

functions.name: xmlHashQLookup
functions.description: Looks up an entry using a qualified name composed of (prefix, name). Useful for namespace-like keys. Returns the stored payload or NULL if not found (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
prefix and name must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings (allowance for NULL prefix unknown)

functions.name: xmlHashQLookup2
functions.signature: void *xmlHashQLookup2(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *prefix, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *prefix2, const xmlChar *name2);
functions.description: Looks up an entry using a qualified two-part key: (prefix,name) and (prefix2,name2). Returns the stored payload or NULL if not found (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
prefix, name, prefix2, and name2 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings

functions.name: xmlHashQLookup3
functions.signature: void *xmlHashQLookup3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *prefix, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *prefix2, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *prefix3, const xmlChar *name3);
functions.description: Looks up an entry using a qualified three-part key: (prefix,name), (prefix2,name2), (prefix3,name3). Returns the stored payload or NULL if not found (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
prefix, name, prefix2, name2, prefix3, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings

functions.name: xmlHashCopySafe
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of a hash table by invoking copy on each payload. If copying an entry fails, dealloc is available to clean up any partially created payloads, enabling a safer copy operation.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
copy must return a new payload copy for each (payload,name) or NULL on error; it must be safe to call for every entry
dealloc must be able to free payloads created by copy in case of failure; it may be called with (payload,name) for cleanup
Returns a new xmlHashTable* on success or NULL on failure (inferred)

functions.name: xmlHashCopy
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of a hash table by invoking copy on each payload. Lacks an explicit cleanup callback; error-handling behavior on partial failures is unspecified here.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
copy must return a new payload copy for each (payload,name) or NULL on error; its allocation must be compatible with eventual deallocation by the caller
Returns a new xmlHashTable* on success or NULL on failure (inferred)

functions.name: xmlHashSize
functions.description: Returns the number of entries currently stored in the hash table (inferred).
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*

functions.name: xmlHashScan
functions.description: Iterates over all entries in the table, invoking scan(payload, data, name) for each. Order of iteration is not specified.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
scan must be a valid callback; it will be called for each entry as scan(payload, data, name)
data is an opaque user pointer passed through to the callback
Callback must tolerate being called multiple times; it must not assume any particular iteration order

functions.name: xmlHashScan3
functions.signature: void xmlHashScan3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, xmlHashScanner scan, void *data);
functions.description: Scans entries matching the composite key (name, name2, name3), invoking scan(payload, data, name) for each match. Matching rules beyond equality are not described here.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings identifying which subset to scan
scan must be a valid callback; it will be called as scan(payload, data, name)
data is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: xmlHashScanFull
functions.description: Iterates over all entries, invoking scan(payload, data, name, name2, name3) with full key components for each entry. Order of iteration is not specified.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
scan must be a valid callback; it will be called as scan(payload, data, name, name2, name3)
data is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: xmlHashScanFull3
functions.signature: void xmlHashScanFull3(xmlHashTable *hash, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *name2, const xmlChar *name3, xmlHashScannerFull scan, void *data);
functions.description: Scans entries matching the composite key (name, name2, name3) and invokes the full scanner callback scan(payload, data, name, name2, name3) for each match.
requirements: hash must be a valid xmlHashTable*
name, name2, and name3 must be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings identifying which subset to scan
scan must be a valid callback; it will be called as scan(payload, data, name, name2, name3)
data is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: htmlInitAutoClose
functions.description: Initialize internal tables/state used for auto-closing HTML elements in the legacy HTML tree builder. Deprecated API retained for backward compatibility.
requirements: May be called before using other legacy auto-close helpers (htmlIsAutoClosed/htmlAutoCloseTag).
Thread-safety of global initialization is unspecified; avoid concurrent first-time calls.

functions.name: htmlTagLookup
functions.description: Lookup the (deprecated) descriptor for an HTML element by tag name and return metadata describing that element (HTML 4.01/XHTML 1.0 model). Deprecated.
requirements: tag must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (xmlChar*).
Returns NULL if tag is unknown.

functions.name: htmlEntityLookup
functions.description: Lookup an HTML entity by its name and return its descriptor (code point, name, description). Deprecated.
requirements: name must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (xmlChar*), not NULL.
Returns NULL if the entity is not found.

functions.name: htmlEntityValueLookup
functions.description: Lookup an HTML entity by its Unicode code point and return its descriptor. Deprecated.
requirements: value is a Unicode scalar value; out-of-range values return NULL.
Returns NULL if no named entity corresponds to value.

functions.name: htmlIsAutoClosed
functions.description: Check whether the given element node has been implicitly auto-closed by the legacy HTML parser’s auto-close rules. Deprecated.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc* from this library.
elem must be a node belonging to doc and not NULL.
Returns nonzero if considered auto-closed, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: htmlAutoCloseTag
functions.description: Apply legacy auto-close rules to close open elements up to the named tag, adjusting the tree accordingly. Deprecated.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*.
name must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 element name (not NULL).
elem must be a node belonging to doc (may be the current insertion point).
Returns nonzero on success/changes, 0 if no action was taken or on failure.

functions.name: htmlParseEntityRef
functions.description: Parse an entity reference from the given string pointer in the context of an HTML parse and return its descriptor. Advances *str past the parsed reference. Deprecated.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCtxt*.
str must be non-NULL and point to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 buffer; *str should point at the beginning of an entity reference (typically '&').
On failure, returns NULL and advances position according to parser behavior (unspecified).

functions.name: htmlParseCharRef
functions.description: Parse a numeric character reference (e.g., &#xNN; or &#NN;) from the current input position in the parser context. Returns the Unicode code point or 0 on failure. Deprecated.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCtxt* positioned at a character reference start ('&').
Return value 0 indicates failure; positive value is the parsed code point.

functions.name: htmlParseElement
functions.description: Parse a single HTML element (start tag, content per legacy algorithm, and end tag handling) from the current parser context position. Deprecated.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCtxt* with input initialized.
Side effects include modifications to the document tree within ctxt.

functions.name: htmlNewParserCtxt
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new HTML parser context for pull-style or higher-level parsing routines.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with htmlFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: htmlNewSAXParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new HTML parser context configured with a SAX handler and user data for event-driven parsing.
requirements: If sax is non-NULL, it must point to a properly initialized htmlSAXHandler structure (callbacks may be NULL individually).
userData is passed to SAX callbacks unmodified.
Returns NULL on failure.
Free with htmlFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: htmlCreateMemoryParserCtxt
functions.description: Create an HTML parser context that reads from an in-memory buffer.
requirements: buffer must point to at least size bytes; it need not be NUL-terminated.
size must be >= 0; size == 0 produces an empty input.
Returns NULL on failure.
Free the context with htmlFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: htmlParseDocument
functions.description: Parse a complete HTML document using the provided parser context and build the resulting tree or emit SAX events depending on configuration.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCtxt* with input configured (e.g., by a create* function).
Return value is 0 on success and a negative value on error (exact codes unspecified).

functions.name: htmlSAXParseDoc
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlSAXParseDoc(const xmlChar *cur, const char *encoding, htmlSAXHandler *sax, void *userData);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string with a custom SAX handler. Builds a doc if handler permits; legacy interface. Deprecated.
requirements: cur must be a NUL-terminated XML/HTML character buffer (xmlChar*).
encoding may be NULL or a label of the source encoding; ignored in many cases.
sax may be NULL (defaults apply) or point to a valid handler; callbacks can be selectively provided.
userData is passed to callbacks.
Returns NULL on parse failure.

functions.name: htmlParseDoc
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a NUL-terminated memory buffer and return a document tree.
requirements: cur must be a NUL-terminated xmlChar* buffer.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCreateFileParserCtxt
functions.description: Create an HTML parser context that reads from a file on disk.
requirements: filename must be a valid path to a readable file; not NULL.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the source encoding.
Returns NULL on failure (e.g., file not found).
Free with htmlFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: htmlSAXParseFile
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlSAXParseFile(const char *filename, const char *encoding, htmlSAXHandler *sax, void *userData);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a file using a custom SAX handler. Legacy interface. Deprecated.
requirements: filename must be a readable file path; not NULL.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the source encoding.
sax may be NULL or a valid handler; if provided, its fields should be initialized.
userData is passed to callbacks.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlParseFile
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a file and return the resulting document tree.
requirements: filename must name a readable file; not NULL.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the source encoding.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlUTF8ToHtml
functions.signature: int htmlUTF8ToHtml(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen);
functions.description: Convert UTF-8 input to an HTML-escaped form, writing ASCII plus character/entity references into out. Returns 0 on success or a negative value on error. Deprecated.
requirements: out may be NULL to query the required output size; otherwise it must point to a buffer of at least *outlen bytes.
outlen must point to the available size on entry; set to bytes written on return.
in must point to the input buffer; may be NULL if *inlen is 0.
inlen must point to the number of input bytes available; set to bytes consumed on return.
Conversion stops on buffer exhaustion or end of input.

functions.name: htmlEncodeEntities
functions.signature: int htmlEncodeEntities(unsigned char *out, int *outlen, const unsigned char *in, int *inlen, int quoteChar);
functions.description: Encode characters in the input as HTML entities suitable for inclusion in attribute or text content. quoteChar controls whether and which quote to escape. Deprecated.
requirements: out may be NULL to query needed size; otherwise must have at least *outlen bytes available.
outlen must be set to output buffer size on entry; updated to bytes written.
in must point to the input buffer (may be NULL if *inlen is 0).
inlen must be set to input length on entry; updated to bytes consumed.
quoteChar specifies the attribute quote to protect (typically ' or "). Use 0 to indicate generic text escaping.

functions.name: htmlIsScriptAttribute
functions.description: Return nonzero if the attribute name is considered to potentially contain script code (legacy heuristic). Deprecated.
requirements: name must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 attribute name, not NULL.
Return value is nonzero for names treated as script-related; 0 otherwise.

functions.name: htmlHandleOmittedElem
functions.description: Enable or disable legacy handling for omitted HTML elements (e.g., implied start/end tags). Returns the previous setting. Deprecated.
requirements: val should be 0 to disable or nonzero to enable behavior.
Thread-safety of the global setting is unspecified; avoid changing it concurrently across threads.

functions.name: htmlCreatePushParserCtxt
functions.signature: htmlParserCtxt * htmlCreatePushParserCtxt(htmlSAXHandler *sax, void *user_data, const char *chunk, int size, const char *filename, xmlCharEncoding enc);
functions.description: Create a push-mode HTML parser context with optional initial data and a SAX handler, suitable for incremental feeding via htmlParseChunk. Available when compiled with push support.
requirements: Requires the library to be built with LIBXML_PUSH_ENABLED.
sax may be NULL or a valid handler; its fields should be initialized as needed.
user_data is passed to callbacks.
chunk may be NULL if size is 0; otherwise must point to at least size bytes.
size must be >= 0.
filename may be NULL or a hint used for error reporting/URL resolution.
enc specifies an initial character encoding hint.
Returns NULL on failure. Free with htmlFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: htmlParseChunk
functions.signature: int htmlParseChunk(htmlParserCtxt *ctxt, const char *chunk, int size, int terminate);
functions.description: Feed a chunk of data to a push-mode HTML parser. If terminate is nonzero, signal end-of-input and finalize parsing.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid push parser context created by htmlCreatePushParserCtxt.
chunk may be NULL only if size == 0 or when terminate != 0 to indicate no more data.
size must be >= 0 and reflect the number of bytes available at chunk.
terminate should be 0 while more data will follow; set to nonzero with the last call.
Returns 0 on success; negative values indicate errors.

functions.name: htmlFreeParserCtxt
functions.description: Free an HTML parser context and associated resources.
requirements: ctxt may be NULL (no effect); otherwise must have been allocated by a corresponding html*Create*/htmlNew* function.
Must not be used after being freed.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReset
functions.description: Reset an HTML parser context to a clean state for reuse.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCxt* (non-NULL).
All previously associated input sources should be finished; resetting in the middle of a parse is undefined.

functions.name: htmlCtxtSetOptions
functions.description: Set parser options on an HTML parser context. Options are a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
requirements: ctxt must be non-NULL.
options must be composed of htmlParserOption bit flags.
Returns 0 on success; negative value on error.

functions.name: htmlCtxtUseOptions
functions.description: Apply and possibly act upon parser options for the given context. Similar to htmlCtxtSetOptions.
requirements: ctxt must be non-NULL.
options must be a combination of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns 0 on success; negative value on error.

functions.name: htmlReadDoc
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlReadDoc(const xmlChar *cur, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a NUL-terminated memory buffer and return a document tree, with fine-grained control via options.
requirements: cur must be a NUL-terminated xmlChar* buffer.
URL may be NULL or a base URI for the document (affects error messages and relative resolution).
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption values.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlReadFile
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlReadFile(const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from a file or URL-like path and return the document tree.
requirements: URL must be a readable path or supported URI; not NULL.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption values.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlReadMemory
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlReadMemory(const char *buffer, int size, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from an in-memory buffer and return a document tree.
requirements: buffer must point to at least size bytes; may be non-NUL-terminated.
size must be >= 0.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a combination of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlReadFd
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlReadFd(int fd, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document from an open file descriptor and return the document tree.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable file descriptor positioned at the start of the content.
The function will read from fd until EOF or completion; caller is responsible for closing fd afterwards.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a combination of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlReadIO
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlReadIO(xmlInputReadCallback ioread, xmlInputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document using custom I/O callbacks and return the document tree.
requirements: ioread must be a valid callback that returns bytes read or 0/negative on EOF/error.
ioclose must be a valid callback to close the input; may be NULL if not needed.
ioctx is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks; may be NULL if callbacks accept it.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtParseDocument
functions.description: Parse a document using a provided HTML parser context and an explicit input source object, returning the resulting document.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid htmlParserCtxt*.
input must be a valid xmlParserInput* initialized to provide data.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReadDoc
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlCtxtReadDoc(xmlParserCtxt *ctxt, const xmlChar *cur, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document into an existing generic parser context from a NUL-terminated buffer.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlParserCtxt* prepared for HTML parsing.
cur must be a NUL-terminated xmlChar* buffer.
URL may be NULL or a base URI.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReadFile
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlCtxtReadFile(xmlParserCtxt *ctxt, const char *filename, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document into an existing generic parser context from a file.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlParserCtxt* prepared for HTML parsing.
filename must be a readable path; not NULL.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReadMemory
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlCtxtReadMemory(xmlParserCtxt *ctxt, const char *buffer, int size, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document into an existing generic parser context from a memory buffer.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlParserCtxt* prepared for HTML parsing.
buffer must point to at least size bytes.
size must be >= 0.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a combination of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReadFd
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlCtxtReadFd(xmlParserCtxt *ctxt, int fd, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document into an existing generic parser context from an open file descriptor.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlParserCtxt* prepared for HTML parsing.
fd must be a valid readable descriptor.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlCtxtReadIO
functions.signature: xmlDoc * htmlCtxtReadIO(xmlParserCtxt *ctxt, xmlInputReadCallback ioread, xmlInputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Parse an HTML document into an existing generic parser context using custom I/O callbacks.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlParserCtxt* prepared for HTML parsing.
ioread must be a valid read callback; ioclose may be NULL or a valid close callback.
ioctx is passed to callbacks; may be NULL if callbacks accept it.
URL may be NULL or a base URI string.
encoding may be NULL or a label for the input encoding.
options is a bitwise OR of htmlParserOption flags.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: htmlAttrAllowed
functions.signature: htmlStatus htmlAttrAllowed(const htmlElemDesc* , const xmlChar* , int);
functions.description: Check whether an attribute (by name) is allowed on a given HTML element according to the deprecated internal content model; returns a status mask. Deprecated.
requirements: First parameter must point to a valid htmlElemDesc for the element.
Second parameter must be a NUL-terminated attribute name (xmlChar*).
Third parameter is an int flag bitmask (semantics unspecified in this header).
Return value is a bitmask of htmlStatus values.

functions.name: htmlElementAllowedHere
functions.description: Check whether a child element name is allowed at the current context of a parent element descriptor in the deprecated model. Deprecated.
requirements: First parameter must point to a valid htmlElemDesc describing the parent element.
Second parameter must be a NUL-terminated child element name (xmlChar*).
Returns nonzero if allowed, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: htmlElementStatusHere
functions.description: Return the status of placing a given element within a given parent according to the deprecated content model. Deprecated.
requirements: Both parameters must point to valid htmlElemDesc structures (parent and child).
Return value is a bitmask of htmlStatus values describing validity/deprecation/requirement.

functions.name: htmlNodeStatus
functions.description: Evaluate the status of an XML/HTML node in context according to the deprecated HTML model, returning a status mask. Deprecated.
requirements: First parameter must be a valid xmlNode* (may be an element node).
Second parameter is an int flag bitmask (semantics unspecified in this header).
Return value is a bitmask of htmlStatus values.

functions.name: htmlNewDoc
functions.description: Create a new HTML xmlDoc. Likely initializes a document node with the provided system/public identifiers (URI and ExternalID) for the DTD. Used to programmatically construct an HTML document prior to serialization or manipulation. Exact initialization details are not specified in this header.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED).
URI and ExternalID, if provided, should be valid null-terminated xmlChar strings; passing NULL is allowed or disallowed unknown.
Returns an xmlDoc*; ownership/allocation and required deallocation routine are unknown from this header (consult libxml2 docs).
Resulting xmlDoc* must be used only with libxml2 APIs expecting an HTML document.

functions.name: htmlNewDocNoDtD
functions.description: Create a new HTML xmlDoc without attaching a DTD. Used when a minimal HTML document is needed or when the caller manages the DTD separately. Specifics of how URI and ExternalID are used are not defined here.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED).
URI and ExternalID should be valid null-terminated xmlChar strings; NULL handling is unknown.
Returns an xmlDoc*; allocation/ownership and how to free are unknown from this header.
Use the returned document only with libxml2 functions that accept HTML documents.

functions.name: htmlGetMetaEncoding
functions.description: Retrieve the character encoding declared via HTML META elements for the given document. Useful to determine the output/input charset associated with the HTML content. Exact return semantics (e.g., NULL when not present, ownership) are not specified here.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED).
doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* representing an HTML document.
Return pointer lifetime/ownership is unknown; treat as read-only and non-owning unless documentation states otherwise.

functions.name: htmlSetMetaEncoding
functions.description: Set or update the HTML META-declared character encoding for the document. Intended to control serialization and processing charset via META tags. Return value semantics (success/error codes) are not specified in this header.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED).
doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* for an HTML document.
encoding should be a valid, null-terminated xmlChar string naming a character encoding; whether NULL unsets encoding is unknown.
Caller must handle the returned int status; exact success/error convention is unknown.

functions.name: htmlDocDumpMemory
functions.description: Serialize an entire HTML document into a memory buffer. Writes the serialized bytes and length to the provided output pointers. Allocation and freeing details for the produced buffer are not specified in this header.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED) and output enabled (LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED).
cur must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* for an HTML document.
mem must be a non-NULL pointer to xmlChar* (output location).
size must be a non-NULL pointer to int (output size).
Buffer ownership and required deallocation function are unknown from this header; consult library docs before freeing.

functions.name: htmlDocDumpMemoryFormat
functions.signature: void htmlDocDumpMemoryFormat(xmlDoc *cur, xmlChar **mem, int *size, int format);
functions.description: Serialize an HTML document to a memory buffer with optional formatting control (e.g., pretty-print vs. raw). The meaning of the format flag is not defined in this header. Buffer allocation/freeing rules are not specified here.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED) and output enabled (LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED).
cur must be a valid, initialized html xmlDoc*.
mem must be a non-NULL pointer to xmlChar* (output buffer pointer).
size must be a non-NULL pointer to int (output size).
format is an integer flag; accepted values and effects are unknown from this header.
Caller must know how to free the returned buffer; details are unknown here.

functions.name: htmlSaveFile
functions.description: Serialize and save an HTML document to a file on disk using default encoding/format settings. Returns an integer status; exact semantics are not specified in this header.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED) and output enabled (LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED).
filename must be a valid, null-terminated path to a writable file; whether it may be NULL is unknown.
cur must be a valid, initialized html xmlDoc*.
Caller must check the returned int for success/failure; exact convention is unknown.

functions.name: htmlSaveFileEnc
functions.signature: int htmlSaveFileEnc(const char *filename, xmlDoc *cur, const char *encoding);
functions.description: Serialize and save an HTML document to a file using a specified character encoding. Returns an integer status; precise success/error codes are not defined here.
requirements: Library must be built with HTML support (LIBXML_HTML_ENABLED) and output enabled (LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED).
filename must be a valid, writable path string.
cur must be a valid, initialized html xmlDoc*.
encoding should be a valid, null-terminated encoding name; whether NULL selects a default is unknown.
Caller must check the returned int; semantics are unspecified here.

functions.name: htmlSaveFileFormat
functions.signature: int htmlSaveFileFormat(const char *filename, xmlDoc *cur, const char *encoding, int format);
functions.description: Serialize and save an HTML document to a file with specified encoding and formatting options. The meaning of the format flag is not defined here. Returns an int status.

Exact return codes are unknown; callers should check for non-zero/zero per library documentation (not present here).

requirements: pattern must point to a null-terminated UTF-8 xmlChar string containing a valid pattern expression.

namespaces may be NULL, or if non-NULL must reference an array of const xmlChar* entries providing prefix/URI pairs, terminated by a NULL entry, following libxml2 namespace binding conventions.
On failure, returns NULL; callers must check the return value before use.
The returned xmlPattern* must be freed with xmlFreePattern (or xmlFreePatternList if part of a list).

functions.name: xmlPatternCompileSafe
functions.signature: int xmlPatternCompileSafe(const xmlChar *pattern, xmlDict *dict, int flags, const xmlChar **namespaces, xmlPattern **patternOut);
functions.description: Safe variant of xmlPatterncompile that returns a status code and writes the compiled pattern to an out-parameter. Intended to avoid returning NULL and to make error handling explicit.
requirements: pattern must be a null-terminated xmlChar string with the pattern to compile.
dict, if provided, must be a valid xmlDict pointer appropriate for the intended usage.
flags must be a bitmask of xmlPatternFlags (XML_PATTERN_DEFAULT, XML_PATTERN_XPATH, XML_PATTERN_XSSEL, XML_PATTERN_XSFIELD).
namespaces may be NULL, or if non-NULL must be an array of const xmlChar* providing prefix/URI pairs terminated by NULL.

patternOut must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlPattern* variable where the result will be stored on success; on failure, the function will not provide a usable pattern (exact out-parameter semantics on failure are unknown).
Callers must check the returned int status before using *patternOut; non-zero/specific values indicating success or failure are not specified here (exact conventions unknown).
On success, the caller becomes responsible for freeing the resulting pattern with xmlFreePattern (or xmlFreePatternList).

functions.name: xmlPatternMatch

Not thread-safe to use the same xmlPattern object concurrently across multiple threads without external synchronization unless the implementation guarantees reentrancy.

functions.name: xmlPatternMinDepth
functions.description: Returns the minimum depth at which the pattern can match in streaming evaluation. Useful for early pruning during streaming.
requirements: comp must be a valid compiled xmlPattern pointer.
Returned int indicates a depth; callers should handle negative values as errors if applicable (exact error conventions unknown).

functions.name: xmlPatternFromRoot

requirements: comp must be a valid compiled xmlPattern pointer.

functions.name: xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt
functions.description: Creates or obtains a streaming context for evaluating the compiled pattern incrementally via push/pop SAX-style events.
requirements: comp must be a valid compiled xmlPattern pointer that is streamable (typically check with xmlPatternStreamable before calling).
On success returns a non-NULL xmlStreamCtxt* to be used with xmlStreamPushNode/xmlStreamPush/xmlStreamPushAttr/xmlStreamPop; callers must free it with xmlFreeStreamCtxt when done.
On failure returns NULL; callers must check the return value before use.

functions.name: xmlFreeStreamCtxt
functions.description: Frees a streaming context obtained via xmlPatternGetStreamCxt (or equivalent). Releases all resources associated with the streaming match state.
requirements: stream must be a pointer returned by xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt, or NULL (behavior on NULL is library-defined/unknown).
Do not use the stream after freeing it.

functions.name: xmlStreamPushNode
functions.signature: int xmlStreamPushNode(xmlStreamCtxt *stream, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns, int nodeType);
functions.description: Pushes a node event into the streaming context, providing the node's local name, namespace URI, and node type. Used to feed a SAX-like stream to evaluate pattern matches incrementally.
requirements: stream must be a valid xmlStreamCtxt* obtained from xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt.
name must be a null-terminated xmlChar string for the node's local name; may be NULL for wildcard tests depending on pattern (exact acceptance unknown).
ns may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string with the namespace URI corresponding to name.
nodeType must be a valid libxml2 node type value (from xmlElementType enum).
Callers must maintain correct hierarchical order: push parent nodes before children and use xmlStreamPop when exiting a node scope.
Return value is an int status indicating progression/match state; callers must check and handle non-success values (exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: xmlStreamPush
functions.signature: int xmlStreamPush(xmlStreamCtxt *stream, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);

functions.name: xmlStreamPushAttr

functions.description: Pushes an attribute node event into the streaming context with the attribute's local name and namespace URI. Used to evaluate attribute-related parts of a pattern during streaming.
requirements: stream must be a valid xmlStreamCtxt* from xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt.

Should be called in a context where an owning element has been pushed if required by the pattern; exact ordering beyond this is implementation-specific/unknown.
Return value is an int status; callers must check and handle it (exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: xmlStreamPop
functions.description: Signals the end of the current node's scope in the streaming context (e.g., element end tag). Must mirror prior push calls to maintain correct depth.
requirements: stream must be a valid xmlStreamCtxt* from xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt.
Calls must follow a proper LIFO order matching prior xmlStreamPush/xmlStreamPushNode invocations so that nesting is balanced.
Return value is an int status; callers must check and handle it (exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: xmlStreamWantsAnyNode

requirements: stream must be a valid xmlStreamCtxt* from xmlPatternGetStreamCtxt.
