The caller retains ownership of doc and must keep it alive until the parser context is no longer needed, unless a parser flag transfers ownership (see xmlRelaxParserSetFlag).

functions.name: xmlRelaxParserSetFlag
functions.description: Sets a parser flag on a Relax NG parser context. Recognized flags match xmlRelaxNGParserFlag (e.g., XML_RELAXNGP_FREE_DOC, XML_RELAXNGP_CRNG).
requirements: ctxt must be a non-NULL parser context created by xmlRelaxNGNew*ParserCtxt().
flag should be one of xmlRelaxNGParserFlag values: 0 (XML_RELAXNGP_NONE), 1 (XML_RELAXNGP_FREE_DOC), or 2 (XML_RELAXNGP_CRNG). Values outside this enum are unspecified.
Return value semantics are not documented here; caller should check for nonzero or negative values to detect failure.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGFreeParserCtxt
functions.description: Frees a Relax NG parser context and any resources associated with it.
requirements: ctxt may be NULL (common libxml2 pattern), in which case the function does nothing; otherwise it must be a valid context created by xmlRelaxNGNew*ParserCtxt().
After this call, ctxt must not be used again.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGSetParserErrors
functions.signature: void xmlRelaxNGSetParserErrors(xmlRelaxNGParserCtxt *ctxt, xmlRelaxNGValidityErrorFunc err, xmlRelaxNGValidityWarningFunc warn, void *ctx);
functions.description: Registers error and warning callback functions for schema parsing diagnostics. Callbacks receive messages during parsing of the schema.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context.
err and/or warn may be NULL to disable that kind of callback; behavior for NULL is consistent with libxml2 patterns (message suppressed).
ctx is a user-supplied pointer passed back to the callbacks; it is not used by libxml2 otherwise and must remain valid for the lifetime of ctxt or until callbacks are changed.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGGetParserErrors
functions.description: Retrieves the currently set error and warning callbacks and their user context from a parser context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context.
err, warn, and ctx are output parameters; pass non-NULL pointers to receive values. Passing NULL for any of them will skip that output.
Returns an int status; exact semantics are not documented here (typical libxml2 returns 0 on success). Callers should check return value for failure indication.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGSetParserStructuredErrors
functions.description: Registers a structured error callback for schema parsing, receiving xmlError objects via the libxml2 structured error mechanism.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context.
serror may be NULL to disable structured errors; otherwise it must conform to xmlStructuredErrorFunc.
ctx is an opaque user pointer provided back on callback and must remain valid while installed.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGSetResourceLoader
functions.description: Installs a custom resource loader callback for schema includes/imports and external resource resolution during Relax NG schema parsing.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context.
loader must be a valid function conforming to xmlResourceLoader; pass NULL to revert to defaults (behavior per libxml2).
vctxt is a user context pointer for loader and must remain valid while in use.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGParse
functions.description: Parses and compiles a Relax NG schema using the given parser context, returning a compiled schema handle for validation.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context created by xmlRelaxNGNew*ParserCtxt().
Returns NULL on parse/compile failure; caller must check for NULL.
The returned schema must be freed with xmlRelaxNGFree().
Do not reuse the parser context after critical failures unless reconfigured; typical usage is: create ctxt -> parse -> free ctxt.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGFree
functions.description: Frees a compiled Relax NG schema created by xmlRelaxNGParse().
requirements: schema may be NULL (common libxml2 pattern), in which case the function does nothing; otherwise it must be a schema returned by xmlRelaxNGParse().
After this call, schema must not be used again.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGDump
functions.description: Writes a human-readable dump of the compiled Relax NG schema to the given FILE stream. Useful for debugging. Only available when libxml2 is built with LIBXML_DEBUG_ENABLED.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_RELAXNG_ENABLED and LIBXML_DEBUG_ENABLED at build time.
output must be a valid FILE* opened for writing; passing NULL is undefined.
schema must be a valid compiled schema (may be NULL to print nothing in some libxml2 APIs, but this is unspecified here).

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGDumpTree
functions.description: Outputs the compiled Relax NG schema as a tree representation to the given FILE stream. Typically used for diagnostics. Only available when libxml2 is built with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_RELAXNG_ENABLED and LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED at build time.
output must be a valid FILE* opened for writing; passing NULL is undefined.
schema must be a valid compiled schema.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGSetValidErrors
functions.signature: void xmlRelaxNGSetValidErrors(xmlRelaxNGValidCtxt *ctxt, xmlRelaxNGValidityErrorFunc err, xmlRelaxNGValidityWarningFunc warn, void *ctx);
functions.description: Registers error and warning callbacks for validation diagnostics produced when validating XML documents against a Relax NG schema.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context.
err and/or warn may be NULL to disable those callbacks.
ctx is a user-supplied pointer returned to the callbacks and must remain valid while installed.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGGetValidErrors
functions.description: Retrieves the currently set error and warning callbacks and user context from a validation context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context.
err, warn, and ctx are output parameters; pass non-NULL pointers to receive values. Passing NULL skips that output.
Returns an int status; exact semantics are not specified here (typical libxml2 returns 0 on success).

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGSetValidStructuredErrors
functions.description: Registers a structured error callback (xmlError-based) for validation-time errors and warnings.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context.
serror may be NULL to disable structured error reporting; otherwise must be a valid xmlStructuredErrorFunc.
ctx must remain valid for the duration of the registration.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGNewValidCtxt
functions.description: Creates a new validation context for validating XML documents against the specified compiled Relax NG schema.
requirements: schema must be a valid schema returned by xmlRelaxNGParse().
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.
The returned context must be freed with xmlRelaxNGFreeValidCtxt().

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGFreeValidCtxt
functions.description: Frees a validation context previously created by xmlRelaxNGNewValidCtxt().
requirements: ctxt may be NULL (no-op in common libxml2 style); otherwise it must be a valid validation context.
After this call, ctxt must not be used again.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidateDoc
functions.description: Validates an XML document against the Relax NG schema associated with the validation context. Returns a status code indicating validity or errors.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context created for the target schema.
doc must be a valid xmlDoc to validate and must remain alive for the duration of the call.
Return convention typically used by libxml2: 0 means valid, >0 means the document is not valid, and <0 indicates an internal or API error; exact values may vary by version.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidatePushElement
functions.description: Begins validation of an element in a progressive (streaming) fashion, pushing the start of an element into the validator.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context.
doc must be the owning document of elem and must be valid.
elem must be a valid element node (xmlNode*) corresponding to the start element being validated.
Return code follows libxml2 conventions (0 success/valid so far, >0 invalid, <0 internal error), but exact values are not documented here.
Calls must be balanced with a corresponding xmlRelaxNGValidatePopElement() for the same element to complete validation.

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidatePushCData
functions.description: Feeds character data (text content) to the progressive validator between pushed elements.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context used for progressive validation.
data must point to a valid buffer of UTF-8 (xmlChar) text of length len, or may be NULL if len is 0 (unspecified here; safest to pass non-NULL when len>0).
len must be >= 0 and represent the number of bytes in data.
Return code follows libxml2 conventions (0 success, >0 invalid content, <0 internal error).

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidatePopElement
functions.description: Signals the end of an element during progressive validation, completing validation for that element.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context that previously received a matching xmlRelaxNGValidatePushElement() for elem.
doc must be the owning document of elem and valid.
elem must be the same element node previously pushed.
Return code follows libxml2 conventions (0 success, >0 invalid, <0 internal error).

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidateFullElement
functions.description: Validates a single element (including its content) in one call, when supported, without fully validating the entire document.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context.
doc must be a valid xmlDoc that owns elem.
elem must be a valid element node whose subtree will be checked.
Return code follows libxml2 conventions (0 valid, >0 not valid, <0 internal error).

functions.name: xmlRelaxNGValidCtxtClearErrors
functions.description: Clears any accumulated error and warning handlers or error state on a validation context, resetting diagnostic configuration to defaults.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid validation context pointer; passing NULL is unspecified.
Effects on previously set callbacks depend on libxml2 version; intent is to clear handlers/state for fresh validation runs.

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetPublicId
functions.description: Returns the current document's public identifier from a SAX2 parsing context. Typically used inside SAX callbacks to query the parser state.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer provided by the parser.
Returns NULL if no public identifier is available.

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetSystemId
functions.description: Returns the current document's system identifier (systemId) from a SAX2 parsing context. Useful to resolve external entities or base URIs.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer provided by the parser.
Returns NULL if no system identifier is available.

functions.name: xmlSAX2SetDocumentLocator
functions.description: Sets the SAX locator for the current parsing context so later callbacks can report positions (line/column, system/public IDs).
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
loc must be a valid pointer to an xmlSAXLocator structure initialized by the caller or parser.
May be called early during parsing before other callbacks rely on locator information.

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetLineNumber
functions.description: Returns the current input line number from a SAX2 parsing context, if available.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Return value may be 0 or negative if line information is unavailable (details unknown).

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetColumnNumber
functions.description: Returns the current input column number from a SAX2 parsing context, if available.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Return value may be 0 or negative if column information is unavailable (details unknown).

functions.name: xmlSAX2IsStandalone
functions.description: Reports whether the current document is declared standalone. Typically reflects the XML declaration's standalone flag.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Return value semantics beyond true/false are unknown; treat non-zero as true.

functions.name: xmlSAX2HasInternalSubset
functions.description: Reports whether the document has an internal subset (DTD) in the prolog.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Return value semantics beyond true/false are unknown; treat non-zero as true.

functions.name: xmlSAX2HasExternalSubset
functions.description: Reports whether the document has an external subset (external DTD).
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Return value semantics beyond true/false are unknown; treat non-zero as true.

functions.name: xmlSAX2InternalSubset
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2InternalSubset(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId);
functions.description: SAX2 callback indicating the presence of an internal subset in the document type declaration. Provides the root element name and optional identifiers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must point to a null-terminated xmlChar string naming the root element.
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
Caller should ensure strings remain valid for the duration of the callback.

functions.name: xmlSAX2ExternalSubset
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2ExternalSubset(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing the external subset for the document type, with the root element name and optional public/system identifiers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a null-terminated xmlChar string.
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetEntity
functions.description: Looks up a general entity by name in the current parsing context and returns its entity descriptor if known.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the entity.
Returns NULL if the entity is not declared or cannot be found.

functions.name: xmlSAX2GetParameterEntity
functions.description: Looks up a parameter entity by name in the current parsing context and returns its entity descriptor if known.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the parameter entity.
Returns NULL if the entity is not declared or cannot be found.

functions.name: xmlSAX2ResolveEntity
functions.description: Resolves an external entity given its public and/or system identifiers and returns an input stream object for the parser.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string; typically at least one of publicId or systemId should be provided (inferred).
Returns NULL if the entity cannot be resolved.

functions.name: xmlSAX2EntityDecl
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2EntityDecl(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, int type, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, xmlChar *content);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing an entity declaration. Provides the entity name, type, optional public/system IDs, and optional content for internal entities.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
type is an integer entity type code as defined by libxml2 (exact values not specified here).
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
content may be NULL or an xmlChar buffer containing the entity value for internal entities; must be valid for the duration of the callback.

functions.name: xmlSAX2AttributeDecl
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2AttributeDecl(void *ctx, const xmlChar *elem, const xmlChar *fullname, int type, int def, const xmlChar *defaultValue, xmlEnumeration *tree);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing an attribute declaration in the DTD. Provides element name, attribute name, type and defaulting information, and possible enumeration tree.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
elem must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the element.
fullname must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the attribute.
type is an integer attribute type code as defined by libxml2 (exact values not specified here).
def is an integer default declaration code (e.g., #IMPLIED/#REQUIRED/#FIXED semantics, exact values not specified).
defaultValue may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
tree may be NULL or a valid xmlEnumeration* describing allowed values for enumerated types.

functions.name: xmlSAX2ElementDecl
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2ElementDecl(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, int type, xmlElementContent *content);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing an element declaration in the DTD. Provides the element name, its content model type, and optional detailed content model tree.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the element.
type is an integer element content type code as defined by libxml2 (exact values not specified).
content may be NULL or a valid pointer to an xmlElementContent tree.

functions.name: xmlSAX2NotationDecl
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2NotationDecl(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing a notation declaration. Provides the notation name and optional public/system identifiers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.

functions.name: xmlSAX2UnparsedEntityDecl
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2UnparsedEntityDecl(void *ctx, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId, const xmlChar *notationName);
functions.description: SAX2 callback announcing an unparsed (external) entity declaration, including its notation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
publicId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
systemId may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
notationName must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.

functions.name: xmlSAX2StartDocument
functions.description: SAX2 callback indicating the start of the document. Typically used to initialize per-document state before further callbacks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Should be called once at the beginning of parsing for a document (by the parser).

functions.name: xmlSAX2EndDocument
functions.description: SAX2 callback indicating the end of the document. Typically used to finalize or clean up per-document state.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
Should be called once at the end of parsing for a document (by the parser).

functions.name: xmlSAX2StartElement
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2StartElement(void *ctx, const xmlChar *fullname, const xmlChar **atts);
functions.description: Deprecated SAX1-style start-element callback. Called with the element name and a NULL-terminated array of attribute name/value pairs.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
fullname must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
atts may be NULL or a NULL-terminated array of xmlChar* alternating name/value pairs (exact layout per libxml2 SAX1; details not fully specified here).
Avoid using in new code; prefer xmlSAX2StartElementNs.

functions.name: xmlSAX2EndElement
functions.description: Deprecated SAX1-style end-element callback. Called with the qualified element name.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
Avoid using in new code; prefer xmlSAX2EndElementNs.

functions.name: xmlSAX2StartElementNs
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2StartElementNs(void *ctx, const xmlChar *localname, const xmlChar *prefix, const xmlChar *URI, int nb_namespaces, const xmlChar **namespaces, int nb_attributes, int nb_defaulted, const xmlChar **attributes);
functions.description: SAX2 namespace-aware start-element callback. Provides local name, optional prefix and URI, namespace declarations, and attributes with defaulting info.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
localname must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
prefix may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
URI may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
nb_namespaces must be >= 0.
If nb_namespaces > 0, namespaces must point to an array large enough to hold the namespace data for all declared prefixes (exact pairing/layout not specified here).
nb_attributes must be >= 0.
nb_defaulted must be >= 0 and <= nb_attributes (inferred from naming; exact constraint values not specified).
If nb_attributes > 0, attributes must point to an array large enough to hold all attribute data for the element (exact layout not specified here).

functions.name: xmlSAX2EndElementNs
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2EndElementNs(void *ctx, const xmlChar *localname, const xmlChar *prefix, const xmlChar *URI);
functions.description: SAX2 namespace-aware end-element callback. Provides local name and the associated prefix and URI, if any.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
localname must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
prefix may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.
URI may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.

functions.name: xmlSAX2Reference
functions.description: SAX2 callback for entity references encountered in content. Provides the reference name.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string naming the entity reference.

functions.name: xmlSAX2Characters
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2Characters(void *ctx, const xmlChar *ch, int len);
functions.description: SAX2 callback for character data. Provides a buffer pointer and its length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
ch must point to a buffer of at least len bytes containing character data (not necessarily null-terminated).
len must be >= 0.

functions.name: xmlSAX2IgnorableWhitespace
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2IgnorableWhitespace(void *ctx, const xmlChar *ch, int len);
functions.description: SAX2 callback for ignorable whitespace in element content. Provides a buffer pointer and its length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
ch must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (not necessarily null-terminated).
len must be >= 0.

functions.name: xmlSAX2ProcessingInstruction
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2ProcessingInstruction(void *ctx, const xmlChar *target, const xmlChar *data);
functions.description: SAX2 callback for a processing instruction node. Provides the PI target and its data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
target must be a non-NULL, null-terminated xmlChar string.
data may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string.

functions.name: xmlSAX2Comment
functions.description: SAX2 callback for a comment node. Provides the comment text.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
value may be NULL or a null-terminated xmlChar string containing the comment text.

functions.name: xmlSAX2CDataBlock
functions.signature: void xmlSAX2CDataBlock(void *ctx, const xmlChar *value, int len);
functions.description: SAX2 callback for a CDATA section. Provides a pointer to the CDATA content and its length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid libxml2 SAX/parse context pointer.
value must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (not necessarily null-terminated).
len must be >= 0.

functions.name: xmlSAXDefaultVersion
functions.description: Deprecated function controlling or querying the default SAX version used by libxml when SAX1 support is enabled.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_SAX1_ENABLED.
version is an integer input; specific accepted values and return semantics are not specified here (unknown).
Do not use in new code; SAX2 APIs are preferred.

functions.name: xmlSAXVersion
functions.description: Initializes a SAX handler structure according to the requested SAX version. Used to set up callback function pointers appropriately.
requirements: hdlr must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlSAXHandler structure writable by the caller.
version is an integer specifying the desired SAX API version (specific values not specified here).
Return value is an integer status/result code (exact semantics not specified).

functions.name: xmlSAX2InitDefaultSAXHandler
functions.description: Initializes an xmlSAXHandler with the default SAX2 callbacks used for building a DOM tree. Optionally enables warnings.
requirements: hdlr must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlSAXHandler structure to be initialized.
warning is an integer flag; non-zero likely enables warnings (exact semantics not specified).
Must be called before using the handler with a parser.

functions.name: xmlSAX2InitHtmlDefaultSAXHandler
functions.description: Initializes an xmlSAXHandler with default SAX2 callbacks appropriate for HTML parsing.
requirements: hdlr must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlSAXHandler structure to be initialized.
Must be called before using the handler for HTML parsing.

functions.name: htmlDefaultSAXHandlerInit
functions.description: Deprecated initialization routine for the default HTML SAX handler.
requirements: No arguments.
Deprecated; prefer xmlSAX2InitHtmlDefaultSAXHandler.

functions.name: xmlDefaultSAXHandlerInit
functions.description: Deprecated initialization routine for the default XML SAX handler.
requirements: No arguments.
Deprecated; prefer xmlSAX2InitDefaultSAXHandler.

functions.name: xmlSchemaFreeType
functions.description: Deallocates and frees an xmlSchemaType and all resources owned by it. Intended for internal/libxml2 schema handling code to release a schema type when it is no longer needed. This header is marked as internal and not guaranteed to be API/ABI stable.
requirements: Call only when LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED is defined (function is present only under that build option).
Argument 'type' must be a valid pointer to an xmlSchemaType obtained/owned by libxml2; after this call, the object must not be used again.
Do not call this function more than once on the same xmlSchemaType instance (no double-free).
Do not pass pointers to memory not allocated/managed for an xmlSchemaType (e.g., stack or embedded structs).
Unknown whether NULL is accepted; callers should ensure 'type' is non-NULL unless documentation/source confirms NULL-safety.

functions.name: xmlSchemaFreeWildcard
functions.description: Deallocates and frees an xmlSchemaWildcard and any associated resources. Used by internal/libxml2 schema code to release wildcard components of schemas. This interface is internal and not guaranteed to be API/ABI stable.
requirements: Call only when LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED is defined (function is present only under that build option).
Argument 'wildcard' must be a valid pointer to an xmlSchemaWildcard owned by libxml2; after this call, the object must not be used again.
Do not call this function more than once on the same xmlSchemaWildcard instance (no double-free).
Do not pass pointers to memory not allocated/managed for an xmlSchemaWildcard.
Unknown whether NULL is accepted; callers should ensure 'wildcard' is non-NULL unless documentation/source confirms NULL-safety.

functions.name: xmlSchematronNewParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new Schematron parser context from a schema located at the given URL (file path, URI, etc.). Use this to prepare parsing/compiling a Schematron schema before validation. Returns a parser context to be passed to xmlSchematronParse and later freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt. Exact URL resolution/encoding rules follow libxml2 conventions; detailed behaviors are not documented here.
requirements: URL must reference a readable Schematron schema resource (e.g., file path or URI) understood by libxml2.
The returned context must be freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt when no longer needed.
Do not pass the returned context to functions other than those expecting xmlSchematronParserCtxt (e.g., xmlSchematronParse, xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt).
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect creation failures (reason unspecified).

functions.name: xmlSchematronNewMemParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new Schematron parser context from an in-memory buffer containing a Schematron schema. Use when the schema is already loaded in memory. Returns a parser context to be parsed with xmlSchematronParse and freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt.
requirements: buffer must point to a memory region containing the complete Schematron schema bytes.
size must be the number of bytes available at buffer and must be non-negative; the buffer must be at least size bytes long.
The memory pointed to by buffer must remain valid and unmodified for the lifetime of the parser context (until after parsing completes).
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation or initialization failure.
The returned context must be freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: xmlSchematronNewDocParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new Schematron parser context from an existing libxml2 xmlDoc representing a Schematron schema. Use when the schema has already been parsed into an xmlDoc tree. The resulting context can be passed to xmlSchematronParse and later freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt.
requirements: doc must be a valid, fully constructed xmlDoc* whose content is a Schematron schema.
The xmlDoc must remain alive (not freed) for at least the duration of parsing/compilation using the returned context.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect failures.
The returned context must be freed with xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt.

functions.name: xmlSchematronFreeParserCtxt
functions.description: Free a Schematron parser context previously created by one of the xmlSchematronNew*ParserCtxt functions. Releases resources associated with schema parsing/compilation.
requirements: ctxt must be a parser context previously returned by xmlSchematronNewParserCtxt, xmlSchematronNewMemParserCtxt, or xmlSchematronNewDocParserCtxt and not already freed.
Do not use ctxt after calling this function.

functions.name: xmlSchematronParse
functions.description: Parse/compile a Schematron schema using the given parser context, producing an xmlSchematron schema object suitable for validation. Returns a compiled schema object on success, or NULL on failure. The schema must later be freed with xmlSchematronFree.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, initialized xmlSchematronParserCtxt created by an xmlSchematronNew*ParserCtxt function and not yet freed.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to handle parse/compile failures.
On success, the returned xmlSchematron must be freed with xmlSchematronFree when no longer needed.

functions.name: xmlSchematronFree
functions.description: Free a compiled Schematron schema created by xmlSchematronParse, releasing all associated resources.
requirements: schema must be a schema object previously returned by xmlSchematronParse and not already freed.
Do not use schema after calling this function.

functions.name: xmlSchematronSetValidStructuredErrors
functions.description: Register a structured error callback to receive validation diagnostics emitted during Schematron validation. The callback conforms to libxml2's xmlStructuredErrorFunc and will be invoked with the provided user data pointer.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchematronValidCtxt created by xmlSchematronNewValidCtxt.
serror should be a valid function pointer compatible with xmlStructuredErrorFunc; passing NULL disables structured error reporting (behavior beyond disabling is not documented here).
ctx is an opaque user data pointer that will be passed back to the callback and may be NULL.
This function should be called before starting validation to ensure all messages are captured.

functions.name: xmlSchematronNewValidCtxt
functions.description: Create a new Schematron validation context for validating XML documents against a compiled schema. The options argument is a bitmask of xmlSchematronValidOptions controlling output/reporting behavior. The returned context is used with xmlSchematronValidateDoc and must be freed with xmlSchematronFreeValidCtxt.
requirements: schema must be a valid compiled schema returned by xmlSchematronParse and not yet freed.

options should be a bitwise OR of xmlSchematronValidOptions values (e.g., XML_SCHEMATRON_OUT_TEXT, XML_SCHEMATRON_OUT_XML). If unsure, pass 0 for defaults; exact effects of each flag follow libxml2 semantics.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation or initialization failure.
The returned context must be freed with xmlSchematronFreeValidCtxt.

functions.name: xmlSchematronFreeValidCtxt
functions.description: Free a Schematron validation context created by xmlSchematronNewValidCtxt, releasing associated resources and any configured callbacks or buffers.
requirements: ctxt must be a validation context previously returned by xmlSchematronNewValidCtxt and not already freed.
Do not use ctxt after calling this function.

functions.name: xmlSchematronValidateDoc
functions.description: Validate an XML document against a compiled Schematron schema using the provided validation context. Returns an int whose exact semantics are not documented here (commonly number of validation errors or a status code); callers should consult libxml2 documentation or treat negative values as errors and non-zero as validation failures if following typical patterns.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchematronValidCtxt created by xmlSchematronNewValidCtxt (configured as needed before calling).
instance must be a valid xmlDoc* representing the XML to validate and must remain alive for the duration of the call.
Caller must check the return value to determine validation success/failure and handle errors according to libxml2 conventions (exact mapping unknown here).

functions.name: xmlCheckThreadLocalStorage
functions.description: Checks that libxml2's thread-local storage (TLS) facilities are available/initialized for the current process/thread. Use to verify the runtime can support per-thread data before using other thread-sensitive APIs. Exact return-value semantics are not documented here; treat non-zero/specific codes as unknown.
requirements: May be called at any time; no arguments required.
Caller should inspect the returned int to determine TLS availability; exact value conventions are unknown from this header.
No side effects or initialization guarantees are documented here; do not assume it initializes threads.

functions.name: xmlNewMutex
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new non-recursive mutex object for mutual exclusion within libxml2-using code. Use the returned mutex with xmlMutexLock/xmlMutexUnlock and release with xmlFreeMutex.
requirements: Must be called before using the mutex in xmlMutexLock/xmlMutexUnlock.
Return value may be NULL on allocation failure (inferred from allocator pattern); callers should check for NULL before use.
The created mutex is non-recursive; locking it twice from the same thread will deadlock (inferred from the existence of xmlRMutex).

functions.name: xmlMutexLock
functions.description: Locks a non-recursive mutex previously created by xmlNewMutex. Blocks until the lock is acquired.
requirements: tok must be a non-NULL pointer returned by xmlNewMutex.
tok must not have been freed with xmlFreeMutex.
Must not be called recursively on the same mutex by the same thread (non-recursive).
Each successful lock must be paired with a corresponding xmlMutexUnlock on the same mutex.

functions.name: xmlMutexUnlock
functions.description: Unlocks a non-recursive mutex previously locked with xmlMutexLock.
requirements: tok must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid mutex created by xmlNewMutex.
tok must currently be locked by the calling thread before unlocking (typical mutex requirement; inferred).
Each unlock should correspond to a prior successful xmlMutexLock.
Do not call after the mutex has been freed.

functions.name: xmlFreeMutex
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a non-recursive mutex created by xmlNewMutex.
requirements: tok must be a pointer returned by xmlNewMutex for the same library instance.
All locks on tok should be released before freeing (inferred common requirement).
Do not use tok after this call (no lock/unlock, no double free).
Whether NULL is accepted is not stated; pass a non-NULL valid mutex pointer to be safe.

functions.name: xmlNewRMutex
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new reentrant (recursive) mutex object. The same thread may lock it multiple times; it must be unlocked the same number of times.
requirements: Return value may be NULL on allocation failure (inferred from allocator pattern); callers should check for NULL before use.
Use only with xmlRMutexLock/xmlRMutexUnlock and release with xmlFreeRMutex.

functions.name: xmlRMutexLock
functions.description: Locks a reentrant (recursive) mutex created by xmlNewRMutex. The calling thread may acquire the same lock multiple times; a matching number of unlocks is required to release it fully.
requirements: tok must be a non-NULL pointer returned by xmlNewRMutex.
tok must not have been freed with xmlFreeRMutex.
Each successful lock must later be balanced by an xmlRMutexUnlock on the same mutex by the same thread.

functions.name: xmlRMutexUnlock
functions.description: Unlocks a reentrant (recursive) mutex previously locked with xmlRMutexLock. For recursive acquisition, must be called as many times as it was locked by the calling thread to fully release.
requirements: tok must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid recursive mutex created by xmlNewRMutex.
tok must currently be locked by the calling thread before unlocking (inferred).
Balance each prior xmlRMutexLock with a corresponding xmlRMutexUnlock.
Do not call after the mutex has been freed.

functions.name: xmlFreeRMutex
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a recursive mutex created by xmlNewRMutex.
requirements: tok must be a pointer returned by xmlNewRMutex for the same library instance.
All locks on tok should be released before freeing (inferred).
Do not use tok after this call (no lock/unlock, no double free).
Whether NULL is accepted is not stated; pass a non-NULL valid mutex pointer to be safe.

functions.name: xmlInitThreads
functions.description: Deprecated. Initializes thread support for the library. Modern libxml2 typically initializes threads lazily or automatically; new code should not call this explicitly.
requirements: Deprecated API; avoid in new code.
If used, call at most once during process lifetime (typical init pattern; exact requirement unknown).
Do not rely on side effects beyond enabling thread support; specifics are not documented here.

functions.name: xmlLockLibrary
functions.description: Acquires a global library-wide lock protecting shared libxml2 state. Use to serialize access to libxml2 when integrating with non-standard threading environments or during sensitive global operations.
requirements: Must be paired with a corresponding xmlUnlockLibrary to avoid deadlocks.
Callers should avoid recursive locking unless the lock is known to be recursive (unknown here).
Use only to protect operations that need to be serialized across threads.

functions.name: xmlUnlockLibrary
functions.description: Releases the global library-wide lock previously acquired by xmlLockLibrary.
requirements: Must be called after a successful xmlLockLibrary call by the same thread to release the lock.
Calls must be balanced 1:1 with xmlLockLibrary invocations.
Do not call if the library lock is not held (avoids undefined behavior; inferred).

functions.name: xmlCleanupThreads
functions.description: Deprecated. Cleans up thread-related resources previously allocated by the library. New code typically should not call this explicitly; cleanup is handled automatically on process shutdown.
requirements: Deprecated API; avoid in new code.
If used with xmlInitThreads, call after thread usage is complete, and not while other threads may still be using libxml2 (inferred caution).
Do not call more than once if cleanup is final (exact rules unknown).

functions.name: __xmlRegisterNodeDefaultValue
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the global/default xmlRegisterNodeFunc callback location (used to get/set the default node registration callback). Typically used via the xmlRegisterNodeDefaultValue macro.
requirements: Available even if deprecated (guarded by XML_DEPRECATED in headers).
Returned pointer refers to a function-pointer variable; caller may read or assign it to install a callback of type: void (*)(xmlNode*).
Callback must be reentrant and handle any node type.

functions.name: __xmlDeregisterNodeDefaultValue
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the global/default xmlDeregisterNodeFunc callback location (used to get/set the default node deregistration callback). Typically used via the xmlDeregisterNodeDefaultValue macro.
requirements: Available even if deprecated (guarded by XML_DEPRECATED in headers).
Returned pointer refers to a function-pointer variable; caller may read or assign it to install a callback of type: void (*)(xmlNode*).
Callback must be reentrant and handle any node type.

functions.name: xmlValidateNCName
functions.description: Validates that the given string is a valid XML NCName. The space parameter influences whether whitespace is allowed/considered.
requirements: value must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Return value indicates validity (exact semantics not documented here).
space meaning is not documented in this header; usage details unknown.

functions.name: xmlValidateQName
functions.description: Validates that the given string is a valid XML QName.
requirements: value must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Return value indicates validity; exact convention unspecified here.
space parameter semantics are not described here; details unknown.

functions.name: xmlValidateName
functions.description: Validates that the given string is a valid XML Name.
requirements: value must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Return value indicates validity; exact convention unspecified here.
space parameter semantics not described; details unknown.

functions.name: xmlValidateNMToken
functions.description: Validates that the given string is a valid XML NMTOKEN.
requirements: value must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Return value indicates validity; exact convention unspecified here.
space parameter semantics not described; details unknown.

functions.name: xmlBuildQName
functions.signature: xmlChar *xmlBuildQName(const xmlChar *ncname, const xmlChar *prefix, xmlChar *memory, int len);
functions.description: Builds a QName from a prefix and local part (ncname). May use caller-provided buffer or allocate a new string.
requirements: ncname must be a valid UTF-8 NCName.
prefix may be NULL for no prefix.
If memory is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; on success, result may be placed there.
If memory is NULL or buffer insufficient, function may allocate and return a newly allocated string that must be freed by the caller with xmlFree (allocator consistent with libxml2).
len should be non-negative; exact behavior for negative is unspecified.

functions.name: xmlSplitQName2
functions.description: Splits a QName into prefix and local name, returning the local part and setting *prefix to a newly allocated prefix if present.
requirements: name must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
prefix must be a valid pointer to xmlChar* variable; on return, *prefix may point to newly allocated memory the caller must free with xmlFree.
Return value (local name) is newly allocated and must be freed by the caller with xmlFree.
If no prefix is present, *prefix may be set to NULL and local name is a copy of name.

functions.name: xmlSplitQName3
functions.description: Identifies the local part of a QName within the input string and returns a pointer into name for the local part; sets *len to the length of the prefix (or similar). No allocation.
requirements: name must be a pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
len must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output length.
Returned pointer is into the original name buffer; caller must not free it.
Exact meaning of *len (prefix length vs. other) is not documented here; details unknown.

functions.name: xmlCreateIntSubset
functions.signature: xmlDtd *xmlCreateIntSubset(xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId);
functions.description: Creates (and attaches to doc) the internal subset (DTD) with the given name/public/system identifiers.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer (may be NULL depending on libxml behavior; not specified here).
name may be NULL per XML rules for externalID-less internal subset; exact requirements not specified here.
Returned xmlDtd* should be freed with xmlFreeDtd when no longer attached/needed.

functions.name: xmlNewDtd
functions.signature: xmlDtd *xmlNewDtd(xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *publicId, const xmlChar *systemId);
functions.description: Creates a new DTD node (internal or external) and optionally associates it with a document.
requirements: doc may be NULL or an existing xmlDoc; association semantics not detailed here.
name/publicId/systemId follow XML DTD identification rules; details not specified here.
Caller must free with xmlFreeDtd if not owned by a document.

functions.name: xmlGetIntSubset
functions.description: Returns the internal subset (DTD) of the document if present.
requirements: doc must be a valid pointer to an xmlDoc.
Returned pointer is owned by the document; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlFreeDtd
functions.description: Frees an xmlDtd structure and its associated allocations.
requirements: cur must be either NULL or a pointer to a DTD previously created by libxml2 APIs.
Do not call on DTDs still attached to a live document (risk of double-free/corruption).

functions.name: xmlNewNs
functions.description: Declares a new namespace on the given element node with URI href and optional prefix.
requirements: node should be an element node where the ns decl will be attached; must be non-NULL.
href is the namespace URI (may be NULL for undeclaration in XML 1.1 contexts; not specified here).
prefix may be NULL to declare default namespace.
Returned xmlNs* is attached to node->nsDef; lifetime tied to node/document.

functions.name: xmlFreeNs
functions.description: Frees a single xmlNs structure.
requirements: cur must be an xmlNs not owned/linked by a live node (freeing attached ns may corrupt tree).
Only free namespaces that were created but not attached, or after detaching; specifics not detailed here.

functions.name: xmlFreeNsList
functions.description: Frees a list (chain) of xmlNs structures.
requirements: cur may be NULL or the head of a standalone namespace list not attached to nodes.
Do not free namespaces still referenced by elements.

functions.name: xmlNewDoc
functions.description: Creates a new, empty XML document with the given XML version string.
requirements: version may be NULL or a string like (xmlChar*)"1.0"; exact validation not specified here.
Caller owns the returned document and must free it with xmlFreeDoc.

functions.name: xmlFreeDoc
functions.description: Frees an xmlDoc and all nodes it contains.
requirements: cur may be NULL or a valid document pointer created by libxml2.
All pointers into the document become invalid after free.

functions.name: xmlNewDocProp
functions.description: Creates a new attribute node in the context of a document (not attached to any element).
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc.
name must be a valid attribute name (QName handling per libxml).
value may be NULL for empty value.
Caller must free with xmlFreeProp if not attached to a node.

functions.name: xmlNewProp
functions.description: Creates and attaches a new attribute to the given element node.
requirements: node must be a valid element xmlNode pointer.
name must be a valid attribute name.
value may be NULL for empty value.
Returned xmlAttr* is owned by the element; do not free directly unless detached.

functions.name: xmlNewNsProp
functions.signature: xmlAttr *xmlNewNsProp(xmlNode *node, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *value);
functions.description: Creates and attaches a new namespaced attribute to the element node.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
ns may be NULL to create an unqualified attribute; otherwise must point to a namespace in scope.
name/value as attribute name/value; value may be NULL.
Ownership is with the node post-creation.

functions.name: xmlNewNsPropEatName
functions.description: Like xmlNewNsProp but may take ownership of the mutable name buffer ("eat name").
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name must be a mutable buffer allocated with the same allocator as libxml2 expects; libxml may take ownership.
ns optional as in xmlNewNsProp.
Do not reuse/free name after call if ownership was taken.

functions.name: xmlFreePropList
functions.description: Frees a list (chain) of attribute nodes.
requirements: cur may be NULL or the head of a detached xmlAttr list.
Do not pass attributes still attached to an element.

functions.name: xmlFreeProp
functions.description: Frees a single attribute node and its children/value.
requirements: cur must be NULL or a detached xmlAttr pointer.
Do not free attributes still attached to a node.

functions.name: xmlCopyProp
functions.description: Copies an attribute (name/value/ns) to the target element and attaches it.
requirements: target must be a valid element node.
cur must be a valid attribute to copy from.
Returned attribute is attached to target; do not free directly.

functions.name: xmlCopyPropList
functions.description: Copies a list of attributes and attaches them to the target element.
requirements: target must be a valid element node.
cur may be NULL or a list head of attributes.
Returned list is attached to target.

functions.name: xmlCopyDtd
functions.description: Deep-copies a DTD structure.
requirements: dtd must be a valid pointer to an existing DTD.
Caller owns the returned DTD and must free it with xmlFreeDtd.

functions.name: xmlCopyDoc
functions.description: Creates a copy of a document. If recursive is nonzero, copies the full tree; otherwise a shallow copy of the document structure.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc.
Caller must free the new document with xmlFreeDoc.
recursive controls depth; exact nonzero/zero semantics inferred from name/signature.

functions.name: xmlNewDocNode
functions.signature: xmlNode *xmlNewDocNode(xmlDoc *doc, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Creates a new element node in the context of a document, with optional namespace and initial content.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc.
name must be a valid element name.
ns may be NULL.
content may be NULL; when non-NULL, content is copied/parsed into text children (exact rules not detailed here).
Returned node is detached; attach to a tree as needed.

functions.name: xmlNewDocNodeEatName
functions.description: Creates a new element node; may take ownership of the mutable name buffer.
requirements: doc must be valid; ns optional.
name must be a mutable buffer; libxml may take ownership — do not free/reuse on success.
content optional.

functions.name: xmlNewNode
functions.description: Creates a new element node with optional namespace; not yet attached to any doc.
requirements: name must be a valid element name.
ns may be NULL.
Caller must attach node to a document or free it with xmlFreeNode.

functions.name: xmlNewNodeEatName
functions.description: Creates a new element node and may take ownership of the name buffer.
requirements: name must be a mutable buffer; may be consumed by the function.
ns optional.
Returned node is detached; manage its lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: xmlNewChild
functions.signature: xmlNode *xmlNewChild(xmlNode *parent, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Creates a new child element under parent with optional namespace and content.
requirements: parent must be a valid element node already linked to a document (typical usage).
name must be a valid element name.
ns optional; content optional.
Returns attached child owned by parent.

functions.name: xmlNewDocText
functions.description: Creates a new text node in the context of a document.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer.
content may be NULL for empty text.
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewText
functions.description: Creates a new text node (no associated document yet).
requirements: content may be NULL for empty text.
Attach to a document later or free with xmlFreeNode.

functions.name: xmlNewDocPI
functions.description: Creates a new processing instruction node in the context of a document.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc.
name is the PI target; must be a valid Name.
content optional (may be NULL).
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewPI
functions.description: Creates a new processing instruction node (no associated doc yet).
requirements: name must be a valid Name; content optional.
Caller attaches or frees node.

functions.name: xmlNewDocTextLen
functions.description: Creates a new text node with at most len bytes from content, associated with doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
content may be NULL if len==0; otherwise must point to at least len bytes.
len should be >= 0; negative behavior unspecified.

functions.name: xmlNewTextLen
functions.description: Creates a new text node from up to len bytes of content (no doc associated).
requirements: content may be NULL if len==0.
len should be >= 0; negative behavior unspecified.

functions.name: xmlNewDocComment
functions.description: Creates a new comment node associated with doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
content optional.
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewComment
functions.description: Creates a new comment node (no doc associated).
requirements: content optional.
Caller must attach or free the node.

functions.name: xmlNewCDataBlock
functions.description: Creates a new CDATA section node with len bytes of content, in the context of doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
content must point to at least len bytes if len>0.
len should be >= 0; behavior otherwise unspecified.

functions.name: xmlNewCharRef
functions.description: Creates a new character reference node (e.g., &#x...;) associated with doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
name should identify the character (format specifics not documented here).
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewReference
functions.description: Creates a new entity reference node associated with doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
name must be the entity name declared in the document's DTD to resolve (not enforced here).
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlCopyNode
functions.description: Copies a node. If recursive is nonzero, copies its subtree; otherwise shallow copy.
requirements: node must be a valid xmlNode pointer.
Returned node is detached; caller must attach or free it.
recursive controls depth; exact semantics inferred.

functions.name: xmlDocCopyNode
functions.description: Copies a node for insertion into the specified document, optionally deep.
requirements: node must be valid; doc must be a valid destination document.
Returned node is detached and associated with doc.
recursive controls depth.

functions.name: xmlDocCopyNodeList
functions.description: Copies a full list (sibling chain) of nodes into the destination document.
requirements: doc must be valid; node may be NULL or head of a list.
Returned list is detached and associated with doc.

functions.name: xmlCopyNodeList
functions.description: Copies a list (sibling chain) of nodes, preserving their relative order.
requirements: node may be NULL or list head.
Returned list is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewTextChild
functions.signature: xmlNode *xmlNewTextChild(xmlNode *parent, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Creates a child element and, if content is provided, adds a text child to it.
requirements: parent must be a valid element node.
name valid; ns optional; content optional.
Returns the newly attached element node.

functions.name: xmlNewDocRawNode
functions.signature: xmlNode *xmlNewDocRawNode(xmlDoc *doc, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *content);
functions.description: Creates a new element node where content is added as raw text without encoding or entity substitution (per typical libxml behavior).
requirements: doc must be valid; ns optional; name valid.
content optional.
Returned node is detached.

functions.name: xmlNewDocFragment
functions.description: Creates a new document fragment node associated with doc.
requirements: doc must be valid.
Returned fragment is detached.

functions.name: xmlGetLineNo
functions.description: Returns the line number of the node in the source document if available, or a special value otherwise.
requirements: node must be a valid pointer.
Return semantics for unavailable line numbers follow libxml conventions (not described here).

functions.name: xmlGetNodePath
functions.description: Builds and returns an XPath-like string representing the node's absolute path.
requirements: node must be valid.
Return value is newly allocated; caller must free it with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlDocGetRootElement
functions.description: Returns the root element node of the document, or NULL if none.
requirements: doc must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the document; do not free.

functions.name: xmlGetLastChild
functions.description: Returns the last child node of the given parent, or NULL if none.
requirements: parent must be valid.
Returned node is owned by the document.

functions.name: xmlNodeIsText
functions.description: Tests whether the node is a text-like node (text/CDATA).
requirements: node must be valid.
Return is nonzero if text; zero otherwise.

functions.name: xmlIsBlankNode
functions.description: Tests whether the node is a blank (whitespace) text node.
requirements: node must be valid.
Return nonzero if blank node; zero otherwise.

functions.name: xmlDocSetRootElement
functions.description: Sets/replaces the root element of the document and returns the previous root if any.
requirements: doc must be valid.
root must be a valid element node (or possibly NULL to remove root; not specified).
Returned previous root, if any, remains owned by the document unless unlinked; details not specified.

functions.name: xmlNodeSetName
functions.description: Changes the name of a node.
requirements: cur must be valid; name must be a valid new name for the node type.
For namespaced elements, consider also ns handling; not detailed here.

functions.name: xmlAddChild
functions.description: Adds cur as the last child of parent; returns the inserted node (possibly merged).
requirements: parent and cur must be valid nodes; must belong to same document or be adapted by libxml.
cur should be detached before adding (libxml may unlink as needed).
Returned node is owned by the document.

functions.name: xmlAddChildList
functions.description: Adds a list (sibling chain) of nodes as children of parent.
requirements: parent valid; cur may be NULL or a detached list.
All nodes must be suitable for insertion into parent.

functions.name: xmlReplaceNode
functions.description: Replaces old node in the tree with cur and returns the replaced node (detached).
requirements: old must be a node in a tree; cur must be a detached node or in a compatible context.
Caller is responsible for freeing or reusing the returned old node.

functions.name: xmlAddPrevSibling
functions.description: Inserts elem as the previous sibling of cur; returns the inserted node (possibly merged).
requirements: cur must be attached in a tree; elem should be detached.
Both nodes must be in or compatible with the same document.

functions.name: xmlAddSibling
functions.description: Adds elem after cur in the sibling list; returns the inserted node (possibly merged).
requirements: cur must be attached; elem should be detached.
Document compatibility required.

functions.name: xmlAddNextSibling
functions.description: Inserts elem as the next sibling of cur; returns the inserted node (possibly merged).
requirements: cur must be attached; elem should be detached.
Document compatibility required.

functions.name: xmlUnlinkNode
functions.description: Detaches a node from its parent and siblings, leaving it orphaned but not freed.
requirements: cur must be attached to a tree to have effect.
After unlinking, caller is responsible for freeing or reusing the node.

functions.name: xmlTextMerge
functions.description: Merges two adjacent text nodes into one and frees/removes the second node; returns the merged node.
requirements: first and second must be text nodes and adjacent siblings within the same parent.
After success, second is invalid (consumed).

functions.name: xmlTextConcat
functions.signature: int xmlTextConcat(xmlNode *node, const xmlChar *content, int len);
functions.description: Appends up to len bytes of content to a text node.
requirements: node must be a text node.
content may be NULL if len==0.
len should be >= 0; behavior otherwise unspecified.
Return value indicates success/failure (details not given here).

functions.name: xmlFreeNodeList
functions.description: Frees a full sibling chain (list) of nodes, including all their descendants.
requirements: cur may be NULL or a list head.
Nodes must be detached or otherwise not double-freed.

functions.name: xmlFreeNode
functions.description: Frees a single node and its subtree if any.
requirements: cur may be NULL or a detached node.
Do not free nodes still linked to a live document unless explicitly intended.

functions.name: xmlSetTreeDoc
functions.description: Recursively sets the ->doc pointer for a node and all its descendants to doc.
requirements: tree must be non-NULL; doc may be NULL or a valid document.
Return value indicates success/failure (not specified).

functions.name: xmlSetListDoc
functions.description: Sets the ->doc pointer for each node in a sibling list to doc.
requirements: list may be NULL or list head; doc may be NULL or valid.
Return value indicates success/failure (not specified).

functions.name: xmlSearchNs
functions.description: Finds the nearest namespace declaration in scope for the given URI (or possibly for a prefix; based on name suggests URI).
requirements: doc and node must be valid pointers in the same tree.
nameSpace must be a UTF-8 string; exact meaning (URI vs prefix) inferred by function name (URI for ByHref is the other API).

functions.name: xmlSearchNsByHref
functions.description: Finds the nearest namespace declaration with the given href (namespace URI) in scope for node.
requirements: doc and node must be valid pointers in the same tree.
href must be a valid UTF-8 URI string.

functions.name: xmlGetNsListSafe
functions.signature: int xmlGetNsListSafe(const xmlDoc *doc, const xmlNode *node, xmlNs ***out);
functions.description: Safely retrieves the list of in-scope namespaces for node, storing an array of xmlNs* in *out.
requirements: doc and node must be valid pointers in the same tree.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlNs** array variable; on success, *out receives an allocated array which the caller must free with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlGetNsList
functions.description: Returns an array of in-scope namespaces for node (NULL-terminated).

functions.name: xmlSetNs

ns may be NULL or must be a namespace in scope or attached appropriately.

functions.name: xmlCopyNamespace

functions.name: xmlCopyNamespaceList
functions.description: Copies a list (chain) of namespace declaration nodes.
requirements: cur may be NULL or head of a namespace list.
Caller must free with xmlFreeNsList.

functions.name: xmlSetProp
functions.description: Sets (creates or updates) an attribute on node by local name.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name must be a valid attribute name; value may be NULL to clear or set empty (exact behavior not specified).

functions.name: xmlSetNsProp
functions.signature: xmlAttr *xmlSetNsProp(xmlNode *node, xmlNs *ns, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *value);
functions.description: Sets (creates or updates) a namespaced attribute on node.
requirements: node must be a valid element node; ns may be NULL for unqualified.
name/value as attribute name/value.
Returned attribute is attached to node.

functions.name: xmlNodeGetAttrValue
functions.signature: int xmlNodeGetAttrValue(const xmlNode *node, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *nsUri, xmlChar **out);
functions.description: Retrieves the value of an attribute by name and optional namespace URI into an output xmlChar* buffer.

nsUri may be NULL to search without namespace; otherwise must match attribute namespace URI.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to xmlChar*; on success, *out receives a newly allocated string to be freed with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlGetNoNsProp
functions.description: Gets the value of a non-namespaced attribute by name. Returns a newly allocated string or NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name must be a valid attribute name.
Return value must be freed with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlGetProp
functions.description: Gets the value of an attribute by name (namespace-agnostic). Returns a newly allocated string or NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name must be valid.
Caller must free the returned string with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlHasProp
functions.description: Checks for an attribute with the given name on node; returns the attribute if found.
requirements: node must be valid element node.
name valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the node; do not free.

functions.name: xmlHasNsProp
functions.signature: xmlAttr *xmlHasNsProp(const xmlNode *node, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *nameSpace);
functions.description: Checks for a namespaced attribute on node by local name and namespace URI.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name valid; nameSpace may be NULL or a URI string.
Returned pointer is owned by the node.

functions.name: xmlGetNsProp
functions.signature: xmlChar *xmlGetNsProp(const xmlNode *node, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *nameSpace);
functions.description: Gets the value of a namespaced attribute; returns a newly allocated string or NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid element node.
name valid; nameSpace is the namespace URI (may be NULL to search any).
Caller must free the returned string with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlStringGetNodeList
functions.description: Parses a string containing markup into a list of nodes as if parsed in the context of doc.
requirements: doc must be valid; value must be a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned list is detached and must be freed with xmlFreeNodeList if not attached.

functions.name: xmlStringLenGetNodeList
functions.signature: xmlNode *xmlStringLenGetNodeList(const xmlDoc *doc, const xmlChar *value, int len);
functions.description: Parses up to len bytes from value into a list of nodes in the context of doc.
requirements: doc must be valid; value must point to at least len bytes if len>0.
len should be >= 0.
Returned list must be managed by caller.

functions.name: xmlNodeListGetString
functions.description: Serializes a node list to a string using doc's context; inLine may affect whitespace/formatting.
requirements: doc must be valid; list may be NULL.
Returned string is allocated; caller must free with xmlFree.
inLine semantics not documented here; details unknown.

functions.name: xmlNodeListGetRawString
functions.signature: xmlChar *xmlNodeListGetRawString(const xmlDoc *doc, const xmlNode *list, int inLine);
functions.description: Serializes a node list to a raw string (less escaping/normalization); inLine may affect behavior.
requirements: doc must be valid; list may be NULL.
Returned string is allocated; caller must free with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlNodeSetContent
functions.description: Replaces the content of a node (text, element, etc.) with the given string.
requirements: cur must be valid; content may be NULL for empty.
Return value indicates success/failure (undocumented here).

functions.name: xmlNodeSetContentLen
functions.signature: int xmlNodeSetContentLen(xmlNode *cur, const xmlChar *content, int len);
functions.description: Sets content of a node from up to len bytes of content.
requirements: cur must be valid; content must point to at least len bytes if len>0.
len should be >= 0.
Return value indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlNodeAddContent
functions.description: Appends content to the existing content of node.
requirements: cur must be valid; content may be NULL for no-op.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlNodeAddContentLen
functions.signature: int xmlNodeAddContentLen(xmlNode *cur, const xmlChar *content, int len);
functions.description: Appends up to len bytes of content to a node.
requirements: cur must be valid; content must have at least len bytes if len>0.
len should be >= 0.

functions.name: xmlNodeGetContent
functions.description: Returns the string value (content) of the node (recursively for elements).
requirements: cur must be valid.
Returned string is allocated; caller must free with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlNodeBufGetContent
functions.description: Appends the node's content into the provided legacy xmlBuffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid xmlBuffer pointer.
cur must be valid.
Return value indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlBufGetNodeContent
functions.description: Appends the node's content into the provided xmlBuf (64-bit aware).
requirements: buf must be a valid xmlBuf pointer.
cur must be valid.
Return value indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlNodeGetLang
functions.description: Returns the in-scope xml:lang value for the node, if any.
requirements: cur must be valid.
Returned string is allocated; caller must free with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlNodeGetSpacePreserve
functions.description: Returns the xml:space handling for the node (e.g., default or preserve).
requirements: cur must be valid.
Return value encoding (e.g., 0/1) not specified here.

functions.name: xmlNodeSetLang
functions.description: Sets the xml:lang attribute for the node.
requirements: cur must be valid; lang may be NULL to remove.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlNodeSetSpacePreserve
functions.description: Sets the xml:space behavior for the node.
requirements: cur must be valid; val encodes the mode (e.g., 0/1) but specifics not detailed here.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlNodeGetBaseSafe
functions.signature: int xmlNodeGetBaseSafe(const xmlDoc *doc, const xmlNode *cur, xmlChar **baseOut);
functions.description: Safely retrieves the base URI in effect for node, writing it to *baseOut.
requirements: doc and cur must be valid pointers.
baseOut must be non-NULL; on success, *baseOut receives an allocated string the caller must free with xmlFree.
Return value indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlNodeGetBase
functions.description: Returns the base URI string in effect for node, or NULL.
requirements: doc and cur must be valid.
Return value must be freed with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlNodeSetBase
functions.description: Sets the base URI of the node.
requirements: cur must be valid; uri may be NULL to remove.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlRemoveProp
functions.description: Removes (unlinks and frees) an attribute from its owning element.
requirements: cur must be a valid attribute currently attached to an element.
After success, cur is freed and must not be used.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlUnsetNsProp
functions.description: Removes a namespaced attribute from node by local name and namespace.
requirements: node must be a valid element node; ns may be NULL for unqualified attribute.
name must be valid.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlUnsetProp
functions.description: Removes an attribute from node by name (not namespace-qualified).
requirements: node must be a valid element node; name valid.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented).

functions.name: xmlAttrSerializeTxtContent
functions.signature: void xmlAttrSerializeTxtContent(xmlBuffer *buf, xmlDoc *doc, xmlAttr *attr, const xmlChar *string);
functions.description: Serializes attribute text content into the provided output buffer, escaping as needed for XML serialization.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
buf must be valid legacy xmlBuffer; doc may be NULL or the owning doc; attr may be NULL to serialize raw string; string is the text to serialize.
Caller manages buf's lifetime.

functions.name: xmlReconciliateNs
functions.description: Reconciles namespace declarations within the subtree, fixing prefixes/URIs as needed to be consistent with doc.
requirements: doc must be a valid document; tree must be a subtree belonging to doc.
Return indicates success/failure (undocumented here).

functions.name: xmlDocDumpFormatMemory
functions.signature: void xmlDocDumpFormatMemory(xmlDoc *cur, xmlChar **mem, int *size, int format);
functions.description: Dumps a document to a memory buffer with optional formatting (pretty print).
requirements: LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED must be enabled at build time.
cur must be a valid document.
mem and size must be non-NULL pointers; on success, *mem points to allocated memory (xmlChar*) to be freed with xmlFree; *size receives byte length.
format nonzero enables formatting.

functions.name: xmlDocDumpMemory
functions.description: Dumps a document to a memory buffer without explicit formatting control.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
cur valid; mem and size non-NULL; *mem must be freed with xmlFree.

functions.name: xmlDocDumpMemoryEnc
functions.signature: void xmlDocDumpMemoryEnc(xmlDoc *out_doc, xmlChar **doc_txt_ptr, int *doc_txt_len, const char *txt_encoding);
functions.description: Dumps a document to a memory buffer using the specified character encoding.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
out_doc valid; doc_txt_ptr and doc_txt_len non-NULL; returned buffer must be freed with xmlFree.
txt_encoding must name a supported encoding (e.g., "UTF-8").

functions.name: xmlDocDumpFormatMemoryEnc
functions.signature: void xmlDocDumpFormatMemoryEnc(xmlDoc *out_doc, xmlChar **doc_txt_ptr, int *doc_txt_len, const char *txt_encoding, int format);
functions.description: Dumps a document to memory with specified encoding and optional pretty-print formatting.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
out_doc valid; doc_txt_ptr/doc_txt_len non-NULL; *doc_txt_ptr freed with xmlFree.
txt_encoding names an encoding; format nonzero enables formatting.

functions.name: xmlDocFormatDump
functions.description: Writes the document to a FILE* with optional pretty printing.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
f must be a valid writable C FILE*.
cur must be a valid document.
format nonzero enables formatting.
Return value is number of bytes written or a status (not specified here).

functions.name: xmlDocDump
functions.description: Writes the document to a FILE* without explicit formatting control.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
f writable; cur valid.
Return value semantics unspecified.

functions.name: xmlElemDump
functions.description: Dumps a subtree (element) to a FILE* using doc's context.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
f writable; doc valid; cur valid node (typically an element).

functions.name: xmlSaveFile
functions.description: Saves the document to a file path using default encoding and formatting.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
filename must be a valid path; cur valid.
Return value is bytes written or status (unspecified).

functions.name: xmlSaveFormatFile
functions.signature: int xmlSaveFormatFile(const char *filename, xmlDoc *cur, int format);
functions.description: Saves the document to file with optional pretty printing.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
filename path valid; cur valid; format nonzero for pretty print.

functions.name: xmlBufNodeDump
functions.signature: size_t xmlBufNodeDump(xmlBuf *buf, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *cur, int level, int format);
functions.description: Serializes a node into an xmlBuf with indentation level and optional formatting.
