buf must be a valid xmlBuf; doc valid; cur valid.
level >= 0 recommended; format nonzero enables formatting.
Returns number of bytes appended.

functions.name: xmlNodeDump
functions.signature: int xmlNodeDump(xmlBuffer *buf, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *cur, int level, int format);
functions.description: Serializes a node into a legacy xmlBuffer with indentation level and optional formatting.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
buf must be a valid legacy xmlBuffer; doc and cur valid.
level >= 0; format nonzero pretty prints.
Return value is number of bytes appended or status (unspecified).

functions.name: xmlSaveFileTo
functions.description: Saves the document to an existing libxml2 output buffer, optionally with a specific encoding.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
buf must be a valid, opened xmlOutputBuffer.
cur valid.
encoding may be NULL for default.
Return value semantics unspecified.

functions.name: xmlSaveFormatFileTo
functions.signature: int xmlSaveFormatFileTo(xmlOutputBuffer *buf, xmlDoc *cur, const char *encoding, int format);
functions.description: Saves the document to an xmlOutputBuffer with optional encoding and pretty printing.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
buf valid and open; cur valid; encoding optional; format nonzero pretty prints.

functions.name: xmlNodeDumpOutput
functions.signature: void xmlNodeDumpOutput(xmlOutputBuffer *buf, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *cur, int level, int format, const char *encoding);
functions.description: Serializes a node to an xmlOutputBuffer with optional indentation, formatting, and explicit encoding.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
buf valid and open for writing; doc and cur valid.
level >= 0; format nonzero enables pretty print; encoding may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlSaveFormatFileEnc
functions.signature: int xmlSaveFormatFileEnc(const char *filename, xmlDoc *cur, const char *encoding, int format);
functions.description: Saves the document to a file with the specified encoding and optional pretty printing.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
filename path valid; cur valid; encoding names a supported encoding; format nonzero pretty prints.

functions.name: xmlSaveFileEnc
functions.signature: int xmlSaveFileEnc(const char *filename, xmlDoc *cur, const char *encoding);
functions.description: Saves the document to a file using the specified encoding.
requirements: Output-enabled build required.
filename path valid; cur valid; encoding supported.

functions.name: xmlIsXHTML
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the given identifiers correspond to an XHTML DTD.
requirements: systemID and/or publicID may be NULL; valid UTF-8 strings when provided.
Return value semantics (which value means true) follow libxml conventions (nonzero true).

functions.name: xmlGetDocCompressMode
functions.description: Gets the compression mode set on a document (zlib level).

Return is an integer compression level (exact range not specified here).

functions.name: xmlSetDocCompressMode
functions.description: Sets the compression mode on a document for serialized output.
requirements: doc must be valid.
mode should be a valid zlib compression level (0-9); exact accepted range not specified here.

functions.name: xmlGetCompressMode
functions.description: Gets the global default compression mode for document saving. Deprecated.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer per-document settings.
Return semantics follow libxml (not specified here).

functions.name: xmlSetCompressMode
functions.description: Sets the global default compression mode for saving. Deprecated.
requirements: Deprecated API; may affect global state.
mode should be a valid zlib level (exact range not specified).

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapNewCtxt
functions.description: Creates a new DOM wrapper context used for advanced DOM operations (adopt/clone/reconcile).
requirements: Caller owns the returned context and must free it with xmlDOMWrapFreeCtxt.

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapFreeCtxt
functions.description: Frees a DOM wrapper context.
requirements: ctxt may be NULL or a context previously created by xmlDOMWrapNewCtxt.
Do not reuse after free.

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapReconcileNamespaces
functions.description: Reconciles namespaces on the given element subtree using the wrapper context; options control behavior.

elem must be a valid element node within a document.
options is a bitmask; exact flags not documented here.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapAdoptNode
functions.signature: int xmlDOMWrapAdoptNode(xmlDOMWrapCtxt *ctxt, xmlDoc *sourceDoc, xmlNode *node, xmlDoc *destDoc, xmlNode *destParent, int options);
functions.description: Adopts a node from sourceDoc into destDoc, optionally attaching under destParent, adjusting namespaces and document pointers.
requirements: ctxt may be NULL or valid.
sourceDoc and destDoc must be valid documents.
node must be a node from sourceDoc.
destParent may be NULL or a node in destDoc when attaching.
options bitmask controls behavior (undocumented here).
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapRemoveNode
functions.signature: int xmlDOMWrapRemoveNode(xmlDOMWrapCtxt *ctxt, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *node, int options);
functions.description: Removes a node from its document using wrapper semantics (cleanup, ns handling).
requirements: ctxt may be NULL or valid; doc must be valid and own node; node must be attached.
options bitmask controls behavior (undocumented).
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlDOMWrapCloneNode
functions.signature: int xmlDOMWrapCloneNode(xmlDOMWrapCtxt *ctxt, xmlDoc *sourceDoc, xmlNode *node, xmlNode **clonedNode, xmlDoc *destDoc, xmlNode *destParent, int deep, int options);
functions.description: Clones a node (optionally deep) from sourceDoc for use in destDoc; returns the clone in *clonedNode and may attach under destParent.
requirements: ctxt may be NULL or valid.
sourceDoc and destDoc must be valid.
node must be valid; clonedNode must be non-NULL and point to a variable to receive the clone.
deep controls deep clone if nonzero.
destParent may be NULL or a node in destDoc.
options is a bitmask; undocumented here.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlChildElementCount
functions.description: Returns the number of child element nodes under parent (DOM ElementTraversal-like).
requirements: parent must be a valid element node.
Return is a count; fits in unsigned long.

functions.name: xmlNextElementSibling
functions.description: Returns the next sibling which is an element node, or NULL if none.
requirements: node must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the document.

functions.name: xmlFirstElementChild
functions.description: Returns the first child that is an element node, or NULL.
requirements: parent must be valid.

functions.name: xmlLastElementChild
functions.description: Returns the last child that is an element node, or NULL.
requirements: parent must be valid.

functions.name: xmlPreviousElementSibling
functions.description: Returns the previous sibling which is an element node, or NULL.
requirements: node must be valid.

functions.name: xmlRegisterNodeDefault
functions.description: Sets the global default callback invoked when nodes are created; returns the previous callback. Deprecated.

Affects global state; thread-specific versions exist.
Deprecated; prefer newer mechanisms.

functions.name: xmlDeregisterNodeDefault
functions.description: Sets the global default callback invoked when nodes are destroyed; returns the previous callback. Deprecated.
requirements: func may be NULL or a function of type void (*)(xmlNode*).
Affects global state; thread-specific versions exist.
Deprecated.

functions.name: xmlThrDefRegisterNodeDefault
functions.description: Sets the thread-default node registration callback; returns previous. Deprecated.
requirements: func may be NULL or a function of type void (*)(xmlNode*).
Thread-local effect; Deprecated.

functions.name: xmlThrDefDeregisterNodeDefault
functions.description: Sets the thread-default node deregistration callback; returns previous. Deprecated.
requirements: func may be NULL or a function of type void (*)(xmlNode*).
Thread-local effect; Deprecated.

functions.name: xmlSetBufferAllocationScheme
functions.description: Sets the global allocation scheme used by legacy xmlBuffer objects. Deprecated.
requirements: Affects global behavior of xmlBuffer growth; deprecated in favor of newer xmlBuf.
scheme must be a valid xmlBufferAllocationScheme enum.

functions.name: xmlGetBufferAllocationScheme
functions.description: Gets the current global allocation scheme for legacy xmlBuffer. Deprecated.
requirements: Deprecated API. Returns one of xmlBufferAllocationScheme values.

functions.name: xmlBufferCreate
functions.description: Creates a new empty legacy xmlBuffer.
requirements: Caller owns the buffer and must free it with xmlBufferFree.

functions.name: xmlBufferCreateSize
functions.description: Creates a new legacy xmlBuffer with at least the given initial size.
requirements: Caller must free with xmlBufferFree.
size is initial capacity; may be adjusted by implementation.

functions.name: xmlBufferCreateStatic
functions.description: Creates a legacy xmlBuffer wrapper around user-provided static memory.
requirements: mem must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes that remains valid for the buffer's lifetime.
Caller must not free mem via xmlBufferFree; only free the xmlBuffer wrapper with xmlBufferFree.

functions.name: xmlBufferResize
functions.description: Resizes a legacy xmlBuffer to at least size bytes. Deprecated.
requirements: buf must be a valid xmlBuffer.
size is the requested size; behavior on shrink/expand depends on scheme.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferFree
functions.description: Frees a legacy xmlBuffer and any internally allocated memory unless it wraps static memory.
requirements: buf may be NULL or a valid xmlBuffer.
If created with xmlBufferCreateStatic, only the wrapper is freed; user manages underlying memory.

functions.name: xmlBufferDump
functions.description: Writes the contents of a legacy xmlBuffer to a FILE*.
requirements: file must be a valid writable FILE*; buf must be valid.
Return value semantics unspecified.

functions.name: xmlBufferAdd
functions.signature: int xmlBufferAdd(xmlBuffer *buf, const xmlChar *str, int len);
functions.description: Appends up to len bytes from str to the buffer.
requirements: buf must be valid; str must point to at least len bytes if len>=0.
len should be >= 0; special values (e.g., -1) behavior unspecified here.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferAddHead
functions.signature: int xmlBufferAddHead(xmlBuffer *buf, const xmlChar *str, int len);
functions.description: Prepends up to len bytes from str to the buffer.
requirements: buf valid; str must have at least len bytes if len>0.
len should be >= 0.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferCat
functions.description: Appends a null-terminated UTF-8 string to the buffer.
requirements: buf valid; str is a null-terminated UTF-8 string.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferCCat
functions.description: Appends a C string (char*) to the buffer, converting as needed.
requirements: buf valid; str is a null-terminated C string.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferShrink
functions.description: Truncates/removes len bytes from the beginning of the buffer. Deprecated.
requirements: buf valid; len is the number of bytes to remove.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferGrow
functions.description: Ensures the buffer can accommodate at least len additional bytes. Deprecated.
requirements: buf valid; len requested growth.
Return indicates success/failure.

functions.name: xmlBufferEmpty
functions.description: Resets the buffer length to zero without freeing the underlying storage.
requirements: buf must be valid.

functions.name: xmlBufferContent
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal content of the buffer (null-terminated).
requirements: buf must be valid.

functions.name: xmlBufferDetach
functions.description: Detaches and returns the internal content buffer, resetting the xmlBuffer. Caller becomes owner of the returned memory.
requirements: buf must be valid.
Returned pointer must be freed by caller with xmlFree.
After detach, buf is empty.

functions.name: xmlBufferSetAllocationScheme
functions.description: Sets the allocation/growth scheme for a specific legacy xmlBuffer.
requirements: buf must be valid; scheme must be a valid enum value.

functions.name: xmlBufferLength
functions.description: Returns the current length (in bytes) of the buffer content.
requirements: buf must be valid.

functions.name: xmlBufferWriteCHAR
functions.description: Appends a null-terminated xmlChar* string to the buffer (helper).
requirements: buf valid; string valid null-terminated.

functions.name: xmlBufferWriteChar
functions.description: Appends a null-terminated C string to the buffer (helper).
requirements: buf valid; string valid null-terminated.

functions.name: xmlBufferWriteQuotedString
functions.description: Writes a string into the buffer, quoting/escaping for XML attribute contexts.

functions.name: xmlBufContent
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal content of the xmlBuf (64-bit aware).

functions.name: xmlBufEnd
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the end (one past last byte) of the xmlBuf content.
requirements: buf must be valid.
Pointer is only valid while buffer is unchanged.

functions.name: xmlBufUse
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently used in the xmlBuf.
requirements: buf must be valid.

functions.name: xmlBufShrink
functions.description: Removes up to len bytes from the beginning of the xmlBuf and returns the amount removed.
requirements: buf must be valid; len is the number of bytes to remove.

functions.name: xmlCreateURI
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty parsed URI object (xmlURI). Use this to initialize a URI structure before filling fields or parsing into it. The returned object must be freed with xmlFreeURI.
requirements: Must be paired with xmlFreeURI to avoid memory leaks.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: xmlBuildURISafe
functions.signature: int xmlBuildURISafe(const xmlChar *URI, const xmlChar *base, xmlChar **out);
functions.description: Builds an absolute URI string from a possibly relative URI and a base URI, writing the result to *out. Safe variant returning a status code instead of the built string directly. Intended to resolve URI references per RFC 2396.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlChar*; on success, *out is set to a newly allocated string that the caller must free with the library's deallocator (e.g., xmlFree).
URI and/or base may be NULL depending on usage, but at least one must provide enough information to form a result; exact rules are unspecified here.
Return value is a status code; callers must check it before using *out (exact success/error values are not documented here).

functions.name: xmlBuildURI
functions.description: Builds and returns a new absolute URI string by resolving URI against base per RFC 2396. Convenience version returning the result directly.
requirements: On success returns a newly allocated xmlChar* which the caller must free with the library's deallocator (e.g., xmlFree).
May return NULL on error; callers must check for NULL.
Inputs should be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings; behavior with invalid encodings is unspecified.

functions.name: xmlBuildRelativeURISafe
functions.signature: int xmlBuildRelativeURISafe(const xmlChar *URI, const xmlChar *base, xmlChar **out);
functions.description: Computes a relative URI reference from URI with respect to base and writes it to *out. Safe variant returning a status code and using an output parameter.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlChar*; on success, *out points to a newly allocated string that the caller must free with the library's deallocator (e.g., xmlFree).
Return value is a status code; callers must verify success before using *out (exact codes are not documented here).
URI and base should be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings; exact handling of NULL inputs is unspecified.

functions.name: xmlBuildRelativeURI
functions.description: Computes and returns a newly allocated relative URI reference that, when resolved against base, yields URI. Convenience version returning the string directly.
requirements: Returns a newly allocated xmlChar* on success; caller must free it with the library's deallocator (e.g., xmlFree).
May return NULL on error; callers must check for NULL.
Inputs should be valid, null-terminated xmlChar strings.

functions.name: xmlParseURI
functions.description: Parses a URI string into a newly allocated xmlURI structure, splitting it into its components as per RFC 2396.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string representing a URI.

requirements: dtd must be a valid xmlDtd pointer
name must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlGetDtdQElementDesc
functions.signature: XMLPUBFUN xmlElement * xmlGetDtdQElementDesc(xmlDtd *dtd, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *prefix);
functions.description: Retrieves a qualified element declaration (with namespace prefix) by name from a DTD. Returns xmlElement or NULL.
requirements: dtd must be a valid xmlDtd pointer
name must be a non-NULL xmlChar string
prefix may be NULL or a namespace prefix string as used in the DTD

functions.name: xmlGetDtdElementDesc
functions.description: Retrieves an element declaration by name from a DTD. Returns xmlElement or NULL.
requirements: dtd must be a valid xmlDtd pointer
name must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlValidGetPotentialChildren
functions.signature: XMLPUBFUN int xmlValidGetPotentialChildren(xmlElementContent *ctree, const xmlChar **names, int *len, int max);
functions.description: Computes the set of element names that are permitted as children at some position in the provided content model tree. Fills names and length. Returns the number of entries or a status code. Available when LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED is defined.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
ctree must be a valid xmlElementContent tree
names must be a valid pointer to an array of xmlChar* with capacity at least max
len may be NULL or a valid pointer to an int to receive the number of names written
max must be >= 0 and indicates capacity of names array

functions.name: xmlValidGetValidElements
functions.signature: XMLPUBFUN int xmlValidGetValidElements(xmlNode *prev, xmlNode *next, const xmlChar **names, int max);
functions.description: Given a position between siblings (prev, next), computes element names that are valid to insert there according to the DTD. Returns the number of names written or a status code. Intended for tools like xmllint --insert.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
prev may be NULL or a valid xmlNode pointer
next may be NULL or a valid xmlNode pointer (typically the following sibling)
prev and next should belong to the same parent and document when both provided
names must point to an array of xmlChar* with capacity at least max
max must be >= 0

functions.name: xmlValidateNameValue
functions.description: Validates that a string conforms to the XML Name production. Returns non-zero if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
value must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlValidateNamesValue
functions.description: Validates that a string is a whitespace-separated list of XML Name tokens (Names). Returns non-zero if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
value must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlValidateNmtokenValue
functions.description: Validates that a string conforms to the XML Nmtoken production. Returns non-zero if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
value must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlValidateNmtokensValue
functions.description: Validates that a string is a whitespace-separated list of XML Nmtoken tokens. Returns non-zero if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED at build time
value must be a non-NULL xmlChar string

functions.name: xmlValidBuildContentModel
functions.description: Builds (or compiles) a content model (often into a regexp/automata) for an element declaration. Deprecated. Available when LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED and LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED are defined. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED and LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED at build time
ctxt must be a valid xmlValidCtxt
elem must be a valid xmlElement declaration node

functions.name: xmlValidatePushElement
functions.signature: XML_DEPRECATED XMLPUBFUN int xmlValidatePushElement(xmlValidCtxt *ctxt, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *elem, const xmlChar *qname);
functions.description: Incrementally validates by pushing an element start (like SAX startElement) into the validator. Deprecated. Available when LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED and LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED are defined. Returns non-zero if valid so far.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED and LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED at build time
ctxt must be a valid xmlValidCtxt
doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer
elem must be a valid element xmlNode in doc
qname must be the qualified name (non-NULL) of elem

functions.name: xmlValidatePushCData
functions.signature: XML_DEPRECATED XMLPUBFUN int xmlValidatePushCData(xmlValidCtxt *ctxt, const xmlChar *data, int len);
functions.description: Incrementally validates character data content during streaming validation. Deprecated. Available when LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED and LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED are defined. Returns non-zero if valid so far.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED and LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED at build time
ctxt must be a valid xmlValidCtxt
data must be a non-NULL pointer to character data
len must be >= 0 and represent the number of code units in data

functions.name: xmlValidatePopElement
functions.signature: XML_DEPRECATED XMLPUBFUN int xmlValidatePopElement(xmlValidCtxt *ctxt, xmlDoc *doc, xmlNode *elem, const xmlChar *qname);
functions.description: Completes the incremental validation of an element by popping it (like SAX endElement). Deprecated. Available when LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED and LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED are defined. Returns non-zero if the element/content was valid.
requirements: Requires LIBXML_VALID_ENABLED and LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED at build time
ctxt must be a valid xmlValidCtxt
doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer
elem must be a valid element xmlNode in doc
qname must be the qualified name (non-NULL) of elem previously pushed

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcess
functions.description: Process XInclude 1.0 directives for an entire parsed XML document. Walks the document and replaces xi:include elements with the referenced content. Typical usage: parse an xmlDoc with libxml2, then call this to resolve includes in place. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: doc must be a valid, fully parsed xmlDoc pointer created by libxml2 (not NULL).
The document should be in a consistent state (no ongoing parsing).
All included resources must be accessible to the default resource loader, or a custom loader must be installed separately.
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessFlags
functions.description: Like xmlXIncludeProcess, but passes parser options down to the internal parses used for included documents. Use this to control parsing behavior (e.g., validation, network access) of included resources via a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer (not NULL).
flags should be a bitwise OR of libxml2 xmlParserOption values that are meaningful for parsing included resources.
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessFlagsData
functions.description: Process XInclude for a whole document while supplying parser options and an opaque user data pointer associated with the processing. The data is typically passed to callbacks (e.g., error handler or resource loader) used during inclusion. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer (not NULL).
flags should be a bitwise OR of xmlParserOption values; unsupported bits are ignored or may cause errors, depending on libxml2 version.
data, if non-NULL, must remain valid for the entire duration of the call (until the function returns).
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessTreeFlagsData
functions.description: Process XInclude directives for a subtree rooted at the given node, supplying parser options and an opaque user data pointer. Only the specified subtree is processed and expanded in place. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: tree must be a valid xmlNode pointer (not NULL) that is attached to an xmlDoc (tree->doc must not be NULL).
flags should be a bitwise OR of xmlParserOption values for parsing included resources.
data, if non-NULL, must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessTree
functions.description: Process XInclude directives within the subtree rooted at the specified node. Expands xi:include elements under that node in place. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: tree must be a valid xmlNode pointer (not NULL) that is attached to an xmlDoc (tree->doc must not be NULL).
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessTreeFlags
functions.description: Like xmlXIncludeProcessTree, but passes parser options (xmlParserOption bitmask) for parsing included resources referenced within the subtree. Returns the number of substitutions made, or -1 on error.
requirements: tree must be a valid xmlNode pointer (not NULL) attached to an xmlDoc.
flags should be a bitwise OR of xmlParserOption values appropriate for parsing included resources.
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeNewContext
functions.description: Create a new XInclude processing context bound to a given document. Use this for incremental or customized processing across multiple nodes, with the ability to set flags, error handlers, and resource loaders on the context before processing. Returns a pointer to the new context, or NULL on error.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc pointer (not NULL).
The returned context must later be freed with xmlXIncludeFreeContext to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeSetFlags
functions.description: Set parser options on an existing XInclude context. The flags control how included resources are parsed (xmlParserOption bitmask). Returns 0 on success or a negative value on error (inferred).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlXIncludeCtxt pointer created by xmlXIncludeNewContext.
flags should be a bitwise OR of xmlParserOption values meaningful for parsing included resources.
The context must not be NULL; otherwise the call fails.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler
functions.description: Install a structured error handler for an XInclude context. Errors and warnings produced during inclusion are reported through the provided callback. The opaque data pointer is passed to the handler when invoked.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlXIncludeCtxt pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear a previously set handler; otherwise it must be a function compatible with xmlStructuredErrorFunc.
data must remain valid for as long as the context may invoke the handler (at least until processing completes or the handler is replaced/cleared).

functions.name: xmlXIncludeSetResourceLoader
functions.description: Install a custom resource loader for an XInclude context. The loader is used to fetch and open resources referenced by xi:include hrefs (and related attributes). The opaque data pointer is passed to the loader when invoked.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlXIncludeCtxt pointer.
loader may be NULL to restore default loading; otherwise it must match the xmlResourceLoader function type expected by libxml2.
data must remain valid for as long as the context may invoke the loader (at least until processing completes or the loader is replaced/cleared).
Custom loaders must honor the flags set on the context if the API requires it (inferred from typical libxml2 patterns).

functions.name: xmlXIncludeGetLastError
functions.description: Retrieve the last XInclude-related error code recorded on the given context. Useful after a processing call to check for the most recent error condition.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlXIncludeCtxt pointer.
Callers should not assume specific error code values beyond 0 meaning no error (inferred); consult libxml2 error codes for interpretation.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeFreeContext
functions.description: Free an XInclude processing context created by xmlXIncludeNewContext and release associated resources. After this call, the context pointer must not be used.
requirements: ctxt must either be NULL (no-op) or a context previously returned by xmlXIncludeNewContext.
The caller must ensure no concurrent processing is active on this context when freeing it.
After freeing, do not use the ctxt pointer again.

functions.name: xmlXIncludeProcessNode
functions.description: Process XInclude for a node or subtree using an existing context. This enables step-by-step or selective inclusion handling within a document. Returns the number of substitutions made for the given node/subtree, or -1 on error.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlXIncludeCtxt pointer configured as needed (flags, handlers, loader).
tree must be a valid xmlNode pointer attached to an xmlDoc that matches the context’s document.
Callers should check the return value: -1 indicates an error; non-negative values indicate how many inclusions were performed.

functions.name: xlinkGetDefaultDetect
functions.description: Returns the current default XLink node-detection callback. This callback is invoked by the link detection layer when links are detected. Deprecated module; avoid in new code.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED (header is guarded).
Function is deprecated; callers should avoid relying on it in new code.
No specific threading or lifetime guarantees are documented for the returned function pointer (unknown).

functions.name: xlinkSetDefaultDetect
functions.description: Sets the global default XLink node-detection callback used by the link detection layer to trigger default link-detection callbacks. Deprecated module; avoid in new code.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED (header is guarded).
Function is deprecated; callers should avoid relying on it in new code.
Argument func must be a valid function pointer of type xlinkNodeDetectFunc (takes void* ctx, xmlNode* node).
Whether NULL is permitted is not documented (unknown); pass a non-NULL pointer unless you know library-specific behavior.
If you want link recognition, callbacks must be provided before parsing (per header comment).
No documented ownership transfer; lifetime/visibility of the provided function pointer beyond the call is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: xlinkGetDefaultHandler
functions.description: Returns the current global XLink handler structure containing the set of link detection callbacks (simple, extended, extended-set). There is no built-in default; you must provide one to enable link recognition. Deprecated module; avoid in new code.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED (header is guarded).
Function is deprecated; callers should avoid relying on it in new code.
There is no default XLink callbacks; to activate link recognition, a handler must be provided before parsing (per header comment).
The ownership and mutability of the returned pointer are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: xlinkSetDefaultHandler
functions.description: Sets the global XLink handler structure used by the link detection layer. The structure contains callbacks for simple, extended, and extended-set links. Deprecated module; avoid in new code.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED (header is guarded).
Function is deprecated; callers should avoid relying on it in new code.
Argument handler must point to a valid xlinkHandler struct whose members (simple, extended, set) are function pointers matching the declared prototypes.
To enable link recognition during parsing, a handler must be provided before parsing (per header comment).
Whether NULL is permitted and whether the struct contents are copied or referenced is not documented (unknown); prefer supplying a non-NULL, long-lived struct.

functions.name: xlinkIsLink
functions.description: Determines whether the given node represents an XLink and returns its type (none, simple, extended, or extended set). The detection layer may expand QName prefixes in role values and resolve href URI-References using xml:base. Deprecated module; avoid in new code.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_XPTR_ENABLED (header is guarded).
Function is deprecated; callers should avoid relying on it in new code.
Argument doc should be a valid xmlDoc pointer (inferred).
Argument node should be a valid xmlNode pointer from the given document (inferred).
The function returns an xlinkType; callers should handle all enum values, including XLINK_TYPE_NONE.

functions.name: __xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilenameValue
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the global variable holding the current xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilename function (factory) used to create input buffers from URIs. Typically used internally or by advanced integrations to inspect or override the default handler.
requirements: May return NULL or a valid pointer to a function variable; callers must check the result before dereferencing.
Intended for advanced/low-level use; the returned pointer value is implementation detail and may be deprecated.

functions.name: __xmlOutputBufferCreateFilenameValue
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the global variable holding the current xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename function (factory) used to create output buffers for URIs. Useful for inspecting or overriding the default output handler.
requirements: May return NULL or a valid pointer to a function variable; callers must check the result before dereferencing.
Only available when LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED is compiled in; otherwise the symbol may be unavailable.

functions.name: xmlCleanupInputCallbacks
functions.description: Unregisters/cleans up all registered input callbacks and resets input I/O state. Use to free resources associated with custom input handlers.
requirements: Should be called when no parser is actively using registered input callbacks.
After calling, previously registered input handlers are no longer available; callers must re-register if needed.

functions.name: xmlPopInputCallbacks
functions.description: Unregisters the most recently registered set of input callbacks (LIFO). Returns an integer status (implementation-defined).
requirements: Safe to call only if at least one input callback set was previously registered.
Return value must be checked to detect failure.

functions.name: xmlRegisterDefaultInputCallbacks
functions.description: Registers libxml2’s built-in default input callbacks (e.g., file, HTTP where applicable). Call this to ensure standard input handlers are available.
requirements: May be called early during initialization before performing I/O.
If custom handlers rely on defaults as fallback, register defaults first or re-register after cleanup.

functions.name: xmlAllocParserInputBuffer
functions.description: Allocates a new parser input buffer configured for the given source encoding. Used as the input source for parsers.
requirements: enc must be a valid xmlCharEncoding value; if unknown, use XML_CHAR_ENCODING_NONE or equivalent.
Caller must free the returned buffer with xmlFreeParserInputBuffer when finished.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilename
functions.description: Creates a parser input buffer to read from a URI or filename using the specified source encoding. Performs lookup to select an appropriate input method based on the URI.
requirements: URI must point to a NUL-terminated string designating a filename or URI.
enc should specify desired source encoding; may be XML_CHAR_ENCODING_NONE to auto-detect.
Returns NULL if no suitable input method is found or on error; callers must check and handle.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateFile
functions.description: [Deprecated] Creates a parser input buffer from an existing stdio FILE* with the given source encoding.
requirements: file must be a valid, open FILE* positioned at the desired read point.
The FILE* remains owned by the caller unless otherwise documented; ensure lifetime covers reads.
enc must indicate the source encoding or auto-detect value.
Function may be removed in future; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateFd
functions.description: Creates a parser input buffer that reads from a POSIX file descriptor using the given source encoding.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor readable by the process.
The descriptor lifetime must outlive the buffer usage unless the implementation takes ownership (unspecified here); callers should verify ownership semantics in libxml2 docs.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateMem
functions.signature: xmlParserInputBuffer * xmlParserInputBufferCreateMem(const char *mem, int size, xmlCharEncoding enc);
functions.description: Creates a parser input buffer that reads from a copy of the provided memory block with known size and source encoding.
requirements: mem must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
size must be >= 0; size == 0 creates an empty input.
The memory can be released by the caller after creation (buffer copies content).
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateStatic
functions.signature: xmlParserInputBuffer * xmlParserInputBufferCreateStatic(const char *mem, int size, xmlCharEncoding enc);
functions.description: Creates a parser input buffer that reads from the provided memory block without copying (static view) using the given source encoding.
requirements: mem must point to at least size bytes of readable memory that remains valid and unmodified for the lifetime of the input buffer.
size must be >= 0.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateIO
functions.signature: xmlParserInputBuffer * xmlParserInputBufferCreateIO(xmlInputReadCallback ioread, xmlInputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, xmlCharEncoding enc);
functions.description: Creates a parser input buffer that reads via user-supplied I/O callbacks and context, with the given source encoding.
requirements: ioread must be a valid function implementing: int (void* context, char* buffer, int len) returning number of bytes read or -1 on error.
ioclose may be NULL or a valid function implementing: int (void* context) returning 0 or -1 on error.
ioctx is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks and must remain valid for the buffer lifetime.
enc must be a valid xmlCharEncoding value.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferRead
functions.description: [Deprecated] Reads up to len bytes into the input buffer from its underlying source. Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.
requirements: in must be a valid pointer to an input buffer.
len must be >= 0.
Callers must check the return value for -1 (error) and for 0 (EOF).

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferGrow
functions.description: [Deprecated] Ensures at least len bytes are available by reading more data into the input buffer. Returns number of bytes read/added or -1 on error.
requirements: in must be a valid pointer to an input buffer.
len must be >= 0.
Callers must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferPush
functions.description: [Deprecated] Pushes len bytes from buf into the input buffer (used for externally provided data). Returns number of bytes pushed or -1 on error.
requirements: in must be a valid pointer to an input buffer.
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlFreeParserInputBuffer
functions.description: Frees a parser input buffer and any associated resources.
requirements: in may be NULL (no effect) or a valid buffer previously allocated/created by libxml2 input buffer APIs.
After this call, the buffer pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: xmlParserGetDirectory
functions.description: Returns the directory portion of the given filename path as a newly allocated string. Useful for resolving relative references.
requirements: filename must be a NUL-terminated string path or URI; behavior for NULL is unspecified here.
Caller owns the returned string and must free it with the appropriate deallocator (xmlFree or free as per libxml2 conventions).
May return NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlRegisterInputCallbacks
functions.signature: int xmlRegisterInputCallbacks(xmlInputMatchCallback matchFunc, xmlInputOpenCallback openFunc, xmlInputReadCallback readFunc, xmlInputCloseCallback closeFunc);
functions.description: Registers a custom set of input callbacks (match, open, read, close) to handle specific URI/filename schemes for parser input.
requirements: matchFunc must implement: int (const char* filename) returning 1 if the handler can handle the resource, 0 otherwise.
openFunc must implement: void* (const char* filename) returning a context or NULL on error.
readFunc must implement: int (void* context, char* buffer, int len) returning bytes read or -1 on error.
closeFunc must implement: int (void* context) returning 0 on success or -1 on error.
All function pointers must be non-NULL.
Return value must be checked to confirm successful registration.

functions.name: __xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilename
functions.description: Internal variant that creates a parser input buffer for a URI using the built-in lookup. Exposed but intended for internal use.
requirements: URI must be a NUL-terminated string.
enc specifies encoding or auto-detect value.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlCleanupOutputCallbacks
functions.description: Unregisters/cleans up all registered output callbacks and resets output I/O state.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
Should be called when no output buffers are in use that depend on registered callbacks.

functions.name: xmlPopOutputCallbacks
functions.description: Unregisters the most recently registered set of output callbacks (LIFO). Returns an integer status.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
Safe to call only if at least one output callback set was registered.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: xmlRegisterDefaultOutputCallbacks
functions.description: Registers libxml2’s built-in default output callbacks (e.g., file). Ensures standard output handlers are available.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
Call early before creating output buffers that rely on defaults.

functions.name: xmlAllocOutputBuffer
functions.description: Allocates a new output buffer, optionally configured with a character encoding handler to convert to the target encoding.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
encoder may be NULL (no conversion) or a valid xmlCharEncodingHandler* matching the desired target encoding.
Caller must free the buffer with xmlOutputBufferClose when finished.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename
functions.signature: xmlOutputBuffer * xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename(const char *URI, xmlCharEncodingHandler *encoder, int compression);
functions.description: Creates an output buffer writing to the specified URI or filename with optional character encoding conversion and compression.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
URI must be a NUL-terminated string identifying the target.
encoder may be NULL or a valid encoding handler for the desired output encoding.
compression is a level value; valid range is implementation-defined; non-negative integers are expected.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateFile
functions.description: Creates an output buffer that writes to an existing stdio FILE* with optional encoding conversion.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
file must be a valid, open FILE* writable at the current position.
Ownership of FILE* is unspecified here; callers should consult libxml2 docs before closing it externally.
encoder may be NULL or a valid handler.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateBuffer
functions.description: Creates an output buffer that appends to an existing xmlBuffer with optional encoding conversion.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
buffer must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer* that remains valid for the lifetime of the output buffer.
encoder may be NULL or a valid handler.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateFd
functions.description: Creates an output buffer that writes to a POSIX file descriptor with optional encoding conversion.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
fd must be a valid, open, writable file descriptor.
encoder may be NULL or a valid handler.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateIO
functions.signature: xmlOutputBuffer * xmlOutputBufferCreateIO(xmlOutputWriteCallback iowrite, xmlOutputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, xmlCharEncodingHandler *encoder);
functions.description: Creates an output buffer that writes via user-supplied I/O callbacks and context with optional encoding conversion.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
iowrite must implement: int (void* context, const char* buffer, int len) returning bytes written or -1 on error.
ioclose may be NULL or implement: int (void* context) returning 0 or -1 on error.
ioctx must remain valid for the lifetime of the output buffer.
encoder may be NULL or a valid handler.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferGetContent
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current content (in output encoding or UTF-8 per handler) accumulated in the output buffer without modifying it.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.
Returned pointer remains valid until the buffer is modified or closed; do not free it.
May return NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferGetSize
functions.description: Returns the current size in bytes of the accumulated content in the output buffer.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferWrite
functions.signature: int xmlOutputBufferWrite(xmlOutputBuffer *out, int len, const char *buf);
functions.description: Writes len bytes from buf to the output buffer. Returns number of bytes written or -1 on error.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.
buf must point to at least len bytes if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
Callers must check the return value for errors/short writes.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferWriteString
functions.description: Writes a NUL-terminated C string to the output buffer. Returns number of bytes written or -1 on error.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.
str must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferWriteEscape
functions.description: Writes the given UTF-8 string to the output buffer using the provided escaping function for special characters. Returns number of bytes written or -1 on error.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.
str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated xmlChar string, typically UTF-8.
escaping must be a valid function of type xmlCharEncodingOutputFunc appropriate for the target encoding/escaping rules.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferFlush
functions.description: Flushes buffered output, pushing any pending data to the underlying sink. Returns 0 on success or -1 on error.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer.
Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferClose
functions.description: Flushes and closes the output buffer, releasing associated resources and underlying I/O as appropriate. Returns 0 on success or -1 on error.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
out must be a valid output buffer; after this call it must not be used again.
Callers must check the return value.
May close the underlying I/O resource depending on how the buffer was created.

functions.name: xmlRegisterOutputCallbacks
functions.signature: int xmlRegisterOutputCallbacks(xmlOutputMatchCallback matchFunc, xmlOutputOpenCallback openFunc, xmlOutputWriteCallback writeFunc, xmlOutputCloseCallback closeFunc);
functions.description: Registers a custom set of output callbacks (match, open, write, close) to handle specific URI/filename schemes for output.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
matchFunc must implement: int (const char* filename) returning 1 if this handler applies, 0 otherwise.
openFunc must implement: void* (const char* filename) returning a context or NULL on error.
writeFunc must implement: int (void* context, const char* buffer, int len) returning bytes written or -1 on error.
closeFunc must implement: int (void* context) returning 0 or -1 on error.
All function pointers must be non-NULL.
Callers must check the return value for success.

functions.name: __xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename
functions.description: Internal variant that creates an output buffer for a URI using the built-in lookup, with optional encoding and compression.
requirements: Only available when compiled with LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED.
URI must be a NUL-terminated string.
encoder may be NULL or a valid handler.
compression should be a non-negative compression level (implementation-defined).
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlCheckHTTPInput
functions.description: [Deprecated] Validates or adjusts an HTTP input for the given parser context and returns a possibly updated xmlParserInput. Historically related to handling HTTP resources.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context.
ret must be a valid parser input (may be modified/validated).
Returns NULL on error; callers must check.
Deprecated; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlNoNetExternalEntityLoader
functions.signature: xmlParserInput * xmlNoNetExternalEntityLoader(const char *URL, const char *ID, xmlParserCtxt *ctxt);
functions.description: [Deprecated] An external entity loader that refuses network access. Provided as a loader callback to disable network retrieval of external entities.
requirements: URL and ID are optional NUL-terminated strings describing the external entity.
ctxt must be a valid parser context when provided.
Returns NULL when network access is required or on error; callers must check.
Deprecated; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlNormalizeWindowsPath
functions.description: [Deprecated] Normalizes a Windows file path string (e.g., converting separators). Returns a newly allocated normalized string.
requirements: path must be a NUL-terminated xmlChar string.
Caller must free the returned string with the appropriate deallocator.
May return NULL on error; callers must check.

functions.name: xmlCheckFilename
functions.description: [Deprecated] Performs a basic validation/check on a filename or path. Exact checks are unspecified here. Returns non-zero if acceptable, 0 otherwise.
requirements: path must be a NUL-terminated string.
Callers must check the return value to decide validity.

functions.name: xmlFileMatch
functions.description: [Deprecated] Input I/O callback: match function for filesystem paths. Returns 1 if the file scheme is supported, 0 otherwise.
requirements: filename must be a NUL-terminated string.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: xmlFileOpen
functions.description: [Deprecated] Input I/O callback: opens a file and returns an opaque context, or NULL on error.
requirements: filename must be a NUL-terminated string naming a readable file.
Caller must check for NULL on failure.
Context must later be passed to xmlFileRead and xmlFileClose only.

functions.name: xmlFileRead
functions.signature: int xmlFileRead(void * context, char * buffer, int len);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Input I/O callback: reads up to len bytes from the file context into buffer. Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.
requirements: context must be a valid context returned by xmlFileOpen.
buffer must point to at least len bytes of writable memory if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
Caller must check the return value for errors/EOF.

functions.name: xmlFileClose
functions.description: [Deprecated] Input I/O callback: closes the file context. Returns 0 on success or -1 on error.
requirements: context must be a valid context returned by xmlFileOpen and not already closed.
Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlIOHTTPMatch
functions.description: [Deprecated] HTTP I/O callback: match function for HTTP/HTTPS URIs. Returns 1 if this handler applies, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Available only when LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED is compiled in.
filename must be a NUL-terminated string.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: xmlIOHTTPOpen
functions.description: [Deprecated] HTTP I/O callback: opens an HTTP/HTTPS resource and returns an opaque input context, or NULL on error.
requirements: Available only when LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED is compiled in.
filename must be a NUL-terminated URI string.
Caller must check for NULL on error.
Context must later be passed to xmlIOHTTPRead and xmlIOHTTPClose only.

functions.name: xmlRegisterHTTPPostCallbacks
functions.description: [Deprecated] Registers default HTTP POST-related callbacks for output. Enables posting via HTTP when output is enabled.
requirements: Available only when both LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED and LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED are compiled in.
Call before using HTTP POST output features.

functions.name: xmlIOHTTPOpenW
functions.signature: void * xmlIOHTTPOpenW(const char * post_uri, int compression);
functions.description: [Deprecated] HTTP I/O callback: opens an HTTP POST output context to post_uri with the given compression level. Returns an opaque context, or NULL on error.
requirements: Available only when both LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED and LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED are compiled in.
post_uri must be a NUL-terminated URI string.
compression is a level value (implementation-defined, non-negative expected).
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: xmlIOHTTPRead
functions.signature: int xmlIOHTTPRead(void * context, char * buffer, int len);
functions.description: [Deprecated] HTTP I/O callback: reads up to len bytes from an HTTP context into buffer. Returns number of bytes read or -1 on error.
requirements: Available only when LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED is compiled in.
context must be a valid HTTP input context returned by xmlIOHTTPOpen.
buffer must point to at least len bytes if len > 0.
len must be >= 0.
Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlIOHTTPClose
functions.description: [Deprecated] HTTP I/O callback: closes an HTTP input/output context. Returns 0 on success or -1 on error.
requirements: Available only when LIBXML_HTTP_STUBS_ENABLED is compiled in.
context must be a valid context previously opened by HTTP I/O open functions and not already closed.
Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilenameDefault
functions.description: Sets the default factory function used to create parser input buffers from URIs, returning the previous factory. Allows overriding the global behavior.
requirements: func may be NULL or a valid function pointer of type xmlParserInputBufferCreateFilenameFunc.
Returns the previous default function; callers may store it to restore later.

functions.name: xmlOutputBufferCreateFilenameDefault
functions.description: Sets the default factory function used to create output buffers for URIs, returning the previous factory.
requirements: Only available when LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED is compiled in.
func may be NULL or a valid function pointer of type xmlOutputBufferCreateFilenameFunc.
Returns the previous default function; callers may store it to restore later.

functions.name: xmlThrDefOutputBufferCreateFilenameDefault
functions.description: [Deprecated] Thread-default variant to set the output-buffer-from-filename factory function for the current thread, returning the previous value.
requirements: Only available when LIBXML_OUTPUT_ENABLED is compiled in.
func may be NULL or a valid function pointer.
Deprecated; behavior may differ across libxml2 versions; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlThrDefParserInputBufferCreateFilenameDefault
functions.description: [Deprecated] Thread-default variant to set the input-buffer-from-filename factory function for the current thread, returning the previous value.
requirements: func may be NULL or a valid function pointer.
Deprecated; avoid in new code; consult libxml2 docs for thread-safety notes.

functions.name: xmlNewAutomata
functions.description: Creates a new (deprecated/internal) libxml2 automaton builder object used to construct a regular-expression automaton before compilation. Intended for internal use; applications should prefer higher-level regexp APIs.
requirements: Library must be built with LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED for this function to be available.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation or initialization failure).
Object must later be released with xmlFreeAutomata to avoid leaks.

functions.name: xmlFreeAutomata
functions.description: Frees an automaton builder object and all resources it owns. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a pointer previously returned by xmlNewAutomata, not already freed.
am may be NULL (behavior unknown from header); if non-NULL it must be valid.
After this call, all xmlAutomataStatePtr obtained from this automaton become invalid.

functions.name: xmlAutomataGetInitState
functions.description: Returns the initial state object of the given automaton builder. Used as a starting point when wiring transitions between states. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid, initialized xmlAutomata* created by xmlNewAutomata.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (e.g., on error or uninitialized automaton).
Returned state must be used only with the same xmlAutomata instance.

functions.name: xmlAutomataSetFinalState
functions.description: Marks the specified state as a final (accepting) state in the automaton. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid xmlAutomata* created by xmlNewAutomata.
state must be a state created from the same automaton (ownership/association must match).
Caller must check the integer return status to detect failure (exact success/failure convention not documented; treat non-success as error).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewState
functions.description: Creates and returns a new state within the given automaton builder. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid xmlAutomata* created by xmlNewAutomata.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure).
The created state is owned by the automaton and must only be used with the same automaton.

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewTransition
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewTransition(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a transition labeled by a single token from state 'from' to state 'to'. Returns the (possibly new) destination state that represents the result of adding this transition. The data pointer can attach opaque user data to the transition. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid xmlAutomata* created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be non-NULL states that belong to the same 'am'.
token must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlChar string representing the transition symbol; exact encoding/allowed values are unspecified here.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer; its lifetime/ownership is not described here.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect failure.

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewTransition2
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewTransition2(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, const xmlChar *token2, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a transition that matches a pair/range/class of two tokens (details not documented) from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be states from the same automaton.
token and token2 must be non-NULL xmlChar strings; precise semantics are not documented here.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewNegTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewNegTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, const xmlChar *token2, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a negated transition (i.e., matches anything except the specified token(s)) from 'from' to 'to'. Exact matching semantics are not documented here. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states belonging to 'am'.
token and token2 must be non-NULL if provided by the intended pattern; exact meaning is unspecified.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewCountTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewCountTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, int min, int max, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a counted transition on a single token with occurrence bounds [min,max] from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid xmlAutomata*.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
token must be a non-NULL xmlChar string.

min and max are integer bounds; exact allowed ranges and conventions (e.g., unbounded) are not documented here—callers should ensure sensible non-negative bounds where min <= max unless library docs specify otherwise.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewCountTrans2
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewCountTrans2(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, const xmlChar *token2, int min, int max, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a counted transition parameterized by two tokens with occurrence bounds [min,max] from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be states belonging to the same automaton.
token and token2 must be non-NULL xmlChar strings.
min and max are integer bounds; exact constraints are not documented—ensure sane values (e.g., min <= max) unless library docs state otherwise.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewOnceTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewOnceTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, int min, int max, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a transition that matches a token a limited number of times ("once" semantics with bounds [min,max]); exact semantics relative to counted transitions are not documented. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
token must be a non-NULL xmlChar string.
min and max are integer bounds; precise rules are not documented—ensure consistent values (e.g., min <= max) unless otherwise specified.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewOnceTrans2
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewOnceTrans2(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, const xmlChar *token, const xmlChar *token2, int min, int max, void *data);
functions.description: Adds a two-token variant of a bounded "once" transition from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states belonging to 'am'.
token and token2 must be non-NULL xmlChar strings.
min and max are integer bounds; exact constraints unknown—use sensible values unless library docs specify otherwise.
data may be NULL or a valid opaque pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewAllTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewAllTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, int lax);
functions.description: Adds a transition that matches all tokens ("any" transition), optionally in a lax mode depending on the 'lax' flag. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
lax is an integer flag; treat 0 as false and non-zero as true.
Caller must check for NULL return (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewEpsilon
functions.description: Adds an epsilon (empty) transition from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewCountedTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewCountedTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, int counter);
functions.description: Adds a transition controlled by an existing counter identified by 'counter' from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
counter must be an identifier previously returned by xmlAutomataNewCounter for this same automaton.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewCounterTrans
functions.signature: xmlAutomataState * xmlAutomataNewCounterTrans(xmlAutomata *am, xmlAutomataState *from, xmlAutomataState *to, int counter);
functions.description: Adds a transition that updates or is gated by the counter identified by 'counter' from 'from' to 'to'. Returns the resulting state. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
from and to must be valid states from the same automaton.
counter must be a valid counter id obtained via xmlAutomataNewCounter on the same automaton.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (failure).

functions.name: xmlAutomataNewCounter
functions.signature: int xmlAutomataNewCounter(xmlAutomata *am, int min, int max);
functions.description: Creates a new counter with bounds [min,max] in the automaton and returns its identifier for use with the counter-based transition APIs. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be valid and created by xmlNewAutomata.
min and max are integer bounds; exact rules are not documented here—use sensible values (e.g., non-negative and min <= max) unless library docs state otherwise.
Caller must check the returned int for an error indicator (exact convention unspecified).

functions.name: xmlAutomataCompile
functions.description: Compiles the built automaton description into a libxml2 regular expression object (xmlRegexp). After compilation, the automaton builder is typically no longer modified. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid automaton that has been constructed and is in a compilable state (e.g., has an initial state; may have final states).
Caller must check the return value for NULL (compilation failure).
The returned struct _xmlRegexp* must be freed using the appropriate libxml2 regexp free function (not specified here).
After successful compilation, modifying 'am' further may be unsupported; consult library docs.

functions.name: xmlAutomataIsDeterminist
functions.description: Checks whether the described automaton is deterministic. Returns a boolean-like int. Deprecated/internal.
requirements: am must be a valid xmlAutomata* created by xmlNewAutomata.
Caller must check the integer result; exact true/false convention is not documented here (commonly 1 for deterministic, 0 for not).

functions.name: __xmlLastError
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local variable holding the last reported error. Deprecated: prefer xmlGetLastError(). Intended for internal/global use via the xmlLastError macro.
requirements: Callers must treat the returned pointer as read-only (const).
The lifetime and thread-local nature of the returned storage are managed by the library; callers must not free it.
Deprecated API; new code should use xmlGetLastError().

functions.name: __xmlGenericError
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local storage slot that holds the generic error callback function (xmlGenericErrorFunc). Typically accessed via the xmlGenericError macro. Deprecated in favor of structured errors.
requirements: Returned value is a pointer to a storage location for a function pointer; dereference to read/write the handler.
Do not free the returned pointer or the function pointer it contains.
Deprecated; prefer xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc() and structured error handling.

functions.name: __xmlGenericErrorContext
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local storage slot that holds user data (context) for the generic error handler. Typically accessed via the xmlGenericErrorContext macro. Deprecated in favor of structured errors.
requirements: Returned value is a pointer to a storage location for a void* context; dereference to read/write the context.
Do not free the returned pointer or the context it contains.
Deprecated; prefer xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc() and structured error handling.

functions.name: __xmlStructuredError
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local storage slot that holds the structured error callback function (xmlStructuredErrorFunc). Typically accessed via the xmlStructuredError macro.
requirements: Returned value is a pointer to a storage location for a function pointer; dereference to read/write the handler.
Do not free the returned pointer or the function pointer it contains.

functions.name: __xmlStructuredErrorContext
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local storage slot that holds user data (context) for the structured error handler. Typically accessed via the xmlStructuredErrorContext macro.
requirements: Returned value is a pointer to a storage location for a void* context; dereference to read/write the context.
Do not free the returned pointer or the context it contains.

functions.name: xmlSetGenericErrorFunc
functions.description: Sets the process/thread-local generic error callback and its user context. Use for legacy printf-style error reporting. Structured errors are preferred.
requirements: ctx is passed back to the handler as its first parameter; it may be NULL.
handler is a function pointer compatible with xmlGenericErrorFunc; it may be NULL (inferred from initGenericErrorDefaultFunc macro).
When handler is non-NULL, it must behave like a printf-style function corresponding to the provided format string.

functions.name: xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc
functions.description: Sets the process/thread-local structured error callback and its user context. Preferred modern mechanism for receiving xmlError structures on errors.
requirements: ctx is passed back to the handler as its first parameter; it may be NULL.
handler is a function pointer compatible with xmlStructuredErrorFunc; it may be NULL (unspecified; treat as implementation-defined).
Handler must not assume ownership of the xmlError pointer passed in.

functions.name: xmlThrDefSetGenericErrorFunc
functions.description: Deprecated thread-default variant of xmlSetGenericErrorFunc. Sets the default generic error callback and context for threads.
requirements: Deprecated; prefer xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc().
ctx is user data passed to the handler; may be NULL.
handler must be compatible with xmlGenericErrorFunc (printf-like).

functions.name: xmlThrDefSetStructuredErrorFunc
functions.description: Deprecated thread-default variant of xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc. Sets the default structured error callback and context for threads.
requirements: Deprecated; prefer xmlSetStructuredErrorFunc().
ctx is user data passed to the handler; may be NULL.
handler must be compatible with xmlStructuredErrorFunc.

functions.name: xmlParserError
functions.description: Legacy printf-style parser error reporter. Typically called by the library to emit an error via the generic error mechanism.
requirements: msg is a printf-like format string; variadic arguments must match the format (as per LIBXML_ATTR_FORMAT(2,3)).
ctx is user data passed through to the generic error handler; may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlParserWarning
functions.description: Legacy printf-style parser warning reporter. Typically called by the library to emit a warning via the generic error mechanism.
requirements: msg is a printf-like format string; variadic arguments must match the format (as per LIBXML_ATTR_FORMAT(2,3)).
ctx is user data passed through to the generic error handler; may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlParserValidityError
functions.description: Legacy printf-style validity error reporter used by the parser when validating.
requirements: msg is a printf-like format string; variadic arguments must match the format (as per LIBXML_ATTR_FORMAT(2,3)).
ctx is user data passed through to the generic error handler; may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlParserValidityWarning
functions.description: Legacy printf-style validity warning reporter used by the parser when validating.
requirements: msg is a printf-like format string; variadic arguments must match the format (as per LIBXML_ATTR_FORMAT(2,3)).
ctx is user data passed through to the generic error handler; may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlParserPrintFileInfo
functions.description: Legacy helper to print current file and line information for a parser input (diagnostics).
requirements: input is a pointer to a struct _xmlParserInput; must be a valid parser input object as used by the library (type is forward-declared here).

functions.name: xmlParserPrintFileContext
functions.description: Legacy helper to print contextual excerpt (around current position) for a parser input (diagnostics).
requirements: input is a pointer to a struct _xmlParserInput; must be a valid parser input object as used by the library (type is forward-declared here).

functions.name: xmlFormatError
functions.signature: void xmlFormatError(const xmlError *err, xmlGenericErrorFunc channel, void *data);
functions.description: Formats an xmlError into human-readable output and emits it through the supplied generic error channel with the given user data.
requirements: err is a pointer to an xmlError to format; treat as read-only.
channel is a valid xmlGenericErrorFunc to receive the formatted message; behavior if NULL is unspecified here.
data is passed to channel as its context parameter.

functions.name: xmlGetLastError
functions.description: Returns the last reported error (thread-local) as an xmlError pointer. Preferred over xmlLastError macro.
requirements: Returned pointer is read-only; do not free.
If no error has been reported in the current thread, the returned value may be NULL (unspecified here, handle gracefully).

functions.name: xmlResetLastError
functions.description: Clears the thread-local last error record.
requirements: Affects only the current thread’s last error state.

functions.name: xmlCtxtGetLastError
functions.description: Returns the last reported error associated with a specific context (opaque pointer).
requirements: ctx is an opaque library context pointer; exact type is not specified here.
Returned pointer is read-only; do not free.

functions.name: xmlCtxtResetLastError
functions.description: Clears the last error associated with a specific context (opaque pointer).
requirements: ctx is an opaque library context pointer; exact type is not specified here.

functions.name: xmlResetError
functions.description: Resets/clears the provided xmlError structure in place.
requirements: err must be a valid pointer to an xmlError to be reset.

functions.name: xmlCopyError
functions.description: Copies the contents of one xmlError structure to another. Returns an int status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: from is a pointer to the source xmlError; treat as read-only.
to is a pointer to the destination xmlError to receive a copy.

functions.name: xmlCheckVersion
functions.description: Checks at runtime that the linked libxml2 library matches the caller’s expected version. Typical usage is to call this early (often at startup) with the compile-time version constant (e.g., LIBXML_VERSION) to verify ABI compatibility before using other libxml2 APIs. If a mismatch is detected, the implementation may report an error and may terminate or otherwise prevent undefined behavior; exact side effects are not specified in this header and are unknown.
