requirements: Argument version must be an integer representing the caller’s expected libxml2 version (commonly the LIBXML_VERSION macro defined at compile time).
Should be called early (preferably before other libxml2 functions) to ensure ABI compatibility; exact timing requirements beyond this are not documented.
No return value is provided; callers must not rely on a return-based error indication.
Thread-safety and side effects on mismatch are not specified here and are unknown.

functions.name: __xmlMalloc
functions.description: When LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED is defined, returns a pointer to the thread-specific malloc() implementation used by libxml2. Typical usage is via the xmlMalloc macro which dereferences this function’s return value; direct calls can be used to retrieve or replace the allocator function pointer.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED; otherwise this symbol is not declared.

Return value is a pointer to a function of type xmlMallocFunc (void *(*)(size_t)). Caller must not invoke the function pointer after the allocator configuration has been torn down or changed by other threads.

functions.name: __xmlMallocAtomic
functions.description: When LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED is defined, returns a pointer to the thread-specific malloc() implementation intended for atomic (no interior pointers) allocations. Historically useful with garbage collectors. Typically accessed via the xmlMallocAtomic macro.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED; otherwise this symbol is not declared.

Return value is a pointer to a function of type xmlMallocFunc (void *(*)(size_t)). Usage semantics beyond being for atomic blocks are library-internal; details about GC interaction are not specified in this header.

functions.name: __xmlRealloc
functions.description: When LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED is defined, returns a pointer to the thread-specific realloc() implementation used by libxml2. Usually accessed via the xmlRealloc macro.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED; otherwise this symbol is not declared.
Return value is a pointer to a function of type xmlReallocFunc (void *(*)(void *, size_t)).

functions.name: __xmlFree
functions.description: When LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED is defined, returns a pointer to the thread-specific free() implementation used by libxml2. Usually accessed via the xmlFree macro.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED; otherwise this symbol is not declared.
Return value is a pointer to a function of type xmlFreeFunc (void (*)(void *)).

functions.name: __xmlMemStrdup
functions.description: When LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED is defined, returns a pointer to the thread-specific strdup() implementation used by libxml2. Usually accessed via the xmlMemStrdup macro.
requirements: Available only when compiled with LIBXML_THREAD_ALLOC_ENABLED; otherwise this symbol is not declared.
Return value is a pointer to a function of type xmlStrdupFunc (char *(*)(const char *)).

functions.name: xmlMemSetup
functions.signature: int xmlMemSetup(xmlFreeFunc freeFunc, xmlMallocFunc mallocFunc, xmlReallocFunc reallocFunc, xmlStrdupFunc strdupFunc);
functions.description: Installs custom memory allocator callbacks (free, malloc, realloc, strdup) for libxml2’s memory layer. Use to override the default allocation functions globally.
requirements: All function pointers passed must be valid non-NULL callbacks matching the specified types.
Callbacks must be compatible with each other (memory allocated by mallocFunc/reallocFunc/strdupFunc must be releasable by freeFunc).
Thread-safety or timing of changes is not specified; callers should avoid changing allocators while other threads may be using libxml2.

functions.name: xmlMemGet
functions.description: Retrieves the currently installed memory allocator callbacks used by libxml2’s memory layer.
requirements: Output pointers must be non-NULL if the corresponding result is desired; behavior for NULL outputs is not specified in this header.
The addresses referenced by freeFunc, mallocFunc, reallocFunc, and strdupFunc must be writable to receive the current callbacks.

functions.name: xmlGcMemSetup
functions.signature: int xmlGcMemSetup(xmlFreeFunc freeFunc, xmlMallocFunc mallocFunc, xmlMallocFunc mallocAtomicFunc, xmlReallocFunc reallocFunc, xmlStrdupFunc strdupFunc);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Installs custom allocator callbacks including a separate mallocAtomic function intended for atomic (no-pointer) blocks to support garbage-collected allocators.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
All function pointers must be valid non-NULL callbacks of the specified types.
mallocAtomicFunc must be suitable for allocating blocks that do not contain pointers and be compatible with freeFunc.
Changing allocators concurrently with libxml2 operations is unsafe; avoid reconfiguration while in use.

functions.name: xmlGcMemGet
functions.signature: int xmlGcMemGet(xmlFreeFunc *freeFunc, xmlMallocFunc *mallocFunc, xmlMallocFunc *mallocAtomicFunc, xmlReallocFunc *reallocFunc, xmlStrdupFunc *strdupFunc);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Retrieves the currently installed GC-aware allocator callbacks, including mallocAtomic.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
Output parameters provided must be writable to receive function pointers.
If an output parameter is not of interest, passing NULL may be acceptable, but this is not specified explicitly in this header.

functions.name: xmlInitMemory
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Initializes libxml2’s memory layer. Historically called before other memory operations; modern libxml2 may initialize automatically.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
Should be called before other memory-layer operations if using legacy initialization patterns.

functions.name: xmlCleanupMemory
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Cleans up libxml2’s memory layer, releasing any internal resources held by the debug memory wrapper or allocation layer.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
Should be called when the memory layer is no longer needed; do not call while other threads may still access libxml2 memory functions.

functions.name: xmlMemSize
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of an allocated memory block previously obtained through libxml2’s memory allocators. Intended for the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: ptr must point to a live allocation created by libxml2’s memory functions.
Behavior for ptr == NULL or for non-libxml2 allocations is not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlMemUsed
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes currently allocated through libxml2’s debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Function is specific to the debug memory wrapper; accurate results may depend on building with memory debugging enabled.

functions.name: xmlMemBlocks
functions.description: Returns the current number of allocated memory blocks tracked by libxml2’s debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Function is specific to the debug memory wrapper; accurate results may depend on building with memory debugging enabled.

functions.name: xmlMemDisplay
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Dumps a summary of memory usage tracked by libxml2’s debug memory wrapper to the given FILE stream.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
fp must be a valid writable FILE* opened for output.

functions.name: xmlMemDisplayLast
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Dumps information about the last nbBytes of memory operations to the given FILE stream using the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
fp must be a valid writable FILE* opened for output.
nbBytes should be non-negative; exact accepted range is not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlMemShow
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Displays details about up to nr memory allocations to the given FILE stream using the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
fp must be a valid writable FILE* opened for output.
nr should be non-negative; exact semantics and limits are not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlMemoryDump
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Dumps memory debugging information to the default output destination. Intended for use with the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.

functions.name: xmlMemMalloc
functions.description: Allocates a new memory block of the requested size via libxml2’s memory layer, returning a pointer to the block or NULL on error.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; valid range unspecified in this header.
Returned memory, if non-NULL, must be released using xmlMemFree or the configured free function.

functions.name: xmlMemRealloc
functions.description: Changes the size of an existing allocation managed by libxml2’s memory layer, returning the new pointer or NULL on error.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by libxml2’s memory allocators.
size is the new requested size in bytes; valid range unspecified.
On failure returning NULL, the original block’s state/ownership semantics are not specified in this header; callers should follow standard realloc patterns conservatively.

functions.name: xmlMemFree
functions.description: Frees a memory block previously allocated through libxml2’s memory layer.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer obtained from libxml2’s allocators (xmlMemMalloc/xmlMemRealloc/xmlMemoryStrdup or configured equivalents).
Allowance for ptr == NULL is not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlMemoryStrdup
functions.description: Duplicates a NUL-terminated C string using libxml2’s memory layer, returning a newly allocated copy or NULL on error.
requirements: str must point to a NUL-terminated string.
Returned memory must be freed using xmlMemFree or the configured free function.

functions.name: xmlMallocLoc
functions.signature: void *xmlMallocLoc(size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Allocates memory recording the source file and line for debugging purposes. Used internally by the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
file should be a valid C string identifying the source file; line should be the source line number.

functions.name: xmlReallocLoc
functions.signature: void *xmlReallocLoc(void *ptr, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Reallocates memory recording the source file and line for debugging purposes. Used internally by the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
ptr must be NULL or a pointer returned by libxml2’s memory allocators.
file should be a valid C string identifying the source file; line should be the source line number.

functions.name: xmlMallocAtomicLoc
functions.signature: void *xmlMallocAtomicLoc(size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Allocates an atomic (no interior pointers) memory block recording the source file and line for debugging purposes. Intended for GC-friendly allocators.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
file should be a valid C string identifying the source file; line should be the source line number.

functions.name: xmlMemStrdupLoc
functions.signature: char *xmlMemStrdupLoc(const char *str, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Duplicates a string while recording the source file and line for debugging. Used by the debug memory wrapper.
requirements: Marked XML_DEPRECATED; avoid new usage.
str must point to a NUL-terminated string.
file should be a valid C string identifying the source file; line should be the source line number.

functions.name: xmlModuleOpen
functions.description: Opens a dynamic module (shared library) and returns an opaque handle for later symbol lookup and closing. Intended for legacy use (deprecated) and only available when libxml is built with module support. Options are flags from xmlModuleOption (XML_MODULE_LAZY, XML_MODULE_LOCAL).
requirements: LIBXML_MODULES_ENABLED must be defined at build time for this API to be available.
This API is deprecated; prefer alternatives if available.
filename must be a non-null C string path to a loadable shared object/module.
options should be a combination (bitwise OR) of xmlModuleOption flags: XML_MODULE_LAZY (1), XML_MODULE_LOCAL (2). Behavior for other bits is unspecified.
On success, the returned xmlModule* must be released exactly once (via xmlModuleClose or xmlModuleFree) to avoid resource leaks.
The returned handle must be treated as opaque; do not dereference xmlModule* or assume structure layout.
Thread-safety is unspecified; if multiple threads may use the same module handle, external synchronization may be required.

functions.name: xmlModuleSymbol
functions.description: Resolves a named symbol exported by a previously opened dynamic module and stores its address in result. Useful for obtaining function or variable pointers from the module. Deprecated and only available when module support is enabled.
requirements: LIBXML_MODULES_ENABLED must be defined at build time for this API to be available.
This API is deprecated.
module must be a valid handle returned by xmlModuleOpen and must not have been closed/freed.
name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string naming an exported symbol in the module.
result must be a non-null pointer to storage; on success, *result will be set to the symbol address; the caller is responsible for casting to the appropriate type.
Do not use the returned symbol pointer after the module has been closed/freed.
Return-value semantics (success/failure codes) are not documented here; the caller must check and handle the function’s return value accordingly.
Thread-safety is unspecified; if resolving symbols concurrently on the same handle, synchronize externally.

functions.name: xmlModuleClose
functions.description: Closes an open dynamic module handle, unloading the module as appropriate. After closing, the handle must not be used. Deprecated and only available when module support is enabled.
requirements: LIBXML_MODULES_ENABLED must be defined at build time for this API to be available.
This API is deprecated.
module must be a valid handle previously returned by xmlModuleOpen and not yet closed/freed.
After a successful call, module becomes invalid and must not be used in any further API calls (including xmlModuleSymbol).
Call exactly once per successfully opened handle to avoid double-close issues; behavior on double close is unspecified.
Return-value semantics (e.g., 0 on success) are not specified here; the caller must check and handle errors based on the integer return value.
Do not close a module while pointers obtained via xmlModuleSymbol are still in use by other code paths unless you can guarantee they are no longer referenced.

functions.name: xmlModuleFree
functions.description: Frees a dynamic module handle. Functionally similar in purpose to xmlModuleClose (exact behavioral differences are not documented here). Deprecated and only available when module support is enabled.
requirements: LIBXML_MODULES_ENABLED must be defined at build time for this API to be available.
This API is deprecated.
module must be a valid handle previously returned by xmlModuleOpen and not yet closed/freed.
After a successful call, module becomes invalid and must not be used in any further API calls.
Call exactly once per successfully opened handle; behavior on double free is unspecified.
Return-value semantics are not specified here; the caller must check and handle errors based on the integer return value.
Do not free a module while pointers obtained via xmlModuleSymbol are still in use unless you know they are no longer referenced.

functions.name: xmlNewTextReader
functions.description: Create a new pull-based XML text reader over an existing libxml2 input buffer, optionally associating a base URI for resolving relative references. Typical use is to construct a reader on a custom input source created with xmlParserInputBufferCreate* and then iterate with xmlTextReaderRead().
requirements: input must be a valid, initialized xmlParserInputBuffer pointer created by libxml2 input buffer APIs
URI may be NULL or a valid zero-terminated string designating the base URI
The caller owns the returned xmlTextReader* and must free it with xmlFreeTextReader()
Reader functions must only be called after successful creation (non-NULL return)

functions.name: xmlNewTextReaderFilename
functions.description: Create a new XML text reader that reads from the resource identified by URI (commonly a filename or IRI). Use xmlTextReaderRead() to iterate nodes.
requirements: URI must be a non-NULL, zero-terminated string pointing to a readable resource
The caller owns the returned xmlTextReader* and must free it with xmlFreeTextReader()
Subsequent calls on the reader require a non-NULL reader object

functions.name: xmlFreeTextReader
functions.description: Destroy and free an xmlTextReader instance and any resources it owns. After this call, the reader pointer must not be used.
requirements: reader may be NULL (no effect) or a valid xmlTextReader* obtained from libxml2 reader creation APIs
Must not be called more than once for the same reader pointer
All further use of reader after this call is invalid

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetup
functions.signature: int xmlTextReaderSetup(xmlTextReader *reader, xmlParserInputBuffer *input, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Reinitialize or configure an existing reader to parse new input with the given URL, character encoding hint, and parser options. Useful for reusing a reader instance.
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader* created by a compatible constructor
input must be a valid xmlParserInputBuffer* for the new content
URL may be NULL or a valid zero-terminated string used as base URI
encoding may be NULL or a valid IANA encoding name string; if NULL, auto-detection applies
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption values
Must only be called when the reader is in a state that allows reconfiguration (implementation-defined; typically before reading or after closing)
Check the returned int for success/failure before using the reader

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetMaxAmplification
functions.description: Set an upper bound on entity expansion amplification for this reader to mitigate entity expansion attacks (billion laughs).
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader*
maxAmpl is an unsigned limit; the exact semantics depend on libxml2 version (unknown details)
Call before or early during parsing for effect; changing mid-parse may have limited impact (unknown)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetLastError
functions.description: Retrieve the last parsing error associated with this reader as an xmlError structure pointer (read-only).
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader*
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by libxml2 and must not be freed or modified by the caller
The returned pointer may become invalid after further reader operations; copy fields if needed

functions.name: xmlTextReaderRead
functions.description: Advance the reader to the next node in the XML stream. Typical iteration is a loop calling Read() until it returns 0 (EOF) or -1 (error).
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader* in a readable state
Check return value: commonly 1 on success, 0 on end of stream, and -1 on error
Do not use node-accessor functions unless Read() has returned 1 at least once

functions.name: xmlTextReaderReadInnerXml
functions.description: Return the XML markup representing the inner content of the current node as a newly allocated utf-8 string.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_WRITER_ENABLED
reader must be positioned on a node that can have inner XML (e.g., element)
The returned xmlChar* must be freed by the caller using xmlFree()
Returns NULL on error or if not applicable; check before use

functions.name: xmlTextReaderReadOuterXml
functions.description: Return the XML markup representing the current node and its content as a newly allocated utf-8 string.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_WRITER_ENABLED
reader must be positioned on a node (typically an element)
The returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
Returns NULL on error or if not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderReadString
functions.description: Return the concatenated text content of the current node and its descendants as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader* positioned on a node
The returned xmlChar* must be freed using xmlFree()
Returns NULL on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderReadAttributeValue
functions.description: When positioned on an attribute node, step through its value chunks (e.g., entity references) as separate nodes. Used to iterate attribute value nodes.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an attribute node; otherwise behavior is implementation-defined or returns 0/-1
Check return value for iteration control (typically 1 on success/advance, 0 when finished, -1 on error)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderAttributeCount
functions.description: Return the number of attributes on the current element node.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element node for a meaningful nonzero count
Negative return may indicate error; check for <0

functions.name: xmlTextReaderDepth
functions.description: Return the depth of the current node in the tree (root is depth 0).
requirements: reader must be valid; function is meaningful after at least one successful Read()
Non-negative return expected; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderHasAttributes
functions.description: Return whether the current node has any attributes (boolean as int).
requirements: reader should be positioned on an element node for meaningful results
Return is an int used as boolean; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderHasValue
functions.description: Return whether the current node has a text value.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Interpret nonzero as true; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderIsDefault
functions.description: Return whether the current attribute node was generated from a default value in the DTD or schema.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an attribute node
Return is int used as boolean; negative may indicate error or not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderIsEmptyElement
functions.description: Return whether the current element is an empty element (e.g., <tag/>).
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element node
Return is int used as boolean; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderNodeType
functions.description: Return the node type of the current node as one of xmlReaderTypes values.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Return value is one of xmlReaderTypes; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderQuoteChar
functions.description: Return the quote character used to enclose the current attribute value (' or ").
requirements: reader should be positioned on an attribute node for meaningful result
Return is the character code of the quote or 0/-1 if not applicable/error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderReadState
functions.description: Return the internal state of the reader (xmlTextReaderMode).
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader*
Return value corresponds to xmlTextReaderMode constants

functions.name: xmlTextReaderIsNamespaceDecl
functions.description: Return whether the current attribute node is a namespace declaration (xmlns or xmlns:prefix).
requirements: reader must be positioned on an attribute node to get a meaningful result
Return is int used as boolean; negative may indicate error or not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstBaseUri
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the base URI of the current node or reader context. Faster, non-allocating variant.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed or modified
Pointer may be transient; copy with xmlStrdup if needed beyond immediate use

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstLocalName
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the local name of the current node.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a named node (e.g., element, attribute)
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; copy if persistence is required

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstName
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the qualified name (QName) of the current node, if available.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a named node
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL if unavailable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstNamespaceUri
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the namespace URI of the current node, if any.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a namespaced node
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstPrefix
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the namespace prefix of the current node, if any.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a namespaced node
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstXmlLang
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the in-scope xml:lang value for the current node, if any.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstString
functions.description: Intern the provided string in the reader's string pool and return a const interned pointer (or an existing one).
requirements: reader must be valid
str may be NULL (likely returns NULL) or a zero-terminated xmlChar string
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; valid as long as reader exists

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstValue
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the value of the current node (e.g., attribute value or text node).
requirements: reader must be positioned on a node that has a value
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL

functions.name: xmlTextReaderBaseUri
functions.description: Return the base URI for the current node as a newly allocated string. Non-const, allocating variant of xmlTextReaderConstBaseUri().
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL on error or if no base URI is available

functions.name: xmlTextReaderLocalName
functions.description: Return the local name of the current node as a newly allocated string. Non-const version of xmlTextReaderConstLocalName().
requirements: reader must be positioned on a named node
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL on error or if not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderName
functions.description: Return the qualified name (QName) of the current node as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a named node
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL on error or if not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderNamespaceUri
functions.description: Return the namespace URI of the current node as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a namespaced node
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if none or on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderPrefix
functions.description: Return the namespace prefix of the current node as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on a namespaced node
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if none or on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderXmlLang
functions.description: Return the in-scope xml:lang value as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if not set or on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderValue
functions.description: Return the value of the current node as a newly allocated string (e.g., attribute value, text node content).
requirements: reader must be positioned on a node that can have a value
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if not applicable or on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderClose
functions.description: Force the reader to finish parsing and release parsing-related resources. After closing, iteration stops and certain queries may still be possible.
requirements: reader must be valid
Check return value for success; negative indicates error
Do not call Read() after successful close

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetAttributeNo
functions.description: Return the value of the attribute at the given index on the current element as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element node with attributes
no must be a valid zero-based attribute index; out-of-range likely returns NULL
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetAttribute
functions.description: Return the value of the attribute with the given qualified name on the current element as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element node
name must be a non-NULL zero-terminated xmlChar string
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree(); NULL if attribute not found

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetAttributeNs
functions.description: Return the value of the attribute with the given local name and namespace URI on the current element as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element node
localName must be non-NULL; namespaceURI may be NULL or a zero-terminated xmlChar string
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree(); NULL if not found

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetRemainder
functions.description: Return the underlying input buffer with the unread remainder of the input stream, detaching it from the reader. Used to access remaining data when aborting a parse.
requirements: reader must be valid
The returned xmlParserInputBuffer*, if non-NULL, becomes the caller’s responsibility to free via the corresponding input buffer API
Reader may no longer be usable for normal reading after detaching the buffer (usage semantics are implementation-defined; treat as terminal)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderLookupNamespace
functions.description: Resolve a namespace prefix in the current context and return the namespace URI as a newly allocated string.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned where namespace context is defined
prefix may be NULL to resolve the default namespace
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if prefix not bound or on error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToAttributeNo
functions.description: Move the reader to the attribute at the specified index of the current element.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element with attributes
no must be a valid zero-based attribute index
Check return value for success (nonzero) vs failure (0) or error (<0) before accessing attribute properties

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToAttribute
functions.description: Move the reader to the attribute with the specified qualified name on the current element.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element
name must be a non-NULL zero-terminated xmlChar string
Check return value before accessing attribute properties

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToAttributeNs
functions.description: Move the reader to the attribute with the given local name and namespace URI on the current element.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element
localName must be non-NULL; namespaceURI may be NULL or a valid xmlChar*
Check return value before accessing attribute properties

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToFirstAttribute
functions.description: Move the reader to the first attribute of the current element.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an element with attributes
Check return value for success (nonzero)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToNextAttribute
functions.description: Move the reader to the next attribute of the current element.
requirements: reader must currently be positioned on an attribute of an element
Use return value to control iteration (nonzero success, 0 no more, <0 error)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderMoveToElement
functions.description: Move the reader back to the element node that owns the current attribute.
requirements: reader must be positioned on an attribute for the move to be meaningful
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderNormalization
functions.description: Return whether text normalization is enabled for the reader.
requirements: reader must be valid
Return is int used as boolean; negative may indicate error or unsupported

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstEncoding
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the character encoding name used by the input, if known.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned pointer is const and must not be freed; may be NULL if unknown

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetParserProp
functions.signature: int xmlTextReaderSetParserProp(xmlTextReader *reader, int prop, int value);
functions.description: Set a parser property on the reader (deprecated in favor of passing options to constructors).
requirements: reader must be valid
prop should be one of xmlParserProperties or a supported property id; value interpreted per property
Check return value for success; unsupported properties may fail

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetParserProp
functions.description: Query a parser property on the reader.
requirements: reader must be valid
prop should be a supported property id; return value semantics depend on property
Negative return may indicate error or unsupported property

functions.name: xmlTextReaderCurrentNode
functions.description: Return the underlying libxml2 tree node corresponding to the current reader position. Useful for interop with tree APIs.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Returned xmlNode* is owned by the reader/document; do not free it
Pointer may become invalid after further reader moves; copy if needed

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetParserLineNumber
functions.description: Return the current parser line number corresponding to the reader position.
requirements: reader must be valid
Non-negative return expected; negative may indicate unavailable/error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetParserColumnNumber
functions.description: Return the current parser column number corresponding to the reader position.
requirements: reader must be valid
Non-negative return expected; negative may indicate unavailable/error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderPreserve
functions.description: Preserve the current node subtree in the resulting document when using reader-to-tree workflows, returning the preserved node.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Returned xmlNode* is owned by the document; do not free
Effect is meaningful when building/preserving a tree; exact behavior depends on reader mode (unknown details)

functions.name: xmlTextReaderPreservePattern
functions.description: Register an XPath-like pattern to preserve matching nodes during reader-based processing.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_PATTERN_ENABLED
reader must be valid
pattern must be a non-NULL zero-terminated xmlChar expression
namespaces may be NULL or an array of prefix/URI pairs terminated by NULL
Check return value for success; invalid patterns will fail

functions.name: xmlTextReaderCurrentDoc
functions.description: Return the current xmlDoc associated with the reader, if any.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned xmlDoc* is owned by libxml2; do not free
May return NULL if not applicable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderExpand
functions.description: Expand the current node and return it as a libxml2 tree node, potentially materializing more of the tree.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Returned xmlNode* is owned by the document; do not free
Subsequent reader operations may invalidate direct pointers; use with care

functions.name: xmlTextReaderNext
functions.description: Skip to the next sibling of the current node, advancing the reader past the current subtree.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Check return value for success/end/error as with xmlTextReaderRead

functions.name: xmlTextReaderNextSibling
functions.description: Advance the reader to the next sibling node at the same depth.
requirements: reader must be valid and positioned on a node
Check return value for success/end/error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderIsValid
functions.description: Return whether the document is valid against the activated validation (DTD/RelaxNG/Schema) for this reader.
requirements: reader must be valid
Validation must have been configured; otherwise the result may be 0 or unspecified
Return is int used as boolean; negative may indicate error

functions.name: xmlTextReaderRelaxNGValidate
functions.description: Enable Relax NG validation using a schema at the given URI/path for this reader.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_RELAXNG_ENABLED
reader must be valid and not yet finished parsing
rng must be a non-NULL zero-terminated string pointing to a readable Relax NG schema (file/URI)
Check return value for success; failures indicate that validation could not be set up

functions.name: xmlTextReaderRelaxNGValidateCtxt
functions.description: Enable Relax NG validation using an existing validation context with options.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_RELAXNG_ENABLED
reader must be valid
ctxt must be a properly initialized xmlRelaxNGValidCtxt*
options is a bitmask of validation options (library-defined)
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderRelaxNGSetSchema
functions.description: Attach a precompiled Relax NG schema to the reader for validation.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_RELAXNG_ENABLED
reader must be valid
schema must be a valid compiled xmlRelaxNG* (or NULL to disable)
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSchemaValidate
functions.description: Enable W3C XML Schema (XSD) validation using a schema at the given URI/path for this reader.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED
reader must be valid and not yet finished parsing
xsd must be a non-NULL zero-terminated string pointing to a readable XSD
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSchemaValidateCtxt
functions.description: Enable XML Schema validation using an existing validation context and options.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED
reader must be valid
ctxt must be a properly initialized xmlSchemaValidCtxt*
options is a bitmask of validation options
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetSchema
functions.description: Attach a precompiled XML Schema to the reader for validation.
requirements: Available only if compiled with LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED
reader must be valid
schema must be a compiled xmlSchema* (or NULL to disable)
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderConstXmlVersion
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the XML version (“1.0”, etc.) declared for the current document.
requirements: reader must be valid
Returned pointer is const; do not free; may be NULL if unknown

functions.name: xmlTextReaderStandalone
functions.description: Return the standalone document declaration value: 1 (standalone), 0 (not standalone), or other per libxml2 semantics.
requirements: reader must be valid
Interpretation follows XML declaration; negative may indicate error or unknown

functions.name: xmlTextReaderByteConsumed
functions.description: Return the number of bytes consumed by the parser from the input so far.
requirements: reader must be valid
Non-negative value expected; negative may indicate unavailable/error

functions.name: xmlReaderWalker
functions.description: Create a reader that walks an existing in-memory xmlDoc tree instead of streaming from I/O.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDoc*
Caller owns the returned reader and must free it with xmlFreeTextReader()

functions.name: xmlReaderForDoc
functions.signature: xmlTextReader *xmlReaderForDoc(const xmlChar *cur, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Create a reader to parse XML from an in-memory buffer (null-terminated or sized by content) with optional base URL, encoding hint, and parser options.
requirements: cur must point to XML content as a zero-terminated xmlChar string
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Caller must free the returned reader with xmlFreeTextReader()

functions.name: xmlReaderForFile
functions.signature: xmlTextReader *xmlReaderForFile(const char *filename, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Create a reader to parse XML from a file on disk, with optional encoding hint and parser options.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL path to a readable file
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Caller must free the returned reader with xmlFreeTextReader()

functions.name: xmlReaderForMemory
functions.signature: xmlTextReader *xmlReaderForMemory(const char *buffer, int size, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Create a reader to parse XML from a memory buffer of given size, with optional base URL, encoding, and parser options.
requirements: buffer must point to at least size bytes of XML content; may contain NULs
size must be non-negative and reflect the buffer length
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Caller must free the returned reader with xmlFreeTextReader()

functions.name: xmlReaderForFd
functions.signature: xmlTextReader *xmlReaderForFd(int fd, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Create a reader to parse XML from a POSIX file descriptor, with optional base URL, encoding, and parser options.
requirements: fd must be an open, readable file descriptor and remain valid for the reader’s lifetime
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Caller must free the returned reader with xmlFreeTextReader()

functions.name: xmlReaderForIO
functions.signature: xmlTextReader *xmlReaderForIO(xmlInputReadCallback ioread, xmlInputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Create a reader that pulls bytes via user-provided I/O callbacks, with optional base URL, encoding, and options.
requirements: ioread must be a valid function conforming to xmlInputReadCallback; it will be called to supply data
ioclose may be NULL or a valid xmlInputCloseCallback; used to close/release ioctx
ioctx is an opaque user context passed to callbacks
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Callbacks must be thread-safe with respect to the reader if used concurrently

functions.name: xmlReaderNewWalker
functions.description: Initialize or reconfigure an existing reader to walk an existing xmlDoc tree.
requirements: reader must be a valid xmlTextReader* (uninitialized or reusable)
doc must be a valid xmlDoc*
Check return value for success before using the reader

functions.name: xmlReaderNewDoc
functions.signature: int xmlReaderNewDoc(xmlTextReader *reader, const xmlChar *cur, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Initialize an existing reader to parse from an in-memory XML string with URL, encoding, and options.
requirements: reader must be valid
cur must be a zero-terminated xmlChar string with XML content
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlReaderNewFile
functions.signature: int xmlReaderNewFile(xmlTextReader *reader, const char *filename, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Initialize an existing reader to parse from a file.
requirements: reader must be valid
filename must be a non-NULL readable path
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlReaderNewMemory
functions.signature: int xmlReaderNewMemory(xmlTextReader *reader, const char *buffer, int size, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Initialize an existing reader to parse from a memory buffer.
requirements: reader must be valid
buffer must point to at least size bytes of XML content
size must be non-negative
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlReaderNewFd
functions.signature: int xmlReaderNewFd(xmlTextReader *reader, int fd, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Initialize an existing reader to parse from a POSIX file descriptor.
requirements: reader must be valid
fd must be an open, readable file descriptor that remains valid for parsing
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlReaderNewIO
functions.signature: int xmlReaderNewIO(xmlTextReader *reader, xmlInputReadCallback ioread, xmlInputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, const char *URL, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Initialize an existing reader to pull data using user-supplied I/O callbacks.
requirements: reader must be valid
ioread must be a valid xmlInputReadCallback function
ioclose may be NULL or a valid xmlInputCloseCallback
ioctx is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks
URL may be NULL or a base URI string
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name
options is a bitmask of xmlParserOption flags
Check return value for success

functions.name: xmlTextReaderLocatorLineNumber
functions.description: Return the source line number indicated by the locator provided to the error callback.
requirements: locator must be the locator passed to an xmlTextReaderErrorFunc callback; may be NULL
Non-negative return expected when available; negative may indicate unavailable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderLocatorBaseURI
functions.description: Return the base URI associated with the locator as a newly allocated string.
requirements: locator must be the locator from an error callback; may be NULL
Returned xmlChar* must be freed with xmlFree()
May return NULL if unavailable

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetErrorHandler
functions.description: Install a per-reader simple error handler callback receiving error messages, severities, and a locator. The arg is passed through to the callback.
requirements: reader must be valid
f may be NULL to remove the handler, or a valid function matching xmlTextReaderErrorFunc
arg is an opaque user pointer supplied back on callbacks
Callback must not longjmp out unless libxml2 is known to be longjmp-safe in this context (general caution)
Callback must be re-entrant/thread-safe relative to caller’s needs

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetStructuredErrorHandler
functions.description: Install a per-reader structured error handler (xmlError*) callback for detailed error reporting.
requirements: reader must be valid
f may be NULL to remove the handler, or a valid xmlStructuredErrorFunc
arg is an opaque user pointer returned on callbacks
Do not free or modify the xmlError* passed to the callback

functions.name: xmlTextReaderGetErrorHandler
functions.description: Retrieve the currently installed simple error handler callback and its user argument for this reader.
requirements: reader must be valid
f and arg may be NULL or valid output pointers; non-NULL pointers must be writable
Returned function pointer and arg are outputs only; do not call if f is NULL

functions.name: xmlTextReaderSetResourceLoader
functions.description: Set a per-reader resource loader callback (custom entity/external resource resolver) with user data.
requirements: reader must be valid
loader may be NULL to clear, or a valid function of type xmlResourceLoader
data is an opaque pointer passed to loader
Loader implementation must follow libxml2 expectations for resource resolution and memory management (library-defined)

functions.name: xmlRegexpCompile
functions.description: Compiles a regular expression (as an xmlChar, typically UTF-8, NUL-terminated string) into a libxml2 regex object usable for matching. Use the returned xmlRegexp* with xmlRegexpExec or the progressive API, and free it with xmlRegFreeRegexp when no longer needed. Details of the accepted regex syntax and error reporting are not specified in this header.
requirements: regexp must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string containing a regular expression.
The caller must release the returned xmlRegexp* with xmlRegFreeRegexp to avoid memory leaks.
Function availability depends on LIBXML_REGEXP_ENABLED being enabled at build time.

functions.name: xmlRegFreeRegexp
functions.description: Frees a compiled libxml2 regular expression created by xmlRegexpCompile. Deprecated status is not indicated for this function; it is the standard deallocator for xmlRegexp objects.
requirements: regexp must be a valid pointer returned by xmlRegexpCompile and not already freed.
Do not use the regexp pointer after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: xmlRegexpExec
functions.description: Executes the compiled regular expression comp against the input string value. Intended for one-shot, non-progressive matching. The exact meaning of the integer return code is not specified here; treat it as a status/result code.
requirements: comp must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid compiled regex from xmlRegexpCompile.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string to be matched.

functions.name: xmlRegexpPrint
functions.description: [Deprecated] Prints a textual representation of the compiled regular expression to the given FILE stream, typically for debugging. Behavior and output format are not specified here.
requirements: output must be a valid FILE* open for writing (e.g., stdout, stderr, or a writable file stream).
regexp must be a non-NULL pointer to a compiled regex from xmlRegexpCompile.

functions.name: xmlRegexpIsDeterminist
functions.description: Checks whether the compiled regular expression is deterministic. Returns an integer indicating determinism; exact return semantics are not specified in this header.
requirements: comp must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid compiled regex from xmlRegexpCompile.

functions.name: xmlRegNewExecCtxt
functions.description: [Deprecated] Creates a progressive regular expression execution context for comp. Optionally registers a transition callback invoked during automaton transitions and associates user data passed back during callbacks. Use with xmlRegExecPushString/xmlRegExecPushString2 to feed input incrementally, and free with xmlRegFreeExecCtxt.
requirements: comp must be a non-NULL pointer to a compiled regex from xmlRegexpCompile.
If callback is non-NULL, it must match the xmlRegExecCallbacks signature and be prepared to receive tokens, transition data, and the provided user data.
The returned context must be freed with xmlRegFreeExecCtxt.

functions.name: xmlRegFreeExecCtxt
functions.description: [Deprecated] Frees a progressive regular expression execution context previously created by xmlRegNewExecCtxt.
requirements: exec must be a valid pointer returned by xmlRegNewExecCtxt and not already freed.
Do not use exec after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: xmlRegExecPushString
functions.description: [Deprecated] Pushes an input string fragment into the progressive execution context exec. The fragment is processed by the regex automaton; data is passed through to callbacks if applicable. Returns an integer status code; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: exec must be a non-NULL execution context created by xmlRegNewExecCtxt.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string fragment to feed into the matcher.

functions.name: xmlRegExecPushString2
functions.signature: int xmlRegExecPushString2(xmlRegExecCtxt *exec, const xmlChar *value, const xmlChar *value2, void *data);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Pushes two input string fragments, value and value2, into the progressive execution context exec in one call. data is passed through to callbacks if applicable. Returns an integer status code; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: exec must be a non-NULL execution context created by xmlRegNewExecCtxt.
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string fragment.
value2 must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string fragment.

functions.name: xmlRegExecNextValues
functions.signature: int xmlRegExecNextValues(xmlRegExecCtxt *exec, int *nbval, int *nbneg, xmlChar **values, int *terminal);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Queries the progressive execution context exec for information about next acceptable values/tokens and terminal state. The function fills output parameters describing the number of positive and negative values, a values array, and whether a terminal state is reachable. Returns an integer status code; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: exec must be a non-NULL execution context created by xmlRegNewExecCtxt.
nbval must be a valid pointer to an int to receive the number of positive values.
nbneg must be a valid pointer to an int to receive the number of negative values.
values must be a valid pointer suitable for receiving xmlChar* entries (allocation/ownership details are unknown from this header).
terminal must be a valid pointer to an int to receive terminal-state information.

functions.name: xmlRegExecErrInfo
functions.signature: int xmlRegExecErrInfo(xmlRegExecCtxt *exec, const xmlChar **string, int *nbval, int *nbneg, xmlChar **values, int *terminal);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves error-related information from the progressive execution context exec, including the input string position or token, counts of positive/negative values, an associated values array, and terminal-state information. Returns an integer status code; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: exec must be a non-NULL execution context created by xmlRegNewExecCtxt.
string must be a valid pointer to receive a const xmlChar* reference associated with the error context.
nbval must be a valid pointer to an int to receive the number of positive values.
nbneg must be a valid pointer to an int to receive the number of negative values.
values must be a valid pointer suitable for receiving xmlChar* entries (allocation/ownership details are unknown from this header).
terminal must be a valid pointer to an int to receive terminal-state information.

functions.name: xmlSaveToFd
functions.signature: xmlSaveCtxt *xmlSaveToFd(int fd, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Creates a new XML/HTML save context that writes serialized output to a file descriptor. Use this to serialize a whole document or subtrees via xmlSaveDoc/xmlSaveTree, then flush/close the context. Encoding may be NULL to use the document's encoding. Options is a bitmask of xmlSaveOption flags.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable file descriptor for the duration of the save context.
encoding may be NULL or a valid IANA/Libxml2-recognized encoding name string.
options is a bitwise OR of xmlSaveOption values; unknown bits are ignored or may cause errors depending on libxml2.
The returned xmlSaveCtxt* must be released by calling xmlSaveClose (or xmlSaveFinish followed by xmlSaveClose) after use.
Thread-safety follows libxml2 global/threading rules; do not share a single context across threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: xmlSaveToFilename
functions.signature: xmlSaveCtxt *xmlSaveToFilename(const char *filename, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Creates a save context that writes serialized output to the specified file path. Use with xmlSaveDoc/xmlSaveTree to serialize content, then flush/close when done. Encoding may be NULL to use the document's encoding. Options is a bitmask of xmlSaveOption flags.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL, valid path to a file that can be created or opened for writing.
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name understood by libxml2.
options is a bitwise OR of xmlSaveOption values.
Caller must close the context with xmlSaveClose (or xmlSaveFinish then xmlSaveClose).
The file will be created/truncated depending on libxml2 I/O layer behavior and permissions; ensure appropriate access rights.

functions.name: xmlSaveToBuffer
functions.description: Creates a save context that writes serialized output into an existing libxml2 xmlBuffer. Use with xmlSaveDoc/xmlSaveTree to serialize content into memory. Encoding may be NULL to use the document's encoding. Options is a bitmask of xmlSaveOption flags.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, initialized xmlBuffer* and remain valid for the life of the context.
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name.
options is a bitwise OR of xmlSaveOption values.
Caller must close the context with xmlSaveClose (or xmlSaveFinish then xmlSaveClose) to finalize output into the buffer.
Do not free or reuse the xmlBuffer until the save context is closed.

functions.name: xmlSaveToIO
functions.signature: xmlSaveCtxt *xmlSaveToIO(xmlOutputWriteCallback iowrite, xmlOutputCloseCallback ioclose, void *ioctx, const char *encoding, int options);
functions.description: Creates a save context that writes serialized output via custom I/O callbacks. Provide write and close callbacks plus an opaque context pointer passed to them. Encoding may be NULL to use the document's encoding. Options is a bitmask of xmlSaveOption flags.
requirements: iowrite must be a valid function pointer matching xmlOutputWriteCallback and able to write data for the entire serialization.
ioclose may be NULL or a valid xmlOutputCloseCallback; if non-NULL it will be called when closing the context.
ioctx is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks; it must remain valid until the context is closed.
encoding may be NULL or a valid encoding name.
options is a bitwise OR of xmlSaveOption values.
Caller must close the context with xmlSaveClose (or xmlSaveFinish then xmlSaveClose).
Callbacks must obey libxml2 callback contracts: write returns number of bytes written or a negative value on error; close returns 0 on success or negative on error.

functions.name: xmlSaveDoc
functions.description: Serializes a full xmlDoc to the given save context. Returns the number of bytes written (or a negative value on error, depending on libxml2). Use after creating a context with xmlSaveTo*.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSaveCtxt* returned by an xmlSaveTo* function and not yet closed.
doc must be a valid, fully constructed xmlDoc*.
Context options and encoding determine output; ensure they are compatible with the document.
After writing, caller should flush or close the context to ensure data is emitted.

functions.name: xmlSaveTree
functions.description: Serializes a subtree starting at the given xmlNode into the save context. Returns the number of bytes written (or a negative value on error).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt* from xmlSaveTo*.
node must be a valid xmlNode* that is part of a document or a well-formed standalone subtree.
Caller should flush or close the context after writing to ensure data is emitted.
Output may depend on the node type and context options (XML vs HTML, formatting flags).

functions.name: xmlSaveFlush
functions.description: Flushes any buffered output of the save context to the underlying sink (file, buffer, or I/O).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt*.
May return a negative value on error depending on libxml2; caller should check the return code.
Flushing does not close the context; caller must still call xmlSaveClose to finish.

functions.name: xmlSaveClose
functions.description: Finalizes and closes the save context, flushing remaining data and releasing associated resources. Should be called once per context when done writing.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSaveCtxt* obtained from xmlSaveTo* and not previously closed.
After this call, the context must not be used again.
Return value should be checked for errors (negative on error depending on libxml2).
If using xmlSaveFinish for detailed error retrieval, call it before xmlSaveClose.

functions.name: xmlSaveFinish
functions.description: Completes serialization and returns a detailed parser/serializer error code (xmlParserErrors) for the save operation. Typically used prior to xmlSaveClose to retrieve a final status.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt*.
Call before xmlSaveClose if you need an xmlParserErrors status code.
After finishing, you still must call xmlSaveClose to release resources.

functions.name: xmlSaveSetIndentString
functions.description: Sets the string used for indentation when formatting is enabled (e.g., XML_SAVE_FORMAT and not XML_SAVE_NO_INDENT). Returns 0 on success or a negative value on error depending on libxml2.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt*.
indent must be a valid C string pointer; may be NULL to reset to default behavior (if supported by libxml2).
Effect applies to subsequent serialization using this context only.

functions.name: xmlSaveSetEscape
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets a custom escaping function used during serialization of character data. Returns status integer. Prefer default escaping behavior in modern libxml2.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt*.
escape must be a function pointer of type xmlCharEncodingOutputFunc or NULL to restore default behavior (depending on libxml2).
Because this API is deprecated, new code should avoid relying on it; behavior may be removed in future versions.

functions.name: xmlSaveSetAttrEscape
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets a custom escaping function specifically for attribute values during serialization. Returns status integer. Prefer default escaping behavior.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, open xmlSaveCtxt*.
escape must be a function pointer of type xmlCharEncodingOutputFunc or NULL to restore default behavior (depending on libxml2).
Deprecated API; avoid in new code.

functions.name: xmlThrDefIndentTreeOutput
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets the thread-local default for tree output indentation (legacy global setting). Returns the previous value. Avoid using; prefer per-context options like XML_SAVE_INDENT/XML_SAVE_NO_INDENT.
requirements: Callable at any time, but affects thread-local global behavior in libxml2 (deprecated).
v is typically 0 or 1 to disable/enable indentation; other values are treated per libxml2 semantics.
New code should not depend on this setting; prefer per-save-context configuration.

functions.name: xmlThrDefTreeIndentString
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets the thread-local default indentation string for tree output (legacy global setting) and returns the previous string pointer. Prefer xmlSaveSetIndentString on a save context.
requirements: v is a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string specifying the indent unit, or possibly NULL to query/reset depending on libxml2 semantics.
Affects thread-local global behavior only; deprecated in favor of per-context configuration.
Returned pointer is managed by libxml2; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: xmlThrDefSaveNoEmptyTags
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets the thread-local default controlling emission of empty tags (legacy behavior). Returns the previous value. Prefer per-context XML_SAVE_EMPTY or XML_SAVE_NO_EMPTY options.
requirements: Callable at any time, but affects thread-local global behavior in libxml2 (deprecated).
v is typically 0 or 1; other values are per libxml2 semantics.
New code should use xmlSaveOption flags instead of this API.

functions.name: xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new schema parser context for a schema located by URL (system identifier). Use this to prepare parsing/compiling an XML Schema from a file or URI. Typical usage: create the parser context, optionally set parser error handlers or resource loader, then call xmlSchemaParse().
requirements: URL may be NULL or a valid C string pointing to a schema location (inferred from libxml2 patterns; exact NULL handling unknown).
The returned xmlSchemaParserCtxt* must be freed with xmlSchemaFreeParserCtxt() when no longer needed (inferred from dedicated free function).

functions.name: xmlSchemaNewMemParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new schema parser context to parse/compile an XML Schema provided from a memory buffer.
requirements: buffer must point to a memory block containing the schema bytes.
size must be the number of bytes in buffer and should be >= 0; negative values are invalid (inferred from common API semantics).
The returned xmlSchemaParserCtxt* must be freed with xmlSchemaFreeParserCtxt() when done.

functions.name: xmlSchemaNewDocParserCtxt
functions.description: Create a new schema parser context from an already parsed XML document containing a schema.
requirements: doc must be a valid, initialized xmlDoc* representing an XML Schema document.
doc must remain alive and unmodified for the lifetime of the parser context (inferred).
Free the returned context with xmlSchemaFreeParserCtxt() when finished.

functions.name: xmlSchemaFreeParserCtxt
functions.description: Free a schema parser context previously created by one of the xmlSchemaNew*ParserCtxt functions.
requirements: ctxt must be either NULL or a pointer returned by an xmlSchemaNew*ParserCtxt function and not already freed.
After this call, ctxt must not be used again.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetParserErrors
functions.signature: void xmlSchemaSetParserErrors(xmlSchemaParserCtxt *ctxt, xmlSchemaValidityErrorFunc err, xmlSchemaValidityWarningFunc warn, void *ctx);
functions.description: Install error and warning callback functions for schema parsing on the given parser context. Messages will be reported through these callbacks using the supplied user context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid parser context created by xmlSchemaNew*ParserCtxt and not yet freed.
err and/or warn may be NULL to disable the corresponding callback (inferred; exact behavior if NULL is unknown).
ctx is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks; if supplied, it must remain valid while parsing occurs.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetParserStructuredErrors
functions.description: Install a structured error callback (xmlStructuredErrorFunc) for schema parsing on the given parser context, receiving detailed xmlError information.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid, live xmlSchemaParserCtxt*.
serror may be NULL to disable structured error reporting (inferred; exact behavior if NULL is unknown).
ctx is an opaque pointer provided back to the callback and must remain valid during parsing.

functions.name: xmlSchemaGetParserErrors
functions.description: Retrieve the currently installed parser error and warning callbacks and their user context from a schema parser context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaParserCtxt*.
err, warn, and ctx may be NULL if the caller is not interested in a particular value (inferred).
If non-NULL, *err, *warn, and *ctx receive the currently configured handlers/context.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetResourceLoader
functions.description: Set a custom resource loader on the parser context to resolve external schema resources (e.g., imports/includes).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaParserCtxt*.
loader is a function pointer of type xmlResourceLoader; if non-NULL, it should adhere to libxml2 resource loading expectations (exact contract not described here).
data is an opaque pointer passed to the loader; it must remain valid for the duration of parsing.

functions.name: xmlSchemaIsValid
functions.description: Query validation status of the validation context. Intended to report whether validation has encountered errors so far. Specific return semantics are not documented here; likely follows libxml2 conventions (non-zero/zero or 0/>0/<0).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt* created by xmlSchemaNewValidCtxt() and not freed.

functions.name: xmlSchemaParse
functions.description: Parse/compile an XML Schema using the provided parser context, producing a compiled xmlSchema object for validation.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid schema parser context with its source set (URL/memory/doc) and not freed.
On success, the returned xmlSchema* must be freed with xmlSchemaFree().
The parser context may report errors via installed callbacks; callers should handle NULL return indicating failure (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaFree
functions.description: Free a compiled xmlSchema object previously returned by xmlSchemaParse().
requirements: schema must be either NULL or a pointer returned by xmlSchemaParse() that has not already been freed.
After this call, schema must not be used.

functions.name: xmlSchemaDump
functions.description: Debug helper: dump a human-readable representation of the compiled schema to the given FILE stream. Available only when compiled with LIBXML_DEBUG_ENABLED.
requirements: This function is available only if LIBXML_DEBUG_ENABLED is defined at build time.
output must be a valid FILE* open for writing (e.g., stdout, stderr, or a file).
schema must be a valid compiled xmlSchema*.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetValidErrors
functions.signature: void xmlSchemaSetValidErrors(xmlSchemaValidCtxt *ctxt, xmlSchemaValidityErrorFunc err, xmlSchemaValidityWarningFunc warn, void *ctx);
functions.description: Install error and warning callbacks for validation on the given validation context. Validation diagnostics will be reported through these callbacks with the provided user context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt* and not freed.
err and/or warn may be NULL to disable the corresponding reporting (inferred; exact behavior if NULL is unknown).
ctx must remain valid while validation occurs.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetValidStructuredErrors
functions.description: Install a structured error callback for validation to receive detailed xmlError data.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
serror may be NULL to disable structured error reporting (inferred).
ctx must remain valid during validation.

functions.name: xmlSchemaGetValidErrors
functions.description: Retrieve the currently installed validation error and warning callbacks and their user context from a validation context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
err, warn, and ctx may be NULL if not needed (inferred).
If non-NULL, outputs receive the current handlers/context.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSetValidOptions
functions.description: Set validation options (bitmask) on the validation context. Currently defined options are values of xmlSchemaValidOption (e.g., XML_SCHEMA_VAL_VC_I_CREATE).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
options must be a bitwise OR of xmlSchemaValidOption flags. At present, the documented flag is XML_SCHEMA_VAL_VC_I_CREATE.
Returns a status code indicating success or failure; exact return semantics are not described here (unknown).

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateSetFilename
functions.description: Set the filename associated with the instance being validated to improve error reporting (e.g., used when no parser context is available).
requirements: vctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
filename should be a NUL-terminated C string; may be NULL to clear (inferred; exact NULL handling unknown).
The string data must remain valid for at least the duration required for error reporting (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidCtxtGetOptions
functions.description: Get the current validation options bitmask from the validation context.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
Return value is a bitmask composed of xmlSchemaValidOption values (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaNewValidCtxt
functions.description: Create a new validation context for validating instance documents against the given compiled xmlSchema.
requirements: schema must be a valid compiled xmlSchema* (from xmlSchemaParse()) and remain alive as long as the validation context is used.
The returned xmlSchemaValidCtxt* must be freed with xmlSchemaFreeValidCtxt().

functions.name: xmlSchemaFreeValidCtxt
functions.description: Free a validation context previously allocated by xmlSchemaNewValidCtxt().
requirements: ctxt must be either NULL or a pointer returned by xmlSchemaNewValidCtxt() and not already freed.
After this call, ctxt must not be used.

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateDoc
functions.description: Validate a parsed XML document against the schema associated with the validation context. Returns a status code indicating validation result (typically 0 for valid, >0 for validation errors, <0 for internal errors; inferred from libxml2 conventions).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt* set up for the target schema.
instance must be a valid, fully built xmlDoc* of the instance document to validate.
Caller should check the return value and/or configured error callbacks to handle validation diagnostics.

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateOneElement
functions.description: Validate a single element node (and typically its subtree) against the schema using the given validation context. Return semantics follow libxml2 validation conventions (inferred).
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
elem must be a valid xmlNode* pointing to an element node belonging to a document tree (inferred).
Caller should inspect the integer return code and error callbacks for details.

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateStream
functions.signature: int xmlSchemaValidateStream(xmlSchemaValidCtxt *ctxt, xmlParserInputBuffer *input, xmlCharEncoding enc, const xmlSAXHandler *sax, void *user_data);
functions.description: Validate an instance document provided as a streaming input buffer against the schema using a SAX-style pipeline. Allows specifying the encoding and a SAX handler plus its user data.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
input must be a valid xmlParserInputBuffer* supplying the document bytes.
enc should specify the character encoding; use XML_CHAR_ENCODING_NONE to auto-detect if appropriate (inferred libxml pattern; exact constant not stated here).
If provided, sax must describe a valid SAX handler compatible with libxml2; user_data is passed to SAX callbacks and must remain valid during validation.
Return value follows libxml2 validation status conventions (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateFile
functions.signature: int xmlSchemaValidateFile(xmlSchemaValidCtxt *ctxt, const char * filename, int options);
functions.description: Validate an instance document loaded from a file given by filename against the schema. Options control validation behavior.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
filename must be a NUL-terminated C string path to a readable file containing the XML instance.
options must be a bitmask of xmlSchemaValidOption values; currently only XML_SCHEMA_VAL_VC_I_CREATE is defined.
Caller should check the integer return code to determine validation success/failure.

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidCtxtGetParserCtxt
functions.description: Obtain the underlying xmlParserCtxt used during validation, if any, from a validation context. Useful for accessing parser diagnostics or state.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
The returned xmlParserCtxt* may be NULL if not applicable (inferred; exact conditions unknown).
The caller must not free the returned parser context; it is owned by the validation machinery (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaSAXPlug
functions.description: Insert schema validation into an existing SAX processing chain by plugging a validation layer. Returns a plug handle and updates the provided SAX handler and user_data pointers to route events through the validator.
requirements: ctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
sax must be a non-NULL pointer to a xmlSAXHandler* variable; on success it may be updated to a wrapped handler.
user_data must be a non-NULL pointer to a void* variable; on success it may be updated to corresponding user data.
The returned plug must later be passed to xmlSchemaSAXUnplug() to restore the original SAX chain.

functions.name: xmlSchemaSAXUnplug
functions.description: Remove a previously installed SAX validation plug, restoring the original SAX handler chain.
requirements: plug must be a plug handle returned by a successful xmlSchemaSAXPlug() call and not already unplugged.
Call exactly once per successful plug to avoid leaks or inconsistent SAX handler state (inferred).
Returns a status code indicating success or failure; exact semantics unknown.

functions.name: xmlSchemaValidateSetLocator
functions.description: Install a callback to locate file and line information for validation errors when node or file context is not otherwise available.
requirements: vctxt must be a valid xmlSchemaValidCtxt*.
f must be a function of type xmlSchemaValidityLocatorFunc that returns 0 on success and -1 on error (as documented for the locator func type).
ctxt is an opaque user context forwarded to the locator callback and must remain valid while used.

functions.name: xmlSchemaInitTypes
functions.description: Initializes the XML Schema datatypes subsystem in libxml2. Typically called once before using any schema datatype APIs. Returns 0 or a non-negative value on success, negative on error (exact codes unspecified).
requirements: Must be called before using other xmlSchema datatype functions if the library does not lazily initialize types (library dependent; details not documented here).
Safe to call when LIBXML_SCHEMAS_ENABLED is defined; otherwise unavailable.
Should be called at most once during process initialization (inferred from typical init pattern).
Check the integer return value for errors before proceeding.

functions.name: xmlSchemaCleanupTypes
functions.description: Cleans up and releases resources associated with the XML Schema datatypes subsystem. Marked deprecated; newer libxml2 versions may not require or recommend calling it.
requirements: Function is deprecated; prefer not to call in new code.
If used, call when no other threads are concurrently using schema datatype APIs (thread-safety not guaranteed; inferred from typical cleanup semantics).
Should be called after all schema datatype objects (e.g., xmlSchemaVal*, xmlSchemaFacet*) are no longer in use (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSchemaGetPredefinedType
functions.description: Looks up a predefined/builtin XML Schema type by its local name and namespace URI (e.g., name="string", ns="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"). Returns a pointer to an internal xmlSchemaType descriptor or NULL if not found.
